The Cubs won, but Dempster was pulled in the seventh, up 5-2, and then watched Carlos Marmol cough up three runs. He's pitched eight times on the road and hasn't won once. Meanwhile, he's 9-0 at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Originally scheduled to face the Nationals, Harang was pushed back to Tuesday due to stiffness in his right forearm. Harang's velocity wasn't where it usually is in his last start, against the Pirates on Monday, but his stuff was still pretty good. The right-hander pitched seven solid innings, giving up three runs on seven hits with a walk and eight strikeouts, but received a no-decision. Harang has just one win in his last nine starts and is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA through three career games against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano looked well rested and sharp in his first start coming off the disabled list last Friday against the St. Louis Cardinals. The right-hander threw six shutout innings and struck out five. He gave up four hits, and only two got out of the infield. He had good tempo and command of his pitches. The Cubs limited him to 87 pitches in the outing, and he'll probably be able to go deeper against the Reds. He's 2-0 this season against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto gave the Reds' overworked bullpen the rest it needed in his last start, against the Nationals on Thursday. The 22-year-old rookie pitched seven solid innings, giving up just three runs on seven hits, walking one and striking out eight. He threw just 95 pitches, with 66 going for strikes. Cueto has given up just six runs in his last four starts. His only career start against the Cubs came on May 5, when he pitched six innings and gave up three runs on six hits, with two walks and eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly gave up two runs on six hits and two walks over seven innings in his last start against the Cardinals, but did not get a decision. St. Louis rallied against Kerry Wood for the win. The lefty was cruising until the sixth when Rick Ankiel led off with a homer. Lilly faced the Reds on April 17, and took the loss, giving up five runs on six hits over six innings while striking out six.
away_pitcher_note: After what he called "the worst outing" of his career on June 24 in Toronto, Arroyo has posted two of his better starts of the season, his last coming on Friday, as he shut down the Nationals and led Cincinnati to a 3-0 victory. Arroyo pitched six shutout innings and gave up just five hits, walking three and striking out three in helping the Reds to their fifth win in seven games. Arroyo likely would have lasted another inning, but went out of the game when a run-scoring situation came about and Cincinnati needed a pinch-hitter.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Marquis' first start since July 1. Because the Cubs wanted to get Carlos Zambrano and Ryan Dempster more starts leading up to the All-Star break, Marquis ended up getting some side work done, and being a backup in the bullpen -- just in case. He faced the Giants in his last outing, giving up two runs on four hits and three walks over seven innings. He's one of the few Cubs who have fared better on the road, compiling a 3.38 ERA away from Wrigley Field as opposed to a 6.29 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: A pair of familiar problems plagued Cain through most of his previous start: He too often threw his fastball around the letters and he didn't attack the strike zone as much as necessary. The righty lasted six innings and gave up five runs and three walks against the Dodgers, unable to beat Los Angeles for the second time this season. Cain was brilliant in eight shutout innings against Cleveland two starts ago, but he's struggled with his consistency all year.

home_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing Harden makes his Cubs debut against a National League team he is pretty familiar with in San Francisco. Harden stymied the Giants in the Bay Bridge Series last month, tossing six shutout innings of one-hit ball and striking out nine, and he holds an 0.84 career ERA against them. He last pitched on July 6 for Oakland, meaning he gets an extra day of rest following a pair of mediocre five-inning outings by his lofty standards.
away_pitcher_note: Correia emerged with a no-decision in his last outing, although it may have been the best of his four starts since he returned from the disabled list. Correia went 6 1/3 innings and was charged with four runs before the Giants proceeded to lose to the Cubs, 6-5. Correia lamented his lack of command with his changeup, which he said was responsible for two mistakes against Jim Edmonds. The first resulted in a second-inning leadoff walk that generated a run; the second was a full-count pitch that Edmonds stroked for a two-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is 10-0 at Wrigley Field, and he will try to finish the first half on a high note. In his last start against the Reds, the right-hander gave up one run on two hits and four walks over seven innings and struck out five. He's the second pitcher in franchise history to win 10 wins in one season after recording at least 20 saves the year before. The only other Cub to do that was Phil Regan. In his last eight home starts, Dempster is 7-0 with a 2.08 ERA, and has gone at least six innings in each of those games. After this start, Dempster will go to the All-Star Game, his second appearance and first since 2000.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum looked human in his most recent start, allowing four runs and nine hits in six innings at New York. It was his first loss of the season in eight road decisions. It also marked the first time he lost following a Giants defeat. He had been 9-0 with a 2.61 ERA before encountering the Mets. The National League All-Star defeated Chicago on July 3, surrendering three runs in six innings while striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler ended his first half on a positive note, allowing four runs over six innings in a win over the Pirates. The right-hander allowed one run over three consecutive starts before yielding five to the Braves on July 4. Moehler faced the Cubs once this year, taking a loss after yielding three runs over five innings. Lifetime vs. the Cubs, Moehler is 1-1 with a 4.18 ERA over seven games (four sarts).
away_pitcher_note: Lilly is looking forward to getting off to a better start in the second half. The lefty did win nine games, but in his last outing July 10 against the Reds, he was pulled after 2 2/3 innings. It was his shortest start of the season. Lilly gave up four runs on six hits, including two home runs, in the loss. He was 7-4 in the second half last year.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has a 3-4 record and a 4.50 ERA over eight career games vs. the Cubs. He allowed eight hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Nationals on July 12, getting a win despite four earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: The All-Star right-hander will try to pick up where he left off in the second half. Zambrano held the Reds to one hit over eight innings in his last start prior to the break. Big Z was limited to 100-105 pitches in that game because it was his second start after being on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder. In his two starts since coming off the DL, he's given up one run on five hits over 14 innings. This was the second straight first half in which Zambrano won 10 games. Let's see if he can match that in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had one of his best outings of the season against the Nationals on July 13, shutting Washington out through seven frames on five hits. His previous start against the Pirates lasted only three innings thanks to a nearly three-hour rain delay -- he allowed no runs on three hits. He's 4-2 all-time against Pittsburgh with a 3.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster ended the first half on a sour note, suffering his first loss at Wrigley Field in 12 starts. The right-hander gave up four runs, seven hits and three walks over 6 2/3 innings in the outing. It's the second time in his dozen starts at home that he's given up four runs. Dempster faced the Astros once this season, May 20, and took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: The Big Unit was probably already in line for his 290th career win against the Phillies, but his two-run double certainly helped his own cause last time out. After going winless in eight starts, Johnson has won two in a row. Johnson missed the Cubs at Wrigley Field, but has never lost to the Cubs in his career, going 12-0 with a 1.98 ERA in 13 starts, including three complete games and an average of more than 10 strikeouts a game.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Harden's second start for the Cubs since he was acquired in a six-player deal from the Athletics. In his debut at Wrigley Field on July 12, he struck out 10, his third career double-digit strikeout game, and threw 5 1/3 scoreless innings. Harden was pulled after 96 pitches. The Cubs will be keeping an eye on his pitch count in hopes of avoiding injury.

home_pitcher_note: Petit will get the nod instead of Micah Owings, who was needed to pitch in relief on Monday due to a depleted bullpen. Petit last pitched on Friday in relief and allowed one run over three innings against the Dodgers. The right-hander has made one start this year -- an emergency start in place of Owings -- and did not get a decision despite allowing just one run in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis went 10 days between starts, and he seemed to benefit from the time off. The right-hander threw seven shutout innings on July 11 against the Giants, giving up three hits. Marquis is needed to step it up in the second half. He has a career 25-33 record after the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Davis had his shortest outing of the year the last time out, but was given a great deal of run support against the Dodgers. Pitching on a full week's rest, he lasted just three innings, giving up five runs (four earned) on five hits and three walks. He didn't factor into the decision. Against the Cubs, Davis is 7-5 with a 3.39 ERA in his career in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly bounced back from his shortest outing of the season in his last start before the All-Star break with one of his best starts of the season Friday night at Houston. Though he wasn't involved in the decision, Lilly went seven innings, allowing just one run on a Carlos Lee homer and just six hits total. He is 1-2 with a 2.73 ERA in five career appearances against the D-backs, including 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA in one start at Chase Field. He beat Arizona at Wrigley Field on May 9, allowing one earned run on three hits over seven innings in a 3-1 Cubs victory.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano wasn't as sharp in his most recent outing, as he walked six in 6 1/3 innings in a 4-1 loss at Houston Saturday night, his first loss to an NL Central Division opponent this season. It was the right-hander's third start since coming off the disabled list. Zambrano has not faced the Marlins this season and is 3-1 with a 2.54 ERA in seven career games against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: After holding the high-powered Phillies offense to four runs (three earned) in five innings on Saturday, Olsen picked up his second straight win. That's a big feat considering the 24-year-old went winless in his previous 11 starts. One problem for Olsen pretty much all year, however, has been his velocity. Against the Phillies, the lefty threw 93 pitches, but most of them barely reached 90 mph on the radar gun -- a big reason why he did not record a strikeout for the first time since April 25.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Dempster turned in one of his better outings of the season, while earning his first road victory since June 2, 2006, against the Cardinals. The right-hander pitched eight scoreless innings against Houston, limiting the Astros to six singles and a walk, while striking out seven. Dempster hasn't faced the Marlins this season and is 1-1 with three saves and a 3.00 ERA in 10 career appearances against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: So far, so good on Johnson's return from Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery. In his first two starts since rebounding from the ligament replacement surgery to his right elbow, Johnson has made steady progress, although he has yet to receive a decision. In his last start, Johnson gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Phillies. He logged 92 pitches and struck out four, walking three. With his velocity in the 93-mph range, Johnson had his sinker working, as he induced 11 ground-ball outs.

home_pitcher_note: Harden has posted back to back 10-strikeout games for the Cubs, but has yet to get a "W." In his last start against Arizona, he gave up one hit -- a solo homer to Alex Romero -- and took the loss. Harden threw 112 pitches, more than the Cubs wanted him to, but Lou Piniella kept him in the game in hopes that the offense would come alive.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad's third outing may not have gone as perfectly as his previous two, but he still pitched pretty well. On Monday against the Braves, Volstad gave up three runs off six hits and three walks in six innings after leaving with 87 pitches -- 55 for strikes. Volstad got into trouble in the second inning, throwing 21 pitches and facing seven batters, but gave up one run and worked out of a bases-loaded, no-out jam unscathed. Volstad was pitching about an hour away from where he grew up for the first time and had at least 15 members of his family in attendance.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis took the loss in his last start, but was another victim of a lack of offense. He gave up three runs on five hits over six innings -- a quality start. But the Cubs couldn't muster any runs. He has not won since June 21 against the White Sox. He's 4-5 with a 6.88 ERA against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: VandenHurk was lights-out in his first start with the Marlins since April 6 on Tuesday against the Braves. He threw five innings of no-hit ball while striking out seven and walking five, but had to leave the game early because he had thrown 94 pitches already. VandenHurk added a little bit more velocity on his fastball and, most importantly, he picked up a slider during his time in the Minor Leagues that he used effectively. The only blemish for VandenHurk was a fourth inning that saw him load the bases with nobody out. But he got out of it with two strikeouts and a pop out to the infield.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers begin their biggest series of the season with their new co-ace on the mound. Sabathia pitched a three-hit shutout at St. Louis on Wednesday for his third consecutive complete game and his fourth Brewers win in as many starts since a July 7 trade from Cleveland. He faced only three, three-ball counts all night and took a no-hitter into the sixth inning. The last Brewers pitcher to go the distance in at least three consecutive starts was Cal Eldred, who worked four straight in 1994. Sabathia lost his only career start against the Cubs, allowing nine runs on eight hits in 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly is coming off a win against Arizona. He did it all, giving up three runs on six hits over six innings, as well as hitting a RBI single, stealing a base, throwing out a potential base stealer and helping in a rundown play. The lefty is one of three Cubs pitchers with at least 10 wins. He faced Milwaukee on April 2, and lost, 8-2.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets was happy with his last outing despite the fact he was in line for a loss until Ryan Braun hit a go-ahead homer in the ninth inning. Sheets lasted seven innings and limited the Cardinals to three runs, only two of which were earned, and four hits. He's 1-0 in two starts against the Cubs this season while allowing three earned runs in 11 1/3 innings (2.38 ERA). Cubs hitters are batting just .132 against Sheets in those games (5-for-38).
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano held the Marlins at bay last time out, striking out six and, more importantly, walking none in seven innings of two-run ball. The Cubs ace had walked six in his previous start. He has a 0.69 ERA in two outings against the Brewers this season, both no-decisions. You know Zambrano will be amped up for this start, facing an NL Central contender on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Parra was seething after his first loss since May 3 ended an eight-decision winning streak. He danced in and out of trouble against the Astros through six innings before running out of luck in the seventh, when Houston loaded the bases without hitting a ball out of the infield. Parra was replaced by reliever David Riske and all three runs scored. "I feel like I'm throwing the ball really well, six innings, seven innings and then a break here or there is the difference between what CC [Sabathia] and Ben [Sheets] are doing. They're coming out of games on a good note versus being taken out of the inning, which I can't stand," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his last start against the Marlins. He gave up one run on two hits over six innings, but he didn't get any offensive support. He also walked six, including loading the bases on three walks with two outs in the fifth before striking out Dan Uggla to escape. Dempster beat the Brewers on April 3, and again April 30, both games at Wrigley Field, where he's 10-1. He's 1-3 with a 3.42 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Bush struggled somewhat in his first appearance since July 10, a delay that came about when Bush and Seth McClung were inserted into an unusual home/road platoon. The right-hander, who has had plentiful success at Miller Park this year, allowed nine hits in five innings and surrendered four runs -- three on home runs by Carlos Lee and Hunter Pence in the fourth. Still, Milwaukee rallied for victory and now have triumphs in the last start from both platooned pitchers. Thursday's game will mark the first time one of the two pitchers has made two consecutive turns in the new system.
away_pitcher_note: It's almost impossible to believe that Harden doesn't have a win. He has struck out 10 in each of his three starts for the Cubs, and despite all those K's, he doesn't have a "W." In his last outing against Florida, he was pulled after throwing 87 pitches in five innings in an effort to keep him strong. He had thrown 112 pitches the outing before. Over 17 1/3 innings in his three Chicago starts, Harden has given up two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis did not get a decision in his last start against the Marlins. He gave up six runs on nine hits and three walks over six innings, but did gut it out. Florida had opened a 5-0 lead after three innings and Marquis was able to stay in the game to save the Cubs bullpen. He made some mistakes -- walking the leadoff man in the first and second innings isn't a good idea -- but was aided by a late inning rally from his teammates. He's 2-0 with a no-decision in three starts this year against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens could flip-flop with Paul Maholm and pitch on Saturday, but while management makes that determination, let's slot him in for Friday. Karstens came to Pittsburgh as part of the six-player trade that sent Xavier Nady and Damaso Marte to the Yankees on Saturday. This will be the right-hander's first Major League appearance this season. In 2006-07, Karstens combined to make 15 appearances (nine starts) with New York, going 3-5 with a 5.65 ERA. He was 6-4 with a 3.80 ERA in 12 Triple-A starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers. The lefty gave up three runs on seven hits, including back to back homers by J.J. Hardy and Ryan Braun, over six innings. Lilly was mad at himself for the mistakes. He finished July 1-1 in five starts. He has faced Pittsburgh twice this year, and did not get a decision in either game.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continued his solid work in his last start against San Diego on July 27. He hurled seven innings and gave up one run on four hits. He recorded nine strikeouts and received a no-decision. Maholm has gone 5-1 in his last 11 starts. He has worked at least six innings in each of his last 15 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano struck out a season-high nine batters in a win over the Brewers in his last start. Big Z threw eight scoreless innings, giving up five hits and two walks. He also hit an RBI single. Zambrano now is batting .349 -- and ranks among the NL leaders with a 2.80 ERA. He is 1-0 in two starts against the Pirates this year, facing them in back-to-back starts in late May. He went 4-1 in July, giving up seven runs over 35 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Snell had arguably his best outing of 2008 against the Rockies at PNC Park his last time out. He struck out eight and walked only one on his way to a quality seven-inning performance. Manager John Russell said he hoped  the start is a turning point for Snell. The right-hander hadn't won a game since June 11. Snell is 1-5 with a 5.26 ERA against the Cubs in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster held the Brewers to one run on five hits and struck out nine over seven innings in his most recent start. The right-hander picked up his second straight win on the road, so that's not a problem any more. He was able to hide his delivery so well, the Brewers couldn't tell when he was throwing his fastball and when it was his split. His approach was to get ahead in the count, and it worked. He is 1-1 vs. Houston this year, with a win July 20.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler fell one out shy of his 11th career complete game and his first in eight years during his last start against the Reds, but the right-hander still walked away with his sixth win of the year. Moehler pitched well in his last outing against the Cubs, allowing one run over seven innings while taking a no-decision on July 18 at Minute Maid Park. He also faced them on May 19, allowing three runs over five innings in a losing effort.
summary: 2008-08-04 - Houston Astros @ Chicago Cubs (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Harden finally got his first win with the Cubs. The right-hander had fanned 10 in each of his first three starts for Chicago, but in his fourth against the Brewers, he struck out nine and got the "W." Harden gave up one run on a solo homer by Prince Fielder. In fact, he's given up three runs in his four starts with the Cubs, and all have been on solo homers.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled in his last start against the Reds, even though only one of the five runs he allowed was categorized as earned. Rodriguez allowed six runs on nine hits, including two home runs to Adam Dunn and another three-run shot to Ken Griffey Jr. in the series finale. The last time Rodriguez faced the Cubs, he dominated. On July 19 at Minute Maid Park, he yielded one earned run over 6 2/3 innings in a winning effort.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis took the loss in his last outing, against the Pirates. The right-hander gave up three runs on eight hits over six innings and struck out two, but he didn't get any run support, as the Cubs were shut out at home for the first time this season. Marquis did post his ninth quality start, but he has lost his past four decisions. The Cubs have scored one run or fewer when he's on the mound in five of his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Backe took a no-decision in his last outing but pitched well enough to win, allowing three runs over six-plus innings to the Mets in a game later won on Mark Loretta's pinch-hit homer. Backe last faced the Cubs on June 20 at Minute Maid Park and yielded four runs over 6 2/3 innings, striking out eight. Backe is 3-6 with a 4.50 ERA over 13 games on the road this year. He has allowed 35 runs over 70 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly has thrown four quality starts in a row since the All-Star Game. Before that, the veteran left-hander held the Cardinals to two runs in six innings on July 5 and got a no-decision. He has a 3.46 ERA against the Cardinals in two starts this year and enjoys a lifetime 3.06 ERA against the Cubs' NL Central rival. He battled in his last start, against Pittsburgh, tossing 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball en route to his 11th win.
away_pitcher_note: Even though he pitched one of his better outings of the year in his last start, Looper did not get enough help from his offense to earn his 11th win. Looper gave up two solo home runs to the Phillies and they did him in. Looper has given up 17 home runs over the year, which put him at the 14th most in the National League. He has not fared all that well against the Dodgers but has allowed two runs or less in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing Cubs ace lowered his ERA for the third start in a row on Sunday against the Pirates. He threw only 82 pitches in five innings and did not receive a decision, as skipper Lou Piniella played it safe after Zambrano had thrown 243 pitches in his previous two starts. That, along with a fifth day of rest, means Zambrano should be well rested for his start against the Cardinals. In his last start against St. Louis, Zambrano worked six scoreless innings for the win, striking out five while giving up four hits. He is 9-4 with a 2.26 ERA in 19 career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Over his last three outings, Wellemeyer has begun to regain his form that made him May's Pitcher of the Month. Giving up two runs or less in each of his last three starts, however, Wellemeyer has received three straight no-decisions. Now he gets to carry his newfound momentum against the Cubs -- the team he entered the Majors with. He has made two starts against Chicago in his career, going 1-1 with a 4.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster should be well-rested for this start. He matched his shortest outing of the season, five innings, in Monday's loss to Houston, but it was Mother Nature's fault. The Cubs-Astros game on Monday was halted by a thunderstorm at the start of the sixth for two hours and 45 minutes. They played two more innings before it was called for good. Dempster gave up two runs against the Astros to fall to 10-2 at home in 2008. He has yet to face the Cardinals this season, but he is very familiar with winning at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Carpenter's third start since returning from the disabled list, where he had spent the entire season. He has allowed one run on eight hits in nine innings so far. He went deeper into the game -- completing five innings -- in his last start than he did the start prior, in which he lasted four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has seemingly turned the corner while allowing runs in just one of his past 14 innings. The best outing of his young career arguably came on Thursday, when he allowed five singles in seven scoreless innings against the Diamondbacks. Just five days earlier, he'd blanked the Brewers for six innings before allowing a pair of seventh-inning runs. Confidence has always been an issue with this right-hander, who has been hurt by an inability to consistently keep his pitches down in the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis picked up his first win since June 21 in his last start, but he wishes he could have pitched better. The right-hander gave up four runs (three courtesy of a Carlos Lee homer) in 6 1/3 innings against the Astros and was backed by 11 Cubs runs. This will be his first start versus the club that drafted him since June 9, 2007. Marquis hopes for better results than that last outing in Atlanta when he was tagged for six runs in 1 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo won a fourth straight decision despite not having his best stuff against the Diamondbacks on Friday night. The 29-year-old rookie hurler's pinpoint location and ability to change speeds has made it difficult for opponents to plan any sort of attack against him. This will essentially be the first time the Cubs have seen him. He threw one pitch in a relief appearance at Wrigley Field on June 12.
away_pitcher_note: Harden did not get a decision in his last outing Tuesday against Houston. He gave up five runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings and admitted to being tired in the sixth. He'll be pitching against the Braves on eight days' rest. One aspect of National League play that he has to get used to is baserunning. In the second, Harden beat out a bunt single, and that may have resulted in the weary legs.

home_pitcher_note: Glavine has overcome the elbow problems that have sidelined him since he was forced to make an early exit from his June 10 start against the Cubs. Mechanically he's felt sound in two Minor League rehab appearances and the elbow discomfort that plagued him in May hasn't been present. The 42-year-old left-hander wants to impress in the season's final two months to at least give himself a chance to pitch again next year.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Cardinals, but he pitched well. The lefty gave up two runs on seven hits and two walks over 7 1/3 innings, and was economical with his pitches, throwing 83. He was pulled in the eighth with a runner on and Albert Pujols coming up. It made sense. This was Lilly's fifth straight quality start, and he's 2-0 in that stretch with a 2.76 ERA. However, he does lead the NL in home runs allowed, and served up No. 26 to Joe Mather.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Mets on Sunday, Johnson gave the Marlins a much-needed win by limiting New York to two runs in seven innings while striking out five and walking just two. The young right-hander has been rolling ever since coming off Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery, and the Marlins are now 6-0 in games he starts this season. In his past two starts -- against the National League East-rival Phillies and Mets -- he is 2-0 and has allowed just two runs in 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano lost his first game in 13 starts at home in his last outing, giving up a career-high nine earned runs on 10 hits over 4 1/3 innings against St. Louis. He also served up four home runs for the first time in his career. Zambrano hit a homer himself, his third of the year, but it wasn't enough. He was coming off a shortened outing prior to his game against the Cardinals, so the problem wasn't that Zambrano was tired. He fell behind and the Cardinals took advantage.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez suffered his second straight loss despite a solid performance against the Cardinals on Monday. Sanchez gave up three runs on six hits while striking out eight -- which tied his career high -- and walking two. He left after throwing a season-high 103 pitches -- 69 for strikes. Sanchez's biggest mistake was a two-run homer he gave up to Yadier Molina in the fourth inning, which gave the Cardinals a 3-2 lead they wouldn't relinquish. But after that, the 24-year-old retired 11 of the next 14 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall got the call over Jason Marquis on short rest or rookie Jeff Samardzija. It'll be the lefty's fourth start this season. He started on June 24 against Baltimore, on June 29 against the White Sox, and July 6 against St. Louis, and picked up a win against the Cardinals. As a starter, Marshall is 1-2 with a 4.08 ERA, giving up eight runs on 18 hits and three walks over 17 2/3 innings. The Cubs had to tweak their rotation after playing a day-night doubleheader against Atlanta on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad's outing against the Cardinals on Tuesday was cut short right before he began to get into a groove. Still, the 21-year-old picked up his first win at home in giving up three runs in five innings to the Cardinals before a long rain delay kicked in. Volstad's only trouble came in the first inning, when he started off the game by loading the bases with nobody out, then gave up a bases-clearing double to Ryan Ludwick. But after that inning, Volstad gave up just two hits and one walk. He retired the last six batters he faced and finished the night throwing 72 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off a big win over the Cardinals. He gave up two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings in the game, striking out six. The former closer is now two wins shy of his career-high of 15. He did not get a decision against the Marlins on July 25, giving up one run on two hits over six innings while striking out six. But he also walked six in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Harden picked up a win in his last start, his second since joining the Cubs on July 8. However, it wasn't pretty. He retired the first eight batters he faced, then walked the bases loaded. Harden finished with five scoreless innings and gave up two hits and walked five. He had trouble with his fastball -- it was up in the warmups and in the game. He'll be working on six days rest against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Getting through the first inning cleanly has been an issue for Cueto, especially in his past two starts. He threw 26 first-inning pitches two starts ago and 27 in the first during a 3-1 Reds win over the Pirates on Thursday. The rookie lasted only five innings and allowed one earned run and four hits, with three walks and seven strikeouts, in what became a solid outing.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly is coming off a win over the Braves last Thursday. The lefty gave up four runs on eight hits over six innings in that game, striking out eight. He's 2-0 with a 3.20 ERA in his last three starts, having struck out 17 over 19 2/3 innings. Lilly is 0-2 so far this season against the Reds. In his last start against Cincinnati, on July 10, the lefty gave up two home runs in 2 2/3 innings. The Reds bashed seven homers in that game.
away_pitcher_note: Key two-out hits hurt Arroyo in a 5-3 loss to the Cardinals on Friday, including Rick Ankiel's first-inning two-run home run on a curveball that was left up. Arroyo gave up five earned runs and nine hits in 6 1/3 innings, with two walks and five strikeouts. He also threw 67 pitches through his first three innings, eventually settling down and pitching well before departing. Still, he paid for the early mistakes.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano did not get a decision in his last outing, against the Marlins. He gave up five runs on four hits and five walks over six innings. The right-hander appears to be rushing his delivery, especially with runners on base; four of the five batters he walked scored. Zambrano is winless in his past three starts, and Cubs manager Lou Piniella says his ace needs to get back on track. He's 3-0 against the Reds this year.
away_pitcher_note: Fogg pitched two scoreless innings of relief in Saturday's loss to St. Louis, resulting in his spot in the rotation being pushed back to Friday. It was later bumped back a day to Thursday due to neck spasms suffered by Aaron Harang, who will pitch on Friday. Fogg seemed headed for a good outing on Wednesday vs. the Pirates, retiring 12 of 14 batters through his first four scoreless innings. It fell apart during a four-run fifth inning, when he threw 33 pitches in a 5-2 loss. Fogg lost command of the strike zone and gave up all four runs and two critical walks in the fifth. There were six hits overall, with two strikeouts. He is winless over his past four starts since being drilled in the face by a batting-practice line drive.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis' last start was in the Cubs' doubleheader on Aug. 13 in Atlanta. In that game, he gave up two runs on six hits and two walks over 5 1/3 innings. He was skipped one turn because the Cubs didn't want to bring him back on short rest against Florida. With an off-day on Monday, they had the luxury of giving Sean Marshall a spot start. Marquis is 2-2 with a 5.46 ERA in five starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Last Saturday, Lannan lasted four-plus innings and gave up a season-high eight earned runs against the Rockies, as his ERA soared from 3.40 to 3.81. He found himself in trouble in the first inning, when Garrett Atkins hit a two-run single. It got worse by the third, when Lannan gave up three more runs. In the fifth, the Rockies batted around and plated six more, three of which were charged to reliever Garrett Mock.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is one win shy of matching his career high in victories, which he set in 2001 with the Marlins. He beat the Marlins in his last start, on Sunday, giving up two runs in six innings and striking out 10. It was his 10th double-digit strikeout game, and his third this season. Dempster feels he's pitching better now than he was earlier in the year and able to throw his splitter and slider for strikes. Whatever it is, it's working.
away_pitcher_note: Perez had another quality start last Sunday, going six innings and giving up three run -- two earned -- against the Rockies. But Perez ended up taking the loss because Colorado took the lead for good in the fourth inning. After Chris Iannetta reached on an error by Pete Orr at shortstop and Troy Tulowitzki walked, Ian Stewart hit a Perez pitch over the right-center field wall to give the Rockies a 3-1 lead.

home_pitcher_note: Harden is making it look easy since moving to the National League. His seventh start since flying from Oakland to Chicago was his most dominant. The baffling right-hander held Cincinnati to two hits in seven innings and struck out 10 on Tuesday, his fourth double-digit strikeout game as a member of the Cubs. He was pulled after 94 pitches, as manager Lou Piniella continues to monitor his workload to keep him healthy for the stretch run and the playoffs. Harden has never faced the Nationals, but he's got to be salivating at the chance to face the National League's worst-hitting team following his best performance in his new uniform.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander rebounded nicely from an effort in which he allowed six earned runs in three innings against the Mets on Aug. 13 to keep the Phillies to four runs (three earned) in 6 1/3 innings on Tuesday. Bergmann, however, ended up with a no-decision after the Nats' bullpen allowed Philadelphia to come back. In two career starts against the Cubs, Bergmann is 0-1 with a 4.76 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens continues to pitch deep into games, but he also continues to give up runs. His four-run, nine-hit performance against the Mets was good enough to give his team a chance to win, but he was opposed by two-time Cy Young Award winner Johan Santana, who threw a shutout. Pirates manager John Russell continues to praise Karstens for the right-hander's ability to attack the strike zone and go after hitters. He'll try to recapture the magic of his first two Pirates starts against the Cubs, whom Karstens shut out over five innings in his National League debut on Aug. 1.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly had a no-hitter broken up by the leadoff batter in the sixth in his last start and wound up losing a 2-1 decision to the Reds. He only gave up two hits in seven innings and struck out seven. That outing lowered his ERA to 4.25, the lowest it's been after a start all season. The lefty dominated Pittsburgh on Aug. 2, holding the Pirates to one run and six hits in 6 1/3 innings for the win. But he was touched up by them in two previous starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Snell picked up just his third win since mid-April his last time out and finally looked dominant in doing so. The right-hander relied heavily on his changeup and slider to complement his fastball, which he established early. The key for Snell continues to be going aggressively after hitters, which he did successfully on Tuesday. If he does so, Snell can limit his pitch count, which has been on the high end early in games too often this year. Snell is winless in two starts against the Cubs this season. He has allowed seven runs in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Let's see if Zambrano can keep his hitting streak going. He belted his fourth home run of the season in his last start to keep his streak alive at seven games. Big Z also picked up the win against the Reds, giving up one run over seven innings. He was able to slow down his delivery and correct some mechanical flaws that have popped up in the last two starts. He did walk the leadoff batter -- something that really annoys the right-hander. Right now, he's batting .361 and has an ERA of 3.29. That's pretty good.

home_pitcher_note: Duke's winless drought continued in Friday's loss at Milwaukee. It's now at eight straight losses dating to June 9. He tinkered with his throwing motion last week, and despite giving up four runs in six innings to the Brewers, was pleased with his delivery. The left-hander has struggled against the Cubs this season, going 0-2 with a 5.91 ERA in four starts, but then again, he's struggled against just about everybody. Duke has had moderate success against Chicago in 12 career starts with a 4-4 record and a 3.16 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis was cruising in his last start, against the Nationals, throwing five scoreless innings before he got into a mess, giving up an infield single and walking the next two batters. The Cubs eventually lost, 13-5, although he did not factor in the decision. Marquis was working on eight days' rest and would prefer to pitch on a regular routine, like the other starters. This will be a chance for the right-hander to show that's the best scenario.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster will be going for a personal-best 16th win in his next start. He picked up No. 15 in his last start, against the Nationals, giving up one run on eight hits over 7 1/3 innings. He now has 18 quality starts. He will face the Phillies for the first time this year. The right-hander also has been productive at the plate and leads the Majors with 16 sacrifice bunts.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels enjoyed Saturday's offensive outburst after receiving an average of two runs of support during his previous four starts. The Phils' ace went seven innings, allowing two runs on five hits to earn the victory. Hamels is now in a three-way tie with Jamie Moyer and Kyle Kendrick for the team lead in victories, with 11. In four career starts against the Cubs, Hamels is 3-1 with a 3.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Harden struck out 11 over seven innings in his last start against the Nationals to match his personal high. The only other time he fanned 11 was on June 26 this year against the Phillies. He now has seven double-digit-strikeout games in his career, and five have come since joining the Cubs on July 8. He gave up one run and has an 0.47 ERA in his last three starts. Harden also did not walk a batter, the sixth time in his career he's avoided that in a start.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday night, Blanton turned in his third quality start in seven outings since joining the Phillies in July. The right-hander held the Dodgers to one run on six hits in six innings, striking out four and walking three. Blanton has recorded a 3.00 ERA in his past five starts. He has never faced the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly wasn't spectacular in his last outing against the Pirates, but he wasn't bad, either. The lefty threw seven strong innings and was able to keep Pittsburgh hitters off balance with a good changeup and a mesmerizing curveball. His only two mistakes came on home runs to two left-handed hitters, but the damage meant little after the Cubs' offense put up 12 runs of support. Lilly will look to keep things going vs. the Phillies, who he is 1-2 with a 5.19 ERA against in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old continues to roll since making his return from a July stint in the Minor Leagues. On Monday, Myers held the Dodgers scoreless in seven innings. The right-hander has now logged 16 scoreless innings in a row, starting when he threw a complete-game shutout against the Nationals on Aug. 20. Since returning from the Minors, Myers is 4-1 with a 1.66 ERA. In eight career starts against the Cubs, Myers is 6-3 with a 2.63 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Marshall fills in for Carlos Zambrano, who was scratched a few hours before game time.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer's streak of allowing three runs or fewer in 14 consecutive starts was snapped by the Mets on Tuesday. New York pounded the veteran left-hander for six runs on nine hits in three innings, his shortest outing of 2008. Still, Moyer remains in a three-way tie with Cole Hamels and Kyle Kendrick for the staff lead in wins, with 11. On Sunday, the veteran will be facing the Cubs, the team with which he broke into the Major Leagues in 1986. Moyer faced them once already this season, allowing four runs on nine hits in five innings on his way to a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis looked like a frontline starter against the Pirates in his last outing, when he threw seven scoreless innings, struck out three and walked none for his ninth win of the year. Catcher Henry Blanco said Marquis' repertoire was in full gear and his fastball had bite. The right-hander continues to give the Cubs plenty of innings. Only once this season has he been unable to pitch past the fourth inning. Marquis is 9-5 with a 5.22 ERA against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt recorded his 22nd win against the Reds in a 4-1 victory on Wednesday. He is 6-2 in his last 10 starts with a 3.02 ERA, averaging 5.7 strikeouts a game. Oswalt is 11-11 all-time against Chicago, losing his only game against the Cubs this season. He earned five runs on 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs tweaked their rotation to give Zambrano extra time because of a tired arm. He had been scheduled to start Sunday. Big Z is 7-1 in 14 starts at Wrigley Field. His velocity had dropped in August, and the Cubs are hoping an extra day or two will help. He did throw a short side session on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Backe strung together two consecutive successful outings with a 3-2 series finale win over the Reds, something that has eluded the right-hander this season. Backe has suffered from inconsistency but is solid when he can keep his pitches low in the zone. He gave up two runs over 6 2/3 innings against Cincinnati, throwing 64 pitches and allowing three hits in six shutout frames. He gave up two in the seventh before being pulled. Backe has lost two of three against the Cubs this season, recording a no-decision in the third. He gave up 11 runs on nine hits over 3 1/3 in his last visit to Wrigley Field, walking six as two Chicago players went deep.

The last time Zambrano pitched at Miller Park was Sept. 14 and he threw a no-hitter. That game was against the Astros, also, who were relocated because of Hurricane Ike. The last time he faced the Brewers on their home turf was last July 29, when he threw eight shutout innings, giving up five runs and striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan wouldn't see it this way because of his start-to-start focus, but Brewers fans would like to see him bounce back from a lousy finish to 2008 and it didn't happen on Opening Day. Suppan, who had a fabulous August but went 0-3 with an 8.44 ERA in September and then lost Game 4 of the National League Division Series, was hit for six runs over four innings against the Giants on Tuesday in a 10-6 Milwaukee loss. He dropped to 0-2 in his four Opening Day starts with an 8.55 ERA and, including Aaron Rowand's blast Tuesday, he has surrendered 10 home runs in those games. Suppan started three straight season openers for the Royals from 2000-2002. He is 6-6 with a 3.60 ERA in his career against the Cubs, including 1-1 last season, when he surrendered 11 runs in 15 innings against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his first start Tuesday in Houston. The right-hander did notch a quality start, giving up two runs on six hits over six innings but the Astros won in extra innings. Dempster struck out five and walked three. He was 4-0 with a 2.40 ERA in five starts against the Brewers last year. His defense definitely helped as Alfonso Soriano robbed Michael Bourn of extra bases with a running catch and also threw out Hunter Pence, who was trying to advance on a long single.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly will start in the Cubs' home opener, and he can only hope the wind is blowing in. Last Wednesday at Houston, he served up four home runs but still got the win as the Cubs scored four runs in each of the first two innings. The four dingers were the most off the lefty since he he gave up a career-high five on June 11, 2003, against Atlanta. Lilly did give up eight hits and wasn't too happy with his outing. He's still a little behind work-wise after participating in the World Baseball Classic. He was 7-5 with a 4.50 ERA in 15 home starts last season.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez dominated the strike zone on Tuesday at Arizona, striking out eight in seven innings and pitching out of a couple of jams in the Rockies' 3-0 victory. It was one of those nights when Jimenez felt his fastball, his split-finger pitch, his curve and his slider. A key to pitching at Wrigley, however, is adjusting to conditions. But Jimenez can handle that, since he does that at Coors Field, where there are nights when one or two of his pitches won't do what he intends. Jimenez made his first Major League start at Wrigley in the final game of the 2006, and is 0-1 with a 4.63 ERA in two starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Harden recorded his eighth career 10-strikeout game in his last start against the Brewers but did not get a decision. He was in line for the win, but Milwaukee rallied in the ninth. Harden gave up three hits over six innings and looked strong. The radar gun at Miller Park was registering mid 90s consistently with his pitches. He was 5-0 with a 1.79 ERA in 15 games at home last season. Harden has never faced the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: The opponent will be familiar. Marquis pitched for the Cubs in 2007-08 and went 23-18 in 63 games before the Rockies acquired him for right-handed reliever Luis Vizcaino. Marquis certainly earned the favor of his home fans Friday, when he held the Phillies to two runs on five hits in seven innings of the home opener, a 9-2 victory. A sinkerball pitcher, Marquis stayed low in the strike zone and forced 13 groundouts, which included three double plays.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Marshall's first start of the season. The lefty won the fifth starter's spot this spring, but struggled a little in two Cactus League outings after he was named. Marshall was the swingman last year, making seven starts and posting a 4.15 ERA and appearing in 27 games in relief and compiling a 3.42 ERA. He is 2-1 with a 3.38 ERA lifetime against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: The Redbirds' Opening Day starter still hasn't quite found the groove that made him so good in 2008 and most of 2007. However, he has an ERA under 2.00 even while he's been searching for his form. That tells you something about how good Wainwright is capable of being. He's had some struggles at Wrigley and against the Cubs, but there's no hesitation to give him the ball in the opener of the first series of the year between the two old rivals.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's first start at home this season. The right-hander was 7-2 at Wrigley last year. In his last start Saturday night at Miller Park, Zambrano gave up three runs on seven hits and three walks over six innings. He did strike out seven, but also threw 118 pitches. Prince Fielder connected on one of those for his first homer. The runs were the first off Zambrano at Miller Park in 20 innings. He was 1-2 with a 12.75 ERA against the Cardinals last year.
away_pitcher_note: Walters impressed the Major League staff in Spring Training, leapfrogging to the top of the sixth-starter chart. He throws strikes and keeps the ball on the ground, two traits that endear any young pitcher to manager Tony La Russa and pitching coach Dave Duncan. Still, Walters struggled somewhat last year in his first exposure to Triple-A, and it will be intriguing to see how he handles big league hitters in his first shot.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster got a little help from Reed Johnson to pick up the win in his last start. Johnson robbed Prince Fielder of a potential grand slam in the fifth. For the game, Dempster gave up four runs on six hits and three walks over six innings while striking out six. He said he didn't feel sharp and kept getting behind hitters. Dempster will be happy to be home. The right-hander was 14-3 last year at Wrigley.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has been exceptional thus far, but he's worked hard. In each of his first two starts, he's stuck it out to get some extra outs when, ideally, he might have benefited from being relieved. Still, each time, he's been able to grind it out and get the job done. He's likely to benefit from the extra day of rest that he'll receive following a little bit of rotation shuffling in the wake of Chris Carpenter's injury.

home_pitcher_note: The left-handed Lilly ignored nasty weather in the Cubs' home opener and held the Rockies to one hit over 6 2/3 innings en route to a win. He struck out eight. This is the first time he's opened the season 2-0 since 2003. Last year, he was 3-0 with a 3.06 ERA against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has simplified his delivery in between starts and it has paid dividends. In his most recent start, he went seven innings against the Diamondbacks on Monday, allowing seven hits, and one earned run. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter. In Wellemeyer's first start of the season, he gave up 12 hits and five runs in a loss to Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Harden struggled in his first start at Wrigley Field on Wednesday, throwing 92 pitches over four innings. He needed 13 pitches to get through the first inning, then threw 14 in one at-bat to Colorado's Garrett Atkins to open the second. For the game, Harden gave up four runs on five hits and four walks while striking out eight. He is 2-0 with a 2.92 ERA lifetime against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: A long layoff had Owings looking a little rusty during a 9-3 loss to the Brewers on Wednesday. The right-hander, who worked one batter into the sixth, gave up four earned runs and five hits over five innings with two walks and two strikeouts. Almost half of his 89 pitches were called for balls (42). It had been 10 days since Owings pitched in any kind of game and that was a Minor League outing at Spring Training. That was because his first regular-season start was scrubbed because a rainout prompted the Reds to recalibrate their rotation. Owings was moved to the bullpen but saw no action. In just 1 1/3 lifetime innings vs. the Cubs, Owings has a 33.75 ERA with five runs allowed on two hits.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty ignored nasty weather in the Cubs' home opener and held the Rockies to one hit over 6 2/3 innings en route to a win. He struck out eight. This is the first time Lilly's opened the season 2-0 since 2003. He was scheduled to start Sunday night vs. the Cardinals but the game was postponed by rain. Lilly was roughed up by the Reds last year, going 0-4 with an 8.15 ERA against them. He's looking for payback.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Cueto held the Astros hitless for the first three frames but lasted just 4 2/3 innings, allowing two hits in a no-decision as the Reds won, 2-1. It was the six walks the right-hander issued -- particularly the three he allowed in the fifth inning -- that put Cueto out of the game early. Last season against the Cubs, Cueto was 1-3 with a 4.68 ERA in four games. He allowed 26 hits in 25 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano's final line wasn't pretty on Friday against St. Louis. He gave up three homers and seven earned runs but also lasted seven innings to help give his bullpen some relief. Throughout his career, Zambrano has pitched well against Cincinnati, going 14-9 with a 3.03 ERA and holding the Reds to a .219 average.
away_pitcher_note: During a 7-0 loss to the Astros on Saturday, Harang was charged with five earned runs and 10 hits in six-plus innings. He walked one and struck out six. Nine of the hits were singles, many of them grounders that squeaked through holes. The pitcher was visibly frustrated with his lack of success and bad luck. Harang is 8-6 with a 4.81 ERA in 19 career games against the Cubs but was 0-3 with a 6.29 ERA last season in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: This start will put Wainwright on seven full days' rest, a decision the Cardinals chalk up to matchups -- they preferred Wainwright against the Cubs and Kyle Lohse against the Mets, rather than vice versa. Still, it should also allow Wainwright an extra bullpen session in which to get sorted out, since he still has yet to have a game in which he pitched up to his own standards.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not factor in the decision his last time out, when he took on the Cardinals. The Cubs eventually won, 7-5, in 11 innings, and Dempster helped keep Chicago in the game, even though he wasn't sharp early. In six innings, Dempster allowed four runs on four hits and retired nine of the final 10 hitters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Boggs entered the spring as the primary candidate to get a start if anything happened to one of the regular starting five. Then he got hurt in Spring Training, and P.J. Walters passed him on the depth chart. But Boggs showed the Cardinals something they liked in his relief appearance last time out, and he'll get a look against Chicago. One thing that impressed the staff last season was that he didn't shrink from difficult or high-profile assignments, and a Saturday afternoon game in front of a big crowd against the Cubs certainly fits that description.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Marshall's second start of the season. He did not get a decision in his first outing against the Cardinals, giving up three runs on seven hits and two walks over five-plus innings. He also struck out four. Lou Piniella's concern was that Marshall had some trouble with the Cardinals' left-handed hitters, and threw too many pitches to them. The lefty, who won the fifth starter spot this spring, is 1-0 with a 2.12 ERA in six games in his career against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Just as it seemed Wellemeyer had gotten sorted out after an iffy spring and start of the season, he was a bit shaky again on Tuesday. As he pointed out, though, some of what happened against him on Tuesday was a matter of ground balls finding holes. Additionally, Wellemeyer hasn't historically done well on long rest, and he had seven days between starts last time out. He'll need to be better against a potent Cubs team, but he's pitched very well against his old team.
away_pitcher_note: Harden showed he's a hearty Canadian in his last start. He shrugged off 40-degree temperatures at Wrigley Field to strike out eight over six innings against the Reds. The right-hander wore short sleeves despite the cold and gave up three hits. It was a much improved outing from his previous start, when he lasted three innings. He's now fanned 26 in his three starts. Harden won his only start against the Cardinals last season.

home_pitcher_note: Haren could easily be 4-0 right now instead of 1-3. Prior to his last start, Haren had received a total of one run of support in three games. The D-backs finally scored some runs for him against the Rockies last Wednesday when they put together a two-run rally in the seventh. Haren allowed just six hits over seven innings to pick up the 2-0 win. His 0-3 start marked the first time a pitcher had started the year losing his first three games while having an ERA under 2.00 since Juan Cruz did it for the Cubs in 2002. With every at-bat potentially a game-changer, Haren did not give in to Colorado hitters and wound up walking two. Overall he has walked just three and fanned 17 in his 19 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a win in his last start but pitched well enough to get a "W." Trouble is, he was outpitched by Johnny Cueto. In Lilly's last two starts, he has not given up an earned run in 13 2/3 innings, and has 10 strikeouts. Against the Reds in his last start, he did not walk a batter over seven innings, giving up five hits. Lilly used his curveball more against Cincinnati. It did the trick. The Reds' only score off him was set up by a throwing error he made fielding a bunt.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has taken Brandon Webb's place in the rotation while the right-hander recovers from shoulder stiffness. In two starts, Petit has allowed five earned runs in 10 innings. Unfortunately the bullpen has struggled both times he has pitched -- in his first outing against the Dodgers, which resulted in an 11-2 loss, and his last time out against the Rockies, which turned into a 9-6 Arizona loss. Petit has filled the spot-starter/long-relief role for the D-backs the past two seasons. Though he doesn't possess overpowering stuff, he has a good feel for pitching and generally has good command.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano took the loss in his last start against the Reds and Aaron Harang. Big Z gave up four runs on seven hits over seven innings while striking out seven. He didn't get much help from his defense -- or himself -- as the Cubs misplayed a couple of balls and Zambrano made a throwing error on a pickoff and the runner eventually scored. Zambrano is 1-2 with a 4.88 ERA in four career starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Any pitcher besides the reigning NL Cy Young Award winner would be a welcomed sight for Davis. The left-hander faced Giants ace Tim Lincecum in his last two starts, pitching eight innings in his first outing against San Francisco and six innings in the second. Davis struggled with his curveball in his last outing against the Giants and was charged with nine hits and five earned runs in the loss. He should be feeling confident at the plate after picking up an RBI against Lincecum.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster kept the Cubs in the game in his last start but didn't get much help. Facing the Cardinals, he gave up three runs on seven hits and one walk over six innings. Dempster struck out six in his second straight no-decision and third in four starts. Dempster said he felt good, but got into jams. He did not get a decision in his only start against the D-backs last year, giving up two earned runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty posted a quality start in his last outing against the Cardinals, but didn't get any offensive support. Marshall held the Redbirds to three runs on six hits and one walk over six innings, striking out five. He did his part, reaching on an error in the fifth which led to the Cubs' first run. He's 1-3 with a 4.38 ERA in his career against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad got the no-decision against the Phillies on Saturday after yielding three runs on four hits through seven innings. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up two solo home runs -- to opposing pitcher Chan Ho Park and Ryan Howard -- and ended up walking one while striking out six. In the sixth, Volstad had the bases loaded with nobody out, but he got out of it with just one run across when he got Ryan Howard to ground into a double play and forced Jayson Werth into a groundout to shortstop. On Thursday, he'll face a Cubs team he gave up four runs to through 12 innings in two no-decisions last year.

home_pitcher_note: Harden picked up the win in his last start, a 10-3 decision against the Cardinals. He struck out nine and gave up four hits, including two solo homers, over six innings. Harden admitted he didn't feel right at the start of the game, but as it progressed, his fastball seemed to pick up a few miles per hour, and it helped his changeup. He was hitting 95 mph on the radar gun pretty regularly.
away_pitcher_note: Not much was known about the 24-year-old Taylor before he made his Major League debut against the Phillies on Sunday. Based on his Minor League numbers, though, it was pretty apparent that he didn't walk many batters. That, however, wasn't the case in his first big-league inning, when he threw 22 of his 38 pitches for balls and ended up giving up two runs. Taylor finished off that game allowing four runs on four hits and six walks in 3 2/3 innings as the Marlins were routed at home. But two of those runs came on a misplay by Jeremy Hermida. The 2006 10th-round Draft pick finished throwing 98 pitches -- 49 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander uncharacteristically invited his own doom in his last start, which he began with the NL's top strikeouts (13) to walks (2) ratio. In five innings against the Diamondbacks, he walked four men, two of whom scored to help defeat him. Lilly has a tough bounce-back assignment: The Marlins are the only MLB team he has never defeated, with a career record of 0-4 and 5.53 ERA in five starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't all bad in Sanchez's last start. The right-hander did suffer a disappointing loss to the Mets at Citi Field. He did surrender a grand slam to Omir Santos in a six-run first inning. And he did log 40 pitches. From that point, though, you have to credit Sanchez for rebounding and soaking up five more innings, which took some pressure off the bullpen. In all, Sanchez worked six innings, allowing those six runs. His ERA rose from 2.50 to 4.13, however. Sanchez threw 108 pitches, a season high. Sanchez has faced the Cubs once in his career, and he won that decision. This will be his first start ever at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Both Zambranos were back in action in his last start, Tuesday in Arizona. The pitcher entered with a 4.85 ERA and held the D-backs to three runs in seven innings. The hitter had been 0-for-9 before logging a three-hit game that included his 17th career homer. Zambrano goes for career win No. 99 against a Marlins team he has handled well in the past.
away_pitcher_note: April was pretty much a struggle for Nolasco. In his five starts, he didn't have an outing longer than six innings, and he reached that total twice. His lone win came on Opening Day, and he had his troubles with shutdown innings. In his last start, at the Mets on April 28, Nolasco had a no-decision, giving up four runs in five innings. Nolasco kept his team in the game and left with the Marlins trailing by a run. Nolasco came up through the Cubs' system, and he was traded to Florida after the 2005 season as part of the Juan Pierre trade. In his lone appearance at Wrigley Field, Nolasco threw two scoreless innings in 2006. It was during his rookie season and it was his first MLB win.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Wednesday in Arizona, Dempster bid farewell to his perfect April record (5-0) since rejoining the rotation last season. But he actually pitched exceptionally well after a rough first inning, holding the D-backs to three hits in his last five frames.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez allowed no earned runs and just three hits in his most recent start on Tuesday, which normally would be a good sign. But he lasted only five innings and received no decision against the Dodgers, due partly to his teammates' misadventures in the field and on the bases. This will be Sanchez's first career start at Wrigley Field, where he has appeared only once in relief.

home_pitcher_note: Marshall was in line for a win in his last start against the Marlins. The lefty held the Fish to one run on six hits over seven innings, striking out six. But Florida rallied and won in extra innings. Marshall has struck out 15 over 18 innings in his last three starts. He pitched two innings in relief last year against the Giants, and is 1-2 with a 7.79 ERA in four games in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has tried to put his National League Cy Young Award-winning season behind him, insisting that it's a new season. Yet he keeps providing reminders of 2008 with his performance. Since going 0-1 with a 7.56 ERA in his first two starts, Lincecum's 2-0 in three starts with a 1.57 ERA. He also has walked four and struck out 33 in 23 innings over that span. Lincecum had one of his best starts last year at Wrigley Field on July 13, when he allowed one run, walked one and struck out nine in eight innings while hitting an RBI triple in a 4-2 Giants victory.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton's return to Atlanta didn't go in his favor, and he ended up tagged with a loss after allowing six runs (five earned) over 4 1/3 innings. The Braves scored four off him in the fifth, due partly to a Lance Berkman error that allowed the bases to be loaded with one out. Hampton has pitched well against the Cubs through his career, compiling a 9-4 record and a 2.98 ERA over 23 games (19 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Harden struggled with his control in his last outing against the Marlins. He walked four, matching a season high, and was pulled after 3 2/3 innings. It was his shortest outing since a 3 2/3-inning start against Texas on May 11, 2008. Harden had struck out 35 in 21 innings prior to the Florida game, when he fanned just two. He did not face the Astros on the Cubs' first trip to Houston, and did not get a decision in his only start against them last year. It also was the 17th time in his career he's given up five or more runs in a game.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz was skipped during the last time through the rotation due to Oswalt's availability after making a 17-pitch start in a rain-delayed game in Atlanta. Ortiz earned his second win of the season after allowing two runs over five innings in a 96-pitch outing against the Brewers in his last start. Ortiz walked four, but only one walk resulted in a run scored. He's frustrated that he's not going deeper into games, which is taxing the bullpen. Ortiz is working on getting ahead earlier in the count, which is something that has eluded him the last couple of starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly will have to pretend he's at Wrigley Field. So far, the lefty has given up one earned run over 21 2/3 innings at home, and has held opponents to a .151 average. In his last outing, he gave up five hits, including a solo homer by Florida's Cody Ross, and went eight innings in a 6-1 win. Lilly struck out 10, the 13th time in his career he's reached double digits. He also recorded only one groundout; the rest were strikeouts or fly-ball outs. And the wind was blowing out. He did beat the Astros in Houston on April 8, but has given up 10 earned runs over 10 innings in two road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush breezed through six innings against Arizona on Sunday, allowing back-to-back singles leading off the fourth but nothing else. But he imploded in the seventh inning, when Mark Reynolds and Justin Upton connected for back-to-back home runs to open the frame and No. 8 hitter Miguel Montero connected three batters later for a two-out, two-strike shot that tied the game and cost Bush a shot at his second win. Bush took a no-decision in his April 11 start against the Cubs, when he allowed three runs on six hits in 6 1/3 innings of an eventual 6-5 Brewers loss. He's just 1-7 against the Cubs in his career.
away_pitcher_note: This would have been Carlos Zambrano's spot in the rotation but he was placed on the 15-day disabled list on Monday with a Grade 2 strained hamstring. Wells was expected to be called up from Triple-A Iowa for the game. The right-hander has appeared in four big league games before, but has not made a start. Included in his starts for Iowa was a stellar effort April 22 when he gave up one hit over seven scoreless innings, striking out four. He walked two.

home_pitcher_note: He wasn't as dominant as his previous three starts (2-0, two earned runs in 23 innings), but Gallardo was still very good against the Pirates on a chilly Monday night in Pittsburgh. He scattered a season-high seven hits in seven innings and limited the damage to three runs, and his ERA over the last four starts is still an impressive 1.50. He missed the Cubs when they came through Milwaukee in early April, and he has yet to record a decision against them in two career starts (five runs in 12 innings for a 3.75 ERA). The last time Gallardo faced the Cubs was last May, when he suffered a serious right knee injury that cost him most of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster had his longest outing of the year in his last start, going seven innings against the Giants. The right-hander struck out seven and walked two while giving up two runs on five hits. It was his first win in two starts at home -- he was 14-3 last year at Wrigley Field. Somehow, he keeps getting assigned road games. He beat the Brewers on April 12 at Miller Park, holding them to four runs on six hits over six innings and striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan did just enough on a miserable night in Pittsburgh to continue his hot streak. He surrendered three runs on five hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings while working only one clean inning -- the fifth -- and throwing 108 pitches. He had not thrown that many since a 110-pitch win over the Cardinals last May 11, before Suppan developed the elbow discomfort that hampered him from June to the end of the season. He's on a roll of late. Since he surrendered 11 runs in 7 2/3 innings over his first two starts, including a nightmarish outing against the Cubs on April 13 in which he issued three bases-loaded walks, Suppan has gone 2-0 with a 3.38 ERA in four games.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall needs to wine and dine his teammates a little bit. The Cubs have scored six runs in the lefty's last three starts. He took the loss in his last game, a 6-2 decision to the Giants. Marshall served up a three-run homer to Bengie Molina in the first and then settled down and scattered four hits over the next six innings. He finished with one walk, one strikeout and threw 95 pitches over seven-plus innings. The arm strength is there, and Marshall is making the most of being on a regular schedule. Now, he just needs some offensive support.

home_pitcher_note: Harden pitched seven strong innings in his last start Wednesday at Houston before giving up three hits, including a two-run homer to Lance Berkman, in the eighth. He gave up three runs and eight hits and threw 99 pitches. He struck out four and walked three. It was his longest outing of the season. He had lasted six innings in three of his previous four starts. Harden, who spent the first 5 1/2 years of his career in the Majors with Oakland, has never faced San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy made one mistake in his last start and it cost him dearly. The right-hander struck out nine batters through five innings, struck out the first batter he faced in the sixth inning, walked a batter and then allowed a two-run home run to Justin Upton. Otherwise, Peavy was sharp, striking out a season-high 12 batters over seven innings and getting a lot of mileage out of his mid-90s fastball that he was able to spot on the outside corner at times as well as his slider. Peavy allowed four hits and had two walks. This coming on the heels of eight shutout innings against the Los Angeles Dodgers in his previous start. That's two starts, two runs, 15 innings and one loss and one no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: After pitching poorly in his first two road games of the season, Lilly threw well last Thursday at Houston to beat the Astros. He lasted six innings, giving up four hits and two runs, striking out five and walking three. He surrendered a two-run homer to Miguel Tejada in the first, but allowed only one hit over the next five innings. Lilly is 4-1 lifetime with a 2.84 ERA in six games against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Young wasn't quite as good as he was in his previous start against the Dodgers on May 2, when he allowed one run in seven innings, but he did pitch well against Arizona on May 7, as he allowed two runs on five hits over six innings. Young had some control issues, walking four, but he also had six strikeouts. He threw 98 pitches in six innings but was lifted for a pinch-hitter with the go-ahead run on base in the seventh inning against the Diamondbacks. Young will make only his second start at Minute Maid Park, where he is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA.
summary: 2009-05-13 - San Diego Padres @ Chicago Cubs (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Dempster was dealing with a small strike zone Saturday in Milwaukee, but he would have escaped with a quality start had he not gone out for a seventh inning. The right-hander threw 111 pitches through six innings, then retired the first man in the seventh before allowing back-to-back home runs -- one of them to light-hitting infielder Craig Counsell. That made for a jagged final line that included three walks and four earned runs, though he did finish with nine strikeouts. Dempster hasn't lasted fewer than six innings in any of his seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: One of these days, Gaudin will actually get to see the mound at pitcher-friendly PETCO Park. Until then, the right-hander will keep pitching on the road as he has in each of his first three starts for the Padres. Gaudin's start Thursday will be his fourth for the Padres, all coming away from San Diego. He is coming off a start where he allowed two runs over seven innings against the Astros at Minute Made Park. Gaudin was able to dial up his fastball to 94 mph at times and showed considerable late movement on his slider, a pitch the Astros had trouble with. Gaudin walked three batters, the third time he's walked at least three. But overall, his command was good.

home_pitcher_note: Wells acquitted himself admirably in his first Major League start Friday, pitching five shutout innings and extending his scoreless-innings streak to 10 1/3 to start his career. Wells wasn't terribly efficient, however, tossing 19 pitches in the first inning, 23 in the third and stranding two runners in each of the first three frames. Still, he settled and faced the minimum in the final two frames before the Cubs' bullpen took over and surrendered a late home run that cost Wells his first Major League win. The 26-year-old should get another shot with Carlos Zambrano still on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler had his best outing of the season in his last start, holding the Padres to one run over seven frames on Saturday. Since his return from the disabled list, he's allowed three runs over 12 innings spanning two starts. Moehler made his season debut against the Cubs at Minute Maid Park on April 8, but was knocked out after just 1 2/3 innings, during which he allowed seven earned runs. In his career, Moehler is 2-1 with a 3.09 ERA over 11 games (eight starts) versus the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Wells acquitted himself admirably in his first Major League start Friday, pitching five shutout innings and extending his scoreless-innings streak to 10 1/3 to start his career. Wells wasn't terribly efficient, however, tossing 19 pitches in the first inning, 23 in the third and stranding two runners in each of the first three frames. Still, he settled and faced the minimum in the final two frames before the Cubs' bullpen took over and surrendered a late home run that cost Wells his first Major League win. The 26-year-old should get another shot with Carlos Zambrano still on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt finally earned that elusive first win in his last start, against the Padres, holding them to four runs over six innings in a landslide Houston win. Oswalt, mainly a fastball-curveball pitcher, admitted he's using his slider more, for no other reason than "I don't know what I'm doing right now. I've kind of lost my mind." Prior to that win, Oswalt took five consecutive no-decisions after losing his first two starts of the season. Oswalt faced the Cubs on Opening Day, taking the loss after allowing three runs over seven frames. In his career against the Cubs, Oswalt is 12-12 with a 3.88 ERA over 27 career games, 26 of which were starts.

home_pitcher_note: Harden picked up the win in his last outing against the Padres, giving up two runs on four hits over six innings. He walked one, and that was encouraging.
