He is the first Phillies pitcher since Paul Byrd in 1998 to win his first two appearances in red and white while allowing fewer than two runs in each. The 2008 American League Cy Young Award winner is 1-0 with a 2.45 ERA in two career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Wells had the roughest start of his rookie season in his last start, snapping a four-game winning streak by allowing career highs of seven runs and five earned runs in his 5 1/3 innings at Coors Field. His slider was ineffective, and he relied on four-seam fastballs and cutters -- with poor results. Wells' big struggle was with his command, as he walked two but found too much of the plate in yielding eight hits. Perhaps most frustrating for Wells was his inability to adapt during the game and his difficulty bearing down and offering shutdown innings. As a result, he let the Rockies resume their attack every time the Cubs staged a minor comeback.
away_pitcher_note: Morton dropped his third straight decision in his last start despite not pitching too poorly against a hot Cardinals lineup. Morton limited St. Louis to one run on seven singles in five innings. His start was cut short, though, because of a quickly escalating pitch count. Morton need 93 pitches to get through five innings. The right-hander continues to struggle with his pitch-to-pitch and inning-to-inning consistency. But being that he has never pitched a full season in the Majors before, that is a somewhat expected growing pain. Morton has made one career start against the Cubs and lasted only 2 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny had a strong first outing for the Cubs after a July 30 trade from Pittsburgh, pitching 7 1/3 innings of one-run, three-hit ball against the Reds. His second time out couldn't have been much different as he was touched for six runs on six hits in 1 1/3 innings. He left the game after suffering a contusion on his right foot when it was struck by a hard-hit ball in the second inning, but X-rays showed no fracture and he is expected to make his next start. His two-out, two-run homer allowed to Troy Tulowitzki could be forgiven as the shortstop had a career night, hitting for the cycle and driving in seven, but Gorzelanny gave up four consecutive hits in the second, all of whom scored.
away_pitcher_note: In his fourth go at getting his 10th win of the year, Duke was denied the victory by his own defense and bullpen. Duke left his last start after 7 1/3 innings, having given up one earned run and one unearned one. He left a runner on base who would eventually score as Duke watched from the bench, which charged Duke with two earned runs allowed in the start. He has pitched at least six innings in 16 of his last 17 starts. Duke is 3-3 with a 3.19 ERA in six career starts at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Harden did not get a decision in his last start vs. the Phillies. He retired the first 16 batters he faced before walking Carlos Ruiz with one out in the sixth. One batter later, Jimmy Rollins spoiled Harden's no-hit bid with a two-run homer. That was one of two hits off Harden in his seven innings of work. He also struck out six. Harden has a 1.95 ERA in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf was nothing short of efficient in his last start as he gave up three runs on six hits in six-plus innings for the win against the Rockies on Tuesday. Ohlendorf is in the midst of a second-half surge as he's 3-1 with a 3.07 ERA in five starts -- the last four of which have been a quality start -- since the All-Star break. If there's anything that could derail him, it might be his ribs. Ohlendorf fielded a ground ball in the sixth inning against the Rockies and had his wind knocked out. He stayed in the ballgame and said he was a little sore postgame.

home_pitcher_note: Correia's 15th quality start of the season got him his eighth victory of the season on Wednesday, when he allowed three runs in six innings against the Brewers at Miller Park. Correia allowed six hits with two walks and four strikeouts and lowered his ERA to 4.51, though he was burned a two RBI singles after getting two strikes on the opposing hitter. It was the fourth consecutive quality start for Correia, who has allowed more than three runs once in his past eight starts. Correia got 10 ground-ball outs and didn't allow a home run for the sixth consecutive start.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly was expected to be activated from the disabled list for this start. The Cubs' lone All-Star, he had been sidelined because of inflammation in his shoulder. In a Minor League tuneup Wednesday for Class A Peoria, he threw 58 pitches over five scoreless innings. Lilly gave up two hits, both in the first inning, walked one and struck out two. He needed just four pitches to get through the fourth inning. This will be Lilly's first start since July 20. In that game against the Phillies, he lasted four innings, and gave up nine runs -- seven earned -- on eight hits over four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carrillo had a rough go in his Major League debut on Thursday against the Brewers. After working a 1-2-3 first inning, the right-hander -- added to the roster earlier in the day -- allowed a 465-foot home run to Prince Fielder in the second inning, back-to-back walks and a three-run homer to Mike Rivera. In the third inning, Carrillo allowed a two-run homer to his former University of Miami teammate Ryan Braun. He faced 15 batters in 2 /13 innings, allowing three home runs, two walks and eight runs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster took the loss in his last start against the Phillies. He struck out eight and gave up six runs on eight hits over seven innings. The right-hander gave up two home runs and now has served up 17 for the season, the most since 2002, when he was charged with 28 combined for Florida and Cincinnati. He should be happy to be on the road. In his last four home starts, Dempster is 1-2 with a 6.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Latos, the 21-year-old rookie and resident top prospect, finally got roughed up in his sixth Major League start. In that outing, Latos allowed the Cardinals seven runs on eight hits over four innings. He surrendered a home run to his counterpart, Adam Wainwright, and was gone in the fifth inning after he allowed the first four batters to reach base. There was nothing wrong with Latos' velocity, but his command wasn't nearly as sharp as it had been in his previous five starts, when he won four times. This will be Latos' first career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Harden was scheduled to start Sunday vs. the Pirates, but that game was postponed by rain. He now will start Wednesday in the series finale against the Padres. Harden is 2-1 with a 1.95 ERA in six starts since the All-Star break, with 47 strikeouts in 37 innings. He's walked 11. Opponents are batting just .150 against the right-hander. His last start was Aug. 11 vs. the Phillies, and he gave up two runs on two hits over seven innings but didn't get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Dodgers manager Joe Torre announced Tuesday that Jeff Weaver will start on Thursday against the Cubs in place of right-hander Hiroki Kuroda, who's recovering from a mild concussion sustained last Saturday. Weaver has started six games for the Dodgers this season, going 2-1 with a 3.08 ERA. His most recent start came in San Francisco on Aug. 12, when he threw three scoreless innings in what was a bullpen day for the Dodgers. Torre said one of the reasons he decided to go with Weaver was because of how the right-hander matched up with the Cubs' lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has made three starts since the Pirates dealt him to the Cubs prior to the non-waiver Trade Deadline; two of them have been good. He held the Reds to one run in 7 1/3 innings in his first start, but in his second start -- against the Rockies -- Gorzelanny was hit in the foot by a line drive and left after surrendering six runs in 1 1/3  innings. However, Gorzelanny bounced back on Saturday, pitching against his old team and making his first start at Wrigley Field as a member of the Cubs. Although he lasted only five innings, Gorzelanny held the Pirates to one run on three hits and struck out eight, one short of his career high. Gorzelanny even struck out the side in the third, dominating the opposing hitters with a high fastball that got up to 93 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf restored order in the wake of Hiroki Kuroda's frightening incident and a bitter extra-inning loss. He took a one-hit shutout into the eighth inning for his ninth quality start in the last 10 outings. He struck out a season-high 10 without a walk, effectively spotting both his fastball and slow curve, and he added his fifth career home run. He's 4-7 lifetime against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells had his worst start of the season on Aug. 9 against the Rockies but bounced back in his last start, against the Pirates on Friday. He benefited from 17 runs of support, throwing six innings and giving up two runs on seven hits. The rookie has won nine of his past 11 starts behind a two-seam fastball that produces many ground balls and makes up for a lack of strikeouts. Wells has held the opposition to three earned runs or fewer in 14 of his 18 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Haeger pitched seven solid innings Monday night against the Cardinals and could get the starting nod against the Cubs. Dodgers manager Joe Torre said after Monday's game that Haeger definitely earned another start but didn't say with any certainty when or if that would be. Much of the decision hinges on who pitches in place of Hiroki Kuroda on Thursday. Kuroda is recovering from a mild concussion, which he sustained Saturday at Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly deserved better in his first start back from being on the DL. The lefty threw six scoreless innings against the Padres, giving up four hits and walking one. In his last 64 2/3 innings, he's walked 10 and struck out 59. He hasn't gotten much support, going 2-6 when he gets three runs or less. He beat the Dodgers on May 29 at Wrigley, holding them to one run on four hits over seven innings. Good news is he had no problems with his shoulder or knee and said he felt healthy.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley looked strong Tuesday night against the Cardinals in his first start back from a strained left hamstring.  Billingsley cruised through the first five innings, allowing just one hit and walking none. And then in the sixth he prevented a big inning by forcing Albert Pujols to ground into an inning-ending double play. Billingsley only threw 77 pitches, which fit in with the Dodgers plan to limit him to between 80-90 pitches in his first outing since Aug. 7 against the Braves. In all, Billingsley gave up two runs on three hits in six innings on the mound. Billingsley is 1-2 with a 3.27 ERA in five career appearances (three of them starts) against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster struck out a season-high 10 batters in his last outing, against the Padres, for his 11th career double-digit strikeout game. He also gave up four runs on eight hits in seven innings, and the Cubs couldn't match that. Dempster wasn't happy with himself -- especially after serving up a solo homer to Adrian Gonzalez leading off the fifth. He's 1-2 with a 4.15 ERA in four starts this month. Opponents were batting .258 off Dempster in the first half. In the second half, they're hitting .296.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano is expected to be activated from the disabled list for this game. Big Z was sidelined because of back spasms, and vowed to be more devoted to doing his abdominal exercises. The Cubs needed their ace this month, but he has made one start, lasting three innings on Aug. 1. He hasn't been as dominating at home, posting a 2-2 record in nine starts with a 3.55 ERA. Zambrano is 5-2 with a 3.17 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Mock continues to get better as a pitcher, but he had some bad luck on Thursday night as the Nationals lost to the Rockies, 4-1, at Nationals Park. Mock cruised through the first four innings, allowing just one hit and striking out six batters. In the fifth inning, however, the Rockies scored two runs, and Mock became the losing pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Harden was stellar in his last start. The right-hander held the Padres to one hit over seven innings, striking out eight. He has fanned 55 in 44 innings since the All-Star break and held teams to eight runs in that stretch. Although he doesn't like to acknowledge the numbers, Harden is better at night and on the road. He is 3-5 with a 6.31 ERA at Wrigley Field. He beat Washington in D.C. on July 16.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals signed Hernandez to a Major League contract on Tuesday night, six days after the Mets gave the veteran his unconditional release. Hernandez will be in the rotation and serve as a mentor for Washington's young starting pitchers. In fact, he will start against the Cubs on Wednesday night, while right-hander J.D. Martin and left-hander John Lannan will be pushed back a day and pitch on Thursday and Friday respectively.

home_pitcher_note: Wells should have received his 10th win in his last start, but he didn't get any run support. Wells gave up two runs -- both unearned -- on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings, while the Cubs were held to one hit by the Dodgers. Wells said he lost his focus briefly, but it definitely was brief. It stung that the only runs off Wells were driven in by opposing pitcher Randy Wolf, who hit a two-run double.
away_pitcher_note: Martin's rookie season has been an up-and-down one, but he has proven to be adept at keeping the Nationals in ballgames and is beginning to build up some innings. He took the loss in his last outing, a 7-3 setback to the Brewers on Friday, but worked a career-best 6 2-3 innings and matched a career high with four strikeouts. In that game, Martin managed to record first-pitch strikes on 20 of his 28 hitters, but he also allowed two first-pitch homers, running up the total of home runs against him to seven in 34 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly has given up two runs in 12 innings in his last two starts, but has yet to get a win -- or much offensive support. The left-hander took the loss in his last start against the Dodgers, serving up two home runs among the three hits he gave up in six innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out five. In his last 70 2/3 innings, Lilly has walked 10 and struck out 64. He leads the Cubs with 16 quality starts. Wrigley Field has been kind to Lilly, who is 6-1 with a 1.86 ERA in nine home starts.
away_pitcher_note: A starter for most of this season in the Minors, Misch will make his first big league start since last year with the Giants. He was 0-1 with a 2.89 ERA in 18 2/3 relief innings with the Mets this season, and a 3.68 mark as a starter in Triple-A. In 2007 with the Giants, Misch pitched two relief innings at Wrigley Field, allowing three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster gave up one run -- unearned -- over seven-plus innings for the win in his last start, against the Dodgers. The right-hander struck out five and was pulled after 101 pitches. He was able to mix speeds well and keep the Dodgers off balance. The three runs scored by the Cubs were a surprise. Dempster has received two or fewer runs in 10 of his 23 starts, and he's 0-6 in those games. He is 4-2 with a 5.01 ERA in nine starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Parnell's fourth start in the big leagues found the middle ground between the brilliance of his second and the nightmare of his third. Parnell gave up five runs in five innings -- all of them on two Ryan Howard home runs. Parnell walked three and hit a batter but was also the victim of some poor defense, as three errors were made behind him. His ERA as a starter is now 8.82. Parnell made two relief appearances against the Cubs late last season, allowing a run on two hits in three innings. Ryan Theriot is the only Cub with a hit off Parnell, as the rest of the team is 0-for-5.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since Aug. 1, Zambrano gave up a season-high eight runs on seven hits over 4 1/3 innings on Aug. 25 against the Nationals and took the loss. Zambrano did show that his back is OK when he hit his fourth homer of the season with one out in the third. He fell behind in the count often and wasn't sharp. The eight runs were the most Big Z has served up since giving up eight last Sept. 19 against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Based more on the lack of available options than his five-inning performance Tuesday in Miami, Figueroa will start again for the Mets on Sunday against the Cubs. He allowed just two runs in his last outing, one of them earned, and afterward cited the Marlins unfamiliarity with his five-pitch array as the reason. If that is indeed why, he may face trouble at Wrigley. Only four big league teams have faced Figueroa more often in his career than the Cubs, who have tagged him for a 4.40 ERA and hit him at a .266 clip. Lifetime, Figueroa is 0-4 against them.

home_pitcher_note: Harden did not get a decision in his last start against the Nationals. He gave up two runs on five hits and two walks over six innings but was pulled with the game tied. It's a good thing this game is at night. The right-hander has given up 19 earned runs over 75 1/3 innings in night games compared to 36 earned runs over 48 2/3 innings during the day time. Harden is 1-1 this year against the Astros, posting a win on May 6 and taking the loss May 17.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his four-game winning streak come to a halt Wednesday in St. Louis, where he gave up 10 hits and three runs in six innings. Afterward, Oswalt criticized his teammates for not playing with desire, prompting Lance Berkman to call a players-only meeting the following day. Oswalt lasted only 1 2/3 innings in his last start at Wrigley Field on July 28 because of a lower back strain. He's 0-1 with a 3.68 ERA in three starts against the Cubs this year and 12-12 with a 3.86 ERA in 29 career games, including 28 starts, against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Wells had trouble with his slider in his last start against the Nationals, and wasn't able to get the ground-ball outs that he normally does. The right-hander served up five runs on five hits and four walks over 6 1/3 innings and took the loss. He's trying to become the first Cubs rookie to reach double-digit wins since Kerry Wood won 13 games in 1998. Wells now has given up five earned runs in two of his last three starts. In two starts against Houston this year, he's not given up a single run over 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Roy Oswalt taking the hill on Monday, Brian Moehler is on tap to face Randy Wells and the Cubs. Moehler turned in a quality start in his last game, though he wasn't around to get the decision in a 4-3 victory over the Cardinals. He allowed three runs on six hits in six innings. Moehler has been far better on the road this season, compiling a 4.35 ERA compared to a 6.14 mark at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly has notched three consecutive solid starts since his return from the disabled list on Aug. 17. He is 0-1 but has posted a 1.86 ERA in that stretch. In his last start, Lilly gave up two runs on six hits in 7 1/3 innings against the Mets for his 17th quality start in 22 outings this season. He has a quality start in all 10 of his outings at Wrigley Field and a 1.92 ERA there. Lilly will next take on the Astros, against whom he has a 3.57 ERA in three appearances this season, all in Houston.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander will make his first start since July 3, when he gave up nine hits and nine runs (eight earned) in two innings in a 13-0 loss to the Giants. He's been relegated to bullpen duty since, mostly in mop-up roles. With a fastball near 100-mph, Paulino's time to prove himself might be running out, if the recent comments made by general manager Ed Wade were any indication. Wade said Paulino needs to take advantage of every chance he gets to pitch, and this start could loom large for his career with the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster has won successive starts for the first time this season. He held the Dodgers to one run on Aug. 23 and gave up four runs in six innings in his last start Saturday against the Mets, but got plenty of offensive support. Dempster has a 4.30 ERA in seven starts since he came off the disabled list July 28, and in his past four outings, he has struck out 30 batters in 27 innings. He will get the call against the White Sox in the makeup of a game that was rained out June 16. Dempster started against the Sox the next day and lost, giving up three runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old makes his third career start and arguably his most important one when facing the Crosstown rivals from the North Side of town. Torres had a triumphant year at Triple-A Charlotte but has allowed seven runs on nine hits over 9 1/3 innings this season in starts against Cleveland and Tampa Bay. Torres has also walked nine and struck out eight. Torres is trying to take hold of the No. 5 starter spot for the near future, when needed, until Jake Peavy gets health.

home_pitcher_note: Afforded leads of 2-0 and 4-3 against the Cubs on Saturday, Parnell allowed eight runs in 4 2/3 innings, the last coming on a grand slam by Jake Fox on an 0-2 slider. His record as a starter after five starts is 1-4. His ERA in those games increased Saturday even though it stood at 8.82 before the game. It's 10.29 now. The slam wasn't the only problem. Parnell surrendered eight other hits and two walks, one a leadoff walk to the opposing pitcher.  He needed 109 pitches to achieve 14 outs. Jerry Manuel didn't commit to Parnell as a member of the rotation beyond this start against the Cubs. But the manager has few alternatives.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano faced the Mets on Sunday, and the results were not pretty. New York pounded the righty for 11 hits and four runs (three earned) in 3 1/3 innings in a 4-1 Cubs loss. Zambrano has not been himself since he came off the disabled list, giving up 12 runs on 18 hits in 7 2/3 innings over two games. The back spasms that sidelined the righty do not appear to be an issue, but he is having mechanical difficulties with his delivery. After Zambrano's last start, manager Lou Piniella said the righty was opening up his front shoulder too much and dragging his arm, which gave hitters too long of a look at the ball. When this happens, Zambrano does not generate the number of swings and misses that he typically does.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa was fantastic in his last outing at Wrigley Field, giving up one run on six hits in seven innings while striking out a career-high 10 batters. Figueroa now has a 2.59 ERA in his last eight appearances, including two starts. Figueroa's ERA in his seven home appearances this season is 6.87, compared to a 1.32 mark in three games on the road. With the win over the Cubs, Figueroa improved to 1-4 with a 3.79 ERA in his career vs. Chicago. Aramis Ramirez is 5-for-12 off Figueroa in his career, including a home run.
away_pitcher_note: Harden had a 1.80 ERA in his first eight starts after the All-Star break but hit a rough spot in his last outing, which came Monday against the Astros. He struck out nine but lost his command and walked six in five innings, giving up five earned runs. Harden also gave up a homer to Carlos Lee, the 22nd long ball he has surrendered this season in 129 innings. He generally has pitched better on the road this season, posting a 5-2 record and a 2.02 ERA away from Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey has taken a step back in his past two starts, losing back-to-back games, but more importantly facing serious command issues. He has walked five batters twice this season, and both have come in his past two starts.  Pelfrey gave up seven runs (six earned) on six hits and five walks at Coors Field on Tuesday, losing hitters he'd gotten ahead on, 0-2, and walking three men in the first inning to load the bases and bring a man home. Manager Jerry Manuel has chalked the struggles up to youth, but he has emphasized that Pelfrey needs to show he can bounce back and deliver again to avoid concerns about his security in the Mets' rotation in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Wells finally picked up his 10th win in his last start to become the first Cubs rookie to reach double-digit wins since Kerry Wood won 13 in 1998. Wells gave up one run, unearned, on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. He struck out four. It was his sixth win in his last nine starts. The Cubs want to be careful with Wells and his innings pitched. He's over his personal best in the Minors. He has thrown six or more innings in four straight starts. The Cubs may want to save him for games vs. NL Central teams. He's 6-1 with a 1.78 ERA in 10 starts against division foes.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen made his Major League debut last Monday and fared pretty well. After allowing a leadoff homer, McCutchen settled in to finish six innings. He allowed three runs and five hits. With the Pirates now going with a six-man rotation for the rest of the season, McCutchen will be a mainstay among the starters. He's not going to overwhelm anyone with his fastball, which is in the 90- to 93-mph range, but he's a guy with above-average command.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly picked up his 10th win in his last start, against the Astros. The lefty threw eight scoreless innings, giving up four hits and striking out five. With the win, he's posted seven straight 10-win seasons. Over his past 86 innings, Lilly has walked 12 and struck out 71. In his past four starts, he's given up four earned runs over 27 1/3 innings for a 1.32 ERA. The only thing wrong with his win over the Astros was an ill-advised attempt to steal second and his head-first slide into the base. He won't be doing that again.

home_pitcher_note: Duke looked as if he was in line for a win entering the sixth inning with a 3-2 lead on Wednesday against the Reds, but fielding woes and a home run by Drew Stubbs turned that chance at a win into a loss. Duke pitched six innings and gave up five runs, three of which were earned in a 5-3 loss. He has lost three of his past four decisions. Duke will look to get back on the winning track against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster was a hard-luck loser in his last start, on Thursday against the White Sox. For the second time this season, all three runs he gave up in a game were unearned, although he also allowed nine hits. Dempster did pitch seven innings, his seventh consecutive outing in which he lasted at least six frames. In his one start against the Pirates this season, Dempster was roughed up for six earned runs in four innings, although five of Pittsburgh's starting position players in that game have since been traded.

home_pitcher_note: The command that Hart showed while with the Cubs earlier this season continues to come only in short spurts here with Pittsburgh. Hart was chased after allowing seven runs (five earned) in 5 2/3 innings his last time out. After going 3-1 with a 2.60 ERA in four starts with the Cubs, Hart has gone 1-4 with a 6.35 ERA in six starts with Pittsburgh. He's had little consistency with his command and has given up six home runs.
away_pitcher_note: While Zambrano hasn't won a game since July 22 at Philadelphia and has spent a session on the disabled list with muscle spasms in his back since that victory, he showed in his last start he may be rounding back into form. He was 0-2 in two starts since coming off the disabled list before he pitched six innings of three-hit baseball and yielded only a solo home run in a no-decision against the Mets at Citi Field on Sept. 4. He has faced the Pirates only once this season. He gave up two runs, one of which was earned, on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision on May 27 in Chicago. He's 6-1 lifetime at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Harden was effective in his five innings against the Mets on Saturday, allowing two runs (one earned) on seven hits while striking out 10. A high pitch count, however, prevented him from going further into the game. Harden is 4-1 with a 2.67 ERA in five career starts against the Reds. This is the fourth time this season Harden will face Cincinnati. He won his first two starts against the Reds before dropping an Aug. 5 decision, 4-0. In that game, Harden allowed three runs (two earned) in six innings. The current Reds roster can't speak to much success against Harden, as it is just 4-for-43 lifetime against the right-hander. Joey Votto and Scott Rolen each have home runs against Harden.
away_pitcher_note: After missing a turn in the rotation with a strained groin, Lehr made it through his Wednesday side bullpen session with no issues and was named Friday's starter. The injury was sustained during his previous start on Sept. 1 vs. Pirates. Despite feeling the strain on his second pitch of the game, Lehr gutted it out for 114 pitches in the game. He worked six innings and gave up four earned runs, six hits and five walks with two strikeouts during an 11-5 win over the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Wells had another stellar outing on Sunday at Citi Field, holding the Mets to seven hits and two runs (one earned) in six innings. Wells' start was foiled, however, by an unearned run in the sixth and a lack of run support. Wells is making his fourth start of the year against the Reds. He is 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in the previous three, and the Cubs have won all three games. In his one home start against Cincinnati, Wells gave up three runs on seven hits in six innings. No current Reds player has an extra-base hit off Wells, though Brandon Phillips is 3-for-8 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto allowed three hits and a run over six innings at Atlanta on Sunday, striking out nine in the no-decision. He walked two and hit two batters, throwing 107 pitches in his second start since coming off the disabled list. Cueto got a victory against Pittsburgh on Aug. 31 to snap a six-game losing streak. He worked into the sixth in that game, the only run scoring on a homer to lead off that inning. Cueto gave up just two other hits and struck out five while walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly served up two runs on two hits over six innings in his last start against the Pirates. The lefty struck out seven, and now has 78 K's in his last 92 innings. He's walked 15 in that stretch. Lilly didn't dominate, just located very, very well. He now has 43 wins since 2007, which ranks among the top in the National League. He was pulled after 87 pitches, so he should be fresh. In his only start against the Reds this season, Lilly took the loss, but held them to one run, unearned, on five hits over seven innings. It was one of his 19 quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey is unbeaten over his last four starts with a 3-0 record and 1.67 ERA. But the latest outing was good, not great. Bailey lasted only 5 2/3 innings for a no-decision during the Reds' 4-3 loss on Monday. He had to be lifted earlier than hoped because he tossed 117 pitches in that short amount of time, with five walks. Bailey allowed only one earned run and five hits with five strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster picked up the win in his last start, against the Pirates, but was helped by a seven-run first inning. That will make any starting pitcher relax. Dempster wasn't sharp and admitted that after the game, and scattered eight hits over 6 1/3 innings. He's 5-3 with a 4.59 ERA at Wrigley, and will be shooting for his 10th win, which would be his fourth season in double-digit wins and second in a row. He's 2-1 against the Brewers this season, last facing them July 2 and picking up a win in a 9-5 Cubs victory.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan didn't have good command in his most recent start against the Cardinals, and it cost him in a three-run fifth inning in which St. Louis hit for the cycle. The big blow was a two-run homer to Albert Pujols, who got ahead in the count, 2-and-0, before hammering a misplaced fastball. "I just tried to move it around and locate the best I could," Suppan said. He has been much more effective this season on the road, going 4-2 with a 3.80 ERA in 12 starts. At Miller Park, Suppan is 2-7 with a 6.39 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano picked up his first win since July 22 in his last start vs. the Pirates. Big Z gave up two runs on five hits over six innings and struck out eight. But how long will he go against the Brewers? Zambrano wasn't happy when Lou Piniella pulled him in the sixth, and the Cubs manager said next time, he'll let the right-hander go the distance, even if it means he throws 200 pitches. Will he or won't he? Piniella did say he wants Zambrano to win three, four more games in the final stretch. He's got about four starts left in the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Worried about the 23-year-old's workload after he spent most of last season on the disabled list, the Brewers skipped Gallardo's last start. That means Gallardo should be fresh for his return to Wrigley Field, site of the devastating knee injury on May 1 of last season that cost Gallardo all but four regular-season starts. Gallardo said he understood the decision by Brewers officials to limit his starts the rest of the way. "I don't want to be shut down. I want to finish out the year strong," Gallardo said. "We're trying to find ways to make that happen. It's somewhat of [a compromise]. I feel like everything is coming out nice and easy. You have to deal with it, I guess. It's in the best interests for me. I know they're looking out."

home_pitcher_note: Harden has pitched well this season and has a 2.39 ERA since the All-Star break. Yet the Cubs have him on a strict pitch count and rarely allow him to throw much more than 100 in order to keep him healthy. When you combine that with a lot of strikeouts and walks, you get some short outings, like the one Harden had in his last start, Friday against the Reds. In that game, he walked five and although he gave up just one run, he left after four innings after throwing 103 pitches. Of Harden's 25 starts, 10 have lasted fewer than six innings, including each of the past three.
away_pitcher_note: Looper has a 3.52 ERA over his past five starts, including a Friday win at Arizona that was quite lucrative for the right-hander. By simply making his 30th start this season, Looper maxed out the performance bonuses in his 2009 contract (meaning an additional $750,000 on top of his $4.75 million salary) and increased the price of his mutual option for 2010. The base salary for that option increased $500,000 to $6.5 million, and the buyout, should the Brewers decline, increased $250,000 to $1 million. Even at a slightly higher price, the Brewers probably want Looper back next season because he's tied for the team lead in wins (pending Yovani Gallardo's start in Chicago on Tuesday) and second among Brewers starters with a .278 batting average against.

home_pitcher_note: Wells has gone at least six innings in 19 of his 23 starts but matched his shortest outing of the season in his last start, on Saturday against the Reds. The National League Rookie of the Year contender pitches to contact with his sinker, which makes him reliant on his infield defense, and that defense let him down. Three errors led to two unearned runs in the second inning, and Wells was knocked out after surrendering five runs in 3 2/3 frames. Wells has not faced the Brewers since his Major League debut back on May 8, when he pitched five scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bush is trying to author a happy ending to an injury-marred season, and his past two starts have him on the way to doing just that. Bush pitched seven innings in each of those outings -- vs. the Cardinals on Sept. 7 and then at Arizona on Saturday -- and allowed three earned runs on 12 hits. Compare that to his previous two starts, in which Bush, fresh off two months on the disabled list with a triceps injury, was tagged for 13 runs and 15 hits in eight total innings. He has thrown 97 pitches in each of his past two outings, further allaying fears that his triceps was still giving him trouble. Bush is 1-7 in his career against the Cubs despite a respectable 4.62 ERA in 13 starts and one relief appearance. He has no decisions and a 3.38 ERA in two starts against the Cubs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Smoltz is returning from a mild bout of shoulder tendinitis, but he insists it's nothing serious at all. He started feeling better almost immediately after getting a shot in the area, and he's eager to get back on the mound. For a renowned big-game pitcher, Friday will represent the biggest game since he joined the Cardinals. His team is slumping and facing its biggest rival.
away_pitcher_note: In Lilly's last start, Sunday against the Reds, he won his 44th game since joining the Cubs in 2007, tying him with Milt Pappas for the most victories in a player's first three seasons with Chicago since 1969. Since coming off the disabled list Aug. 17, Lilly has compiled a 1.37 ERA in six starts, striking out 30 and walking eight. But the All-Star lefty has not been as effective on the road this season, with an ERA about three runs higher than his 1.60 mark at Wrigley Field. He has a 2.40 ERA in two starts against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will be looking to put an uncharacteristic outing behind him. His last time out, he was touched for seven runs, six of them in one inning. He insisted it was just a matter of the one inning, but manager Tony La Russa said Carpenter looked a little off all night. Either way, he'll be watched closely as he faces the Cubs in a nationally televised Saturday afternoon contest.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster picked up the win in his last start against the Brewers. He held Milwaukee to four hits and one walk over eight scoreless innings. Dempster has faced the Cardinals three times this season, and has two no-decisions and one loss. In his last three games, he's given up seven runs over 21 1/3 innings while striking out 15. He joins John Smoltz as the only pitchers to record at least three straight 20-save seasons followed by consecutive 10-win campaigns as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright gets the Sunday night ESPN game, and he'd have it no other way. Wainwright loves big moments, and the final Cubs-Cardinals game of the year certainly qualifies. He's back to form after a one-game hiccup at the start of the month, and he's still just two wins away from a milestone 20th. Wainwright has faced the Cubs four times already this year, going 3-0 with a 2.67 ERA and an average of over 7 1/3 innings per start.
away_pitcher_note: It looked like Zambrano was in top form Tuesday when he took on the Brewers at Wrigley Field and sailed through four innings, striking out eight and giving up one hit. He then got two outs in the fifth before allowing a single to pitcher Yovani Gallardo that snowballed into a five-run inning and knocked Zambrano out of the game. That inning raised Zambrano's ERA to 6.93 in five starts since he came off the disabled list Aug. 25. He had one rough outing against the Cardinals this season, allowing seven runs in seven innings on April 17 but held St. Louis to three runs in six innings on July 12.

home_pitcher_note: Looper struggled to get through the fifth inning at Wrigley Field on Wednesday but managed to win his 13th game, a new career high after notching 12 wins in each of the previous two seasons as a starter. He had to work through some discomfort, the result of a batting practice line drive that struck him square in the back the previous afternoon and caused his back to tighten in the middle innings of his outing against the Cubs. He knew he was chasing a personal milestone. "I knew that going in," Looper said. "I had 12 [wins] every year, and to get the 13th is nice."
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs have decided to skip Rich Harden and insert Gorzelanny into the rotation. Harden was roughed up by the Brewers in his last start, giving up five runs on five hits and three walks over three innings. This will be Gorzelanny's fifth start with the Cubs. He's 2-1 with a 4.74 ERA in nine appearances since joining Chicago on July 30. In his four previous starts with the Cubs, the lefty is 2-1 with a 4.82 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bush pitched 5 2/3 innings to beat the Cubs on Thursday, then hustled home to welcome a new member to the family. Bush's wife, Carrie, was to be induced into labor on Friday morning. "He had a lot on his mind with the baby coming, and that's something we had been talking a lot about over the last couple of days," Brewers pitching coach Chris Bosio said. "He gave us a chance to win it, and that's what we're looking for. The offense and the bullpen came through." Jody Gerut provided most of the offense with a grand slam, and four relievers worked the final 3 1/3 innings for a 7-4 win. It was a rare win for Bush, who is just 2-7 against the Cubs despite a respectable 4.73 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wells was upset with himself after giving up five earned runs in four innings in his last start, Thursday against the Brewers. The rookie walked a season-high five, for a total of eight in his past 7 2/3 innings. That's not a recipe for success for Wells, who issued two or fewer free passes in 19 of his first 22 starts. But Wells said manager Lou Piniella "hit a nerve," when they talked in the dugout after Wells' outing. Piniella told his pitcher to go back to doing what he has for most of this season: challenging hitters in the strike zone and getting ahead in the count, rather than nibbling at the corners of the plate. Wells said he will fix the problem before his next start.

home_pitcher_note: With Manny Parra's ailing neck still an issue, Narveson is likely to make a third straight start instead, and he certainly did nothing to dissuade his use on Friday. Narveson threw five innings and allowed just one run, the lengthiest outing of his big league career. He has allowed just five earned runs since rejoining the team from Triple-A Nashville on Aug. 21, posting a 2.11 ERA over nine appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija will sub for Ted Lilly, who is being given a few extra days because of tendinitis in his left shoulder. This will be Samardzija's second big league start. He made his first start Aug. 12 against Philadelphia, giving up seven runs on eight hits over 3 1/3 innings while striking out four. The right-hander, who was the Cubs' fifth-round pick in 2006, has split time this season between the big league team and Triple-A Iowa. For the season, he's 1-2 with a 7.89 ERA in 19 games with the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Penny's 3-3 with a 2.64 ERA lifetime against the Cubs. He has enjoyed pitching thus far at AT&T Park, where he's 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two starts since joining San Francisco. Penny is coming off his worst start as a Giant, yielding seven runs and five hits while walking three in only 2 2/3 innings last Saturday at Los Angeles. Penny complained that he wasn't throwing decent offspeed pitches, which hampered his performance significantly.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his last start, despite a stellar effort. He went eight innings, striking out six. It was his 10th consecutive start of six or more innings, and second consecutive outing of eight innings. Dempster beat the Giants on May 4 at Wrigley Field, giving up two runs on five hits over seven innings and striking out seven. He's now 3-1 in his last six road starts, and has given up 11 earned runs over 40 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum must accumulate 21 strikeouts in his remaining pair of projected starts to eclipse Christy Mathewson's modern-day franchise record of 267, which was set in 1903. He's also striving to become only the ninth Giant since the franchise moved to San Francisco in 1958 to win the National League ERA title. He'd be the first to accomplish that feat since Jason Schmidt did so in 2003. No Giant in franchise history has led the league in both ERA and strikeouts. In Lincecum's previous appearance against the Cubs this year, he worked seven innings at Wrigley Field, allowing two runs and four hits in a 6-2 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano did not get a decision in his last start against the Cardinals. He gave up two runs on five hits over six innings, striking out six and left in line for the win. With his six Ks, he passed Greg Maddux and moved into sole possession of fifth place on the Cubs' all-time strikeout list. He now has one win in his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: For all the disappointments and criticism he has received on the other side of the Bay, Zito has been a terrific September-stretch pitcher throughout his career. A short (4 1/3-inning) no-decision outing in his last start, in Arizona, was a rare blip on a radar which has seen him go 23-9 in 45 September starts when his team has been in a playoff race. The left-hander has been as reliable in the second half of this season, having essentially halved his ERA (5.01 before the All-Star break and 2.58 since). A wounded team like the Cubs could be perfect for keeping alive Zito's hopes of a .500 season.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will get another look before the season ends. The lefty started Monday against the Brewers and matched his career high in strikeouts with nine. He gave up two runs on six hits over five innings. He figures in the Cubs' plans in 2010, either in the rotation or as a long man in the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: It's fair to say that Cain has been slumping. A National League All-Star, Cain has one win in his past 11 starts and a 6.75 ERA in his past five. The longball has plagued Cain, who has yielded two home runs in four of his past 10 starts. The Cubs occupy a prominent place in Cain's personal history. He threw his first career complete game against them, a two-hitter, on Sept. 9, 2005. Lifetime, Cain is 4-2 with a 2.81 ERA against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie pitcher apparently was able to convince the Cubs to give him two more starts. Wells was worried his last game, last Tuesday in Milwaukee, would be his last. Instead, he has a chance at two more wins. In his last outing, Wells gave up one run on seven hits, including Prince Fielder's 41st homer. That was Wells' first win since Sept. 1. He's won five of his last eight road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his last start, but did post his seventh quality start in his last 11 outings. He has thrown six or more innings in 26 of his 29 starts. Dempster is trying to finish with 200 innings this year, and will make two more starts -- this one vs. the Pirates and in the season finale Oct. 4. His next win will be No. 87, and he would be the second active pitcher with 87 wins and 87 saves. John Smoltz has 213 wins and 154 saves.
away_pitcher_note: Hart did not look good in his last start, one in which he lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up eight runs on eight hits and three walks. It was a step backward for the righty, who, in his previous outing, finally found some consistency with his command and new delivery' motion. This time he pitched with hardly any fastball command and never found any rhythm with his slider. This might be Hart's last start of the season and it's one from which he'd like to salvage something positive. Since coming to the Pirates, he is 1-6 with a 6.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was given a few extra days this week because of tendinitis in his left shoulder. He should've gotten the win in his last outing against the Cardinals. The lefty gave up two runs on five hits over 7 2/3 innings, striking out six. He did not walk a batter, the 10th start this year in which he has done that. Lilly did notch career strikeout No. 1,300, but he'd rather have the "W." The lefty was pulled in the eighth after throwing 110 pitches so he didn't have to face Albert Pujols. St. Louis won on a walk-off homer by Matt Holliday. Lilly has faced the Brewers once this year, July 5, and won.
away_pitcher_note: His line may not be overly impressive, but Morton actually pitched quite well his last time out. He allowed four runs on four two-out hits in the third inning, but otherwise dominated. Manager John Russell lauded Morton's improved aggressiveness afterward. Morton has seemed to find some control of the movement he has on his pitches, and the result of that is improved efficiency. This will be Morton's first start at Wrigley Field since a disastrous outing there in August when he allowed 10 runs in just one inning.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano was masterful in his last outing, throwing a two-hit shutout against the Giants, who were battling to stay alive in the NL Wild Card race. Zambrano fanned eight in his first shutout since his no-hitter last September 2008. Big Z gave up two singles, and he also drove in two runs. With a win against the Pirates, Zambrano has a chance to finish the season with double-digit wins for the seventh straight year. Zambrano now has made 237 starts for the Cubs, passing Dick Ellsworth for 13th on the team's all-time list.
away_pitcher_note: As he did on Friday, Karstens will lead a parade of bullpen arms to help the Pirates get through this game. The Pirates need Karstens to start in place of Ross Ohlendorf, who has been shut down because of a high innings total. The right-hander allowed one run on three hits in three innings of relief in his last spot start. The Pirates would ideally like to get four innings out of Karstens, with five innings being a bonus. He'll be followed by various relievers who can give the Pirates multiple innings.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Samardzija's third Major League start. In his last outing, Sept. 23 against Milwaukee, the right-hander took the loss, but pitched well. He gave up three runs on five hits over five innings and appeared to have better command of his pitches. It was a big improvement over his first big league start Aug. 12 against the Phillies, when he lasted 3 1/3 innings. Samardzija will be pitching in Mexico this winter to add a few innings.
away_pitcher_note: If it weren't for some stellar defensive plays made behind him on Saturday, Maholm's last start likely would have turned out much worse than it did. As it was, the lefty battled again without his bread-and-butter sinker and allowed three runs on seven hits and three walks. Maholm lost his chance at going for a 10-win season when the Pirates bullpen blew a save in the start, though he can salvage a .500 record with a win in this, his final start of the year. Maholm is 4-1 but with a 7.06 ERA in nine starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny picked up the win in his last outing against the Giants, giving up one run on five hits and three walks over five innings. He struck out five. The lefty has a good chance at making the Cubs' 2010 rotation, and he's done nothing to give the team reason to think they need to add another pitcher this offseason.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner experienced his first Major League victory in more than three months in his last start, against the San Diego Padres on Sunday. He pitched seven innings, giving up four runs on three hits. He walked two and struck out seven. Buckner has pitched better over his past few outings, going at least six innings in four of his past five starts and lowering his ERA by 2.04 over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is harder on himself than anyone else. He was mad after his last start because the Giants took a quick 2-0 lead in the first two innings. The right-hander gave up five runs on a season-high 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings. Lou Piniella says the right-hander has a spot in the 2010 rotation and everything else he does this year is a bonus. Wells wants to finish strong. He's got a chance to finish with the most wins by a Cubs rookie since Kerry Wood won 13 in 1998.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera remains the likely starter for Saturday, although there is a chance Yusmeiro Petit has a chance to start depending on how things worked out in the bullpen in San Francisco. Cabrera was a starter with the Baltimore Orioles and Washington Nationals, who released him on June 5. He's worked five scoreless innings over his past three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster needs five innings to reach his personal goal of 200. That shouldn't be a problem. The right-hander threw a five-hit shutout in his last start against the Pirates to pick up his 87th career win. He is the second active pitcher with at least 87 wins and 87 saves. John Smoltz is the other one, although he's well ahead of Dempster. The game against the Pirates was Dempster's 10th career shutout. He's been on a roll and is 2-0 with a 0.84 ERA in his last four starts, striking out 22 and walking five over 32 innings. He has not given up an earned run in his last 26 innings at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Davis needs to pitch at least 4 2/3 innings to reach his goal of 200. He'll need to be a little more efficient with his pitches to reach the goal. He threw 103 pitches and lasted just four innings in his last outing, a loss to the Giants. He walked five, hit a batter and allowed seven hits as he fell to 1-4 over his last nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Enright has made three appearances this spring, allowing two hits over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wells struck out five over 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Reds. He's expected to go three or four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe concluded his frustrating first season in Atlanta by posting a 6.65 ERA and allowing opponents to produce a .336 batting average in his final nine starts.  Determined to experience an immediate rebound, he spent the offseason overhauling his delivery and ridding himself of the bad habits that altered his mechanics.  The 36-year-old right-hander, who is now bringing his hands in front of his face during his delivery from the windup, displayed much greater consistency with his command during the Grapefruit League season. While making an Opening Day start for the fourth time in five years, he will be looking to duplicate last year's performance, during which he limited the Phillies to two hits over eight scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's sixth Opening Day assignment. He picked up his first win last year in a 4-2 victory over the Astros. Fergie Jenkins was the last Cubs pitcher to start six Opening Day games. Zambrano is coming off a disappointing season, in which he did not reach double digit wins for the first time since becoming a full-time starter in 2003. Now 28, Zambrano is entering his 10th season with the Cubs. He arrived in spring camp trimmer, having shed 15 pounds, and spent the offseason doing core exercises to avoid any back problems.

home_pitcher_note: With concerns about the right shoulder inflammation he battled during the early days of Spring Training in the past, Jurrjens is looking show why so many believe his future is so bright.  The 3.10 ERA he has compiled during his first two Major League seasons ranks eighth among Major Leaguers who have compiled at least 400 innings during the past two years.  The 2.60 ERA he posted last year ranked third in the National League.  The 24-year-old right-hander allowed two earned runs or fewer in 26 of the 34 starts that he made last year.   He made his only career start against the Cubs last year and allowed four earned runs and seven hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster got off to a slow start last season, going 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA in his first five starts. The right-hander is determined to change that this season. You also won't be seeing him jumping over any fences. Dempster missed time last season after breaking a toe when he tried to clear the dugout fence at Wrigley. The right-hander scuffled on the road, going 4-5 with a 3.38 ERA. He did total 200 innings for the fifth time in his career, which is one of Dempster's goals each year.

home_pitcher_note: Widely regarded as one of the game's top young pitchers, Hanson made his much-anticipated Major League debut in early June and then spent the next four months living up to tremendous expectations. The 23-year-old right-hander surrendered three two-run homers in his Major League debut and then posted a 2.59 ERA in his final 20 starts.  Armed with four plus pitches, including a slider that has been compared to the successful one that John Smoltz displayed, Hanson recoded 91 strikeouts and issued 26 walks in the 86 2/3 innings that he completed after the All-Star break.  This will be his first career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells was the surprise of 2009. The right-hander was called up May 8 and never looked back. He was the first Cubs rookie to reach double-digits in wins since Kerry Wood did so in 1998. Wells' 27 starts were the most by a Cubs rookie since Mike Harkey made 27 in 1990. He led NL rookies in starts and finished second in wins and innings pitched. A converted catcher, Wells is still learning.

home_pitcher_note: The end of the 2009 season was huge for Bailey, as he posted a 6-1 record and 1.70 ERA over his final nine starts in the big leagues. Between Triple-A Louisville and the Reds, Bailey worked 203 innings and struck out 168. Perhaps most importantly, the 23-year-old is pitching with more confidence and is finally comfortable after two years under the white-hot spotlight as everyone anointed him the next big thing. Unlike past camps where he tried and failed to make the club, Bailey was locked in as the No. 4 starter from the beginning and could prepare himself more for the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is eager to redeem himself. After two bad seasons with the Mariners, the right-hander has been encouraged this spring by his outings and by the direction he's gotten. His sinker is back, his shoulder is strong and his mother is in town. Silva's mother has been denied a visa from Venezuela for the last three years but was able to get a 10-year visa and joined him in Arizona. Home cooking helps. He had his best years when she was in the U.S.

home_pitcher_note: During his Opening Day start on Monday -- an 11-6 loss to the Cardinals -- Harang gave up four runs (three earned) over five innings, with two walks, three strikeouts and two home runs. He said he made only two mistakes, which happened to be the home run pitches. In the first inning with two outs and two strikes, Albert Pujols slugged a fastball over the plate for a solo home run to center field. Colby Rasmus hit a solo homer in the top of the fourth to right field. Harang still had good velocity, in the 93-94 mph, which has the Reds optimistic that he is in position to be better than last year.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano struggled in his sixth Opening Day start, lasting just 1 1/3 innings against the Braves. That matched the shortest outing of his career. He gave up eight runs, six hits and two walks -- very unimpressive for the ace of the Cubs staff. Big Z said the problem was location. He fell behind in the count. Zambrano is smart enough and talented enough to correct the mistakes. Last year, he was 1-1 with a 1.98 ERA in two starts against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Leake will be making his Major League debut and will be the first Drafted starting pitcher since Jim Abbott in 1988 to make the leap with no stop in the Minor Leagues. Leake won the fifth starter's job over Aroldis Chapman and lefty prospect Travis Wood during camp by going 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in six spring games, including two starts. He allowed 16 hits, four walks and had 10 strikeouts over 18 innings.  The eighth-overall selection in the 2009 First-Year Player Draft, Leake was 16-1 with a 1.36 ERA in 17 games for Arizona State last season.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny won a spot in the rotation over Sean Marshall, but both pitched well. Lou Piniella wanted to have at least one lefty in the rotation while the team waits for Ted Lilly to return from shoulder surgery. Gorzelanny has been a starter most of his career. Last season with the Cubs, he was 4-2 with a 5.63 ERA in 13 games (seven starts). The Evergreen Park, Ill., native has a 3-2 record and 6.00 ERA in six career games vs. the Reds. Last year, the lefty did much better on the road, posting a 5-2 record and 4.22 ERA away from home.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster gets the call to start the home opener. The right-hander should have a win after pitching six solid innings against the Braves on Wednesday. He struck out nine and gave up one run on three hits. But a high pitch count -- he threw 95 in six innings -- forced his exit. Last year, Dempster was 7-4 with a 3.97 ERA in 14 home starts compared to 4-5 with a 3.38 ERA in 17 road games. He faced the Brewers four times in '09 and had the upper hand, posting a 3-1 record and 3.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davis endured an awful first inning against the Rockies on Wednesday, throwing half of his 40 pitches out of the strike zone, including two in the dirt that eluded catcher George Kottaras. But he limited the damage to three runs and then settled in nicely, throwing 29 of his final 48 pitches for strikes while the Brewers rallied for a 5-4 win. Davis happily settled for a no-decision, and so did his manager. "He got out there into the fifth [inning] and it wasn't completely ugly," Ken Macha said. "It could have been a blowout there in the first inning." Davis is 9-6 with a 3.20 ERA in 16 career starts against the Cubs including 3-2 with a 1.93 ERA in six starts at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Wells didn't get his first win last year until his eighth start. This season, the sophomore picked up his first "W" and the team's first win in his first start. Wells threw six scoreless innings against the Braves, giving up six hits and striking out one. He was helped by three double plays. If he keeps the ball on the ground, he'll do fine. Against the Brewers last year, Wells was 1-1 in three starts with a 3.60 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A rare blown save by Trevor Hoffman cost Bush a win in his season debut, but the good news for Bush and the Brewers is that the right-hander appears back on track after a 2009 season marred by injury. He worked 5 2/3 innings against the Cardinals and was a strike away from getting through the sixth inning with only one run on the board when Matt Holliday connected for a two-run homer. It would prove Bush's final pitch, but he was looking at the bright side. "It's been about 10 months since I've been out on the mound and felt like I didn't have anything to hold back on," said Bush, who wasn't the same last season after a Hanley Ramirez line drive struck him near the elbow. He's just 2-8 with a 5.13 ERA in 16 career appearances against the Cubs, 15 of them starts.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano redeemed himself after a disastrous Opening Day start. The right-hander struck out nine over seven innings against the Reds on Saturday for his first win. It was a much improved outing after lasting just 1 1/3 innings back on the season opener. This will be Big Z's first start at home, where he was 2-5 with a 5.03 ERA last season compared to 7-2 with a 2.73 ERA on the road. In his career, Zambrano is 46-39 at Wrigley compared to 59-30 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan gets the nod as the Brewers' fifth starter over left-handers Chris Narveson and Manny Parra despite a decidedly subpar spring in which he allowed 14 runs and 21 hits in 16 1/3 innings while dealing with a neck injury. That ailment -- cervical disc pain -- landed Suppan on the 15-day disabled list to start the year but he made a rehab start at Class A Wisconsin on Friday and appears set to debut against the Cubs. Suppan has a very respectable 3.63 ERA in 23 career starts against Chicago, including a 3.77 ERA in 12 starts at Wrigley Field. He's in the final season of a four-year contract.

home_pitcher_note: Silva came out of his last start April 9 after throwing 71 pitches over six innings because of some discomfort in his right shoulder. He was limited last season because of shoulder problems, so the Cubs are giving him plenty of rest. The plan is to keep Carlos Zambrano, Ryan Dempster and Randy Wells on a five-day routine and insert Silva and Tom Gorzelanny when there are openings. Silva looked solid in his Cubs debut against the Reds, giving up one run on three hits and striking out three. This will be his first start ever at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old right-hander, who went 3-11 with a 6.27 ERA a year ago, got roughed up by the Phillies in his first start of the season when he allowed four runs (all earned) on four hits over five innings. He struck out four and walked four before leaving the game with his team leading 5-4.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny did not get a win in his first start of the season on April 11 against the Reds. In that game, he gave up one run on four hits over 6 1/3 innings and struck out seven. It was a solid performance, but the Cubs lost the game, as the Reds rallied for two runs in the eighth. He will have to watch out for Carlos Lee, who loves to hit at Wrigley Field and has a .429 average against the Cubs lefty. The Cubs tweaked the rotation and gave Ryan Dempster an extra day, moving him to Sunday after the right-hander threw 114 pitches in his second start.
away_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander has deserved better in his first two starts, but the Astros struggled to get much offense going in those two games against Tim Lincecum of the Giants and Roy Halladay of the Phillies. Against San Francisco, Oswalt allowed three earned runs on seven hits over six innings. Against Philly, he allowed two earned runs on five hits in six innings, while striking out eight and walking two in a 2-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off his first win but not his best-pitched start of the young season. In his first outing, on April 7 against the Braves, he gave up one run on three hits over six innings but didn't get a decision. On Monday, in the home opener against the Brewers, he gave up five runs on seven hits and four walks over 6 1/3 innings and got the win. He admitted that he wasn't as aggressive as he would like. Dempster did throw 114 pitches, which is why the Cubs gave him an extra day and pushed him back to Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw, who went 14-12 with a 3.02 ERA a year ago, has gotten mixed results in his first two outings of the season. Against the Giants, Rodriguez allowed three earned runs on seven hits in six innings. On Monday against the Cardinals, he was tagged for four earned runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings -- with St. Louis slugger Albert Pujols accounting for all four runs with an RBI single and then a three-run home run.

home_pitcher_note: Though some defensive blunders undermined Niese last Wednesday in Denver, nothing hurt more than Ryan Spilborgh's three-run homer to the deepest part of Coors Field. Niese allowed nine hits and one walk in total, striking out two. But the Mets could not do nearly enough offensively to turn those numbers into a win. Niese will now open the Mets homestand against the Cubs, the team that handed him the first loss of his Major League career in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Wells did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers. In that game, he gave up four runs on 10 hits over 6 1/3 innings while striking out seven. The one mulligan Wells would like to have is a walk he issued to pitcher Dave Bush in the fifth. Bush scored that inning on Rickie Weeks' two-run double, which gave the Brewers the lead. He last faced the Mets on Sept. 6 in New York, and took the loss, despite giving up one earned run on seven hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Featuring a sharp split-fingered fastball, along with good control of his slider and curve, Mike Pelfrey blanked a potent Rockies offense for seven innings on Thursday in Denver. Continuing to grow more confident in his secondary pitches, Pelfrey is no longer relying solely on his power sinker to generate outs. That much should serve him well against the Cubs, who mustered only one run in eight innings in their lone meeting with Pelfrey last season.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano had to leave his last start because of cramps in his right hand and right calf, and also because he threw 121 pitches over five innings. The Brewers were aggressive and fouled a lot of pitches off, which was part of the reason for the high pitch count. Big Z hasn't thrown that many pitches since he totaled 125 on July 24, 2008. That year, he topped 100 pitches in 18 of his starts, including a 130-pitch game May 28 against the Dodgers. He was 0-1 in two starts against the Mets last season.

home_pitcher_note: Uncharacteristically throwing his offspeed pitches for strikes, Perez flashed a sharp slider and some stellar control on Friday in St. Louis. That not only helped him negate his dip in fastball velocity, but also allowed him to submit one of his finest efforts of the past two seasons. Whether Perez can sustain his low-velocity success remains to be seen. But if he can continue to feature the type of control he had against the Cardinals, Perez should, at the very least, be serviceable. His next test will come against the Dodgers, who walked seven times but could not beat him last July at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is coming off his second straight stellar start to kick off the season, having allowed five hits while striking out five and walking none in seven solid innings during a 7-2 win over the Astros in his first Cubs start at Wrigley Field. Silva last pitched against the Mets on June 18, 2007, when he gave up 10 hits and four runs in six innings in a losing effort as a member of the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Santana defeated the Cubs in his only start against them as a member of the Mets, at Shea Stadium on Sept. 28, 2008. He allowed two runs in eight innings. His career record against them, including four starts with the Twins, is 2-0. Alfonso Soriano is the only Cubs player with more than six career at-bats against Santana, and he is hitless in 10. Santana has produced a 9-4 record and 2.68 ERA in 16 starts at Citi Field. His best performance in three starts this season came Saturday in St. Louis in the 20-inning game. He threw seven scoreless innings, allowing four hits and a walk and striking out nine.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny took the loss in his second start of the season, against the Astros on Saturday. The left-hander gave up two runs on three hits in three innings, but he left the game for precautionary reasons after getting hit by line drive on his throwing shoulder. Gorzelanny last stared against the Mets on April 30, 2008, and got the win, pitching five shutout, one-hit innings for the Pirates. It may be Gorzelanny's final chance to prove he deserves to stay in the starting rotation with Ted Lilly scheduled to come off the 15-day disabled list and rejoin the starting staff.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers bumped Suppan's start a few days in order to split their two left-handers in the rotation, and the result is that the veteran right-hander will make his second start of the season after seven days' rest. Suppan started the year on the disabled list with a neck injury and was only so-so against the Cubs on a wind-blown afternoon at Wrigley Field on April 15, allowing four runs on six hits in five innings. Suppan surrendered home runs to Derrek Lee and Marlon Byrd that probably would have cleared the fence even without a stiff breeze blowing straight out, and he'll have to keep the Cubs in the ballpark to have success in the rematch. Suppan was 3-8 with a 6.39 ERA at Miller Park last year.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster should be 3-0. In his two starts in which he did not get a decision, he has given up two earned runs over 13 2/3 innings. In his lone win, which was against Milwaukee, he wasn't as sharp, serving up five runs over 6 1/3 innings. The good news about his last outing against the Astros on Sunday was he bounced back fine after throwing 114 pitches vs. the Brewers on April 12. Ryan Braun homered off Dempster in the last meeting at Wrigley Field and is 6-for-26 lifetime off the right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers aren't about to bail on Davis after three starts, but it's time for the left-hander to start pitching to his track record. Davis has been steady as she goes since resurrecting his career in Milwaukee in 2003, but his first three starts of the reunion tour have been forgettable. He has yet to pitch past the fifth inning and couldn't hold a 10-0, first-inning lead in Washington on Sunday. Davis was lifted with two outs in the fifth inning and the Brewers had to hold off a Nationals charge for an 11-7 win. Davis will continue to get the ball "for right now," manager Ken Macha said on Tuesday, hardly a ringing endorsement.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly returns to the Cubs rotation after passing all the tests in his rehab. He's coming back from arthroscopic surgery on his left shoulder. He made his last Minor League start Monday in Peoria. In that game, Lilly threw threw 88 pitches over seven innings and picked up the win. He struck out nine and gave up one run on three hits and one walk. Of his total pitches, 63 were strikes. The lefty also singled and was thrown out trying to steal. The shoulder actually has been the least of his problems as he was slowed this spring by the flu and then early in April by back problems.

home_pitcher_note: Bush delivered seven shutout innings against the Pirates on Tuesday just when the team needed a quality outing. He allowed only three hits -- two of them to Andrew McCutchen and the other an infield single to pinch-hitter John Raynor, who was promptly erased on a double play. Bush notched his first win of the season but could easily be 3-0; he exited with the lead on April 9 against the Cardinals and April 14 against the Cubs, only to see the game slip away each time by a reliever.
away_pitcher_note: This would've been Carlos Zambrano's turn in the rotation but he's now in the bullpen. Wells stays on schedule. In his last start Monday against the Mets, Wells gave up one run on six hits over six innings but did not get the win as the bullpen imploded. He faced the Brewers on April 14 at Wrigley Field and struck out the side to start the game, then got into trouble in the fifth. He finished giving up 10 hits, four runs, and striking out seven over 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Silva has been stellar so far. The right-hander has given up two earned runs over 19 innings for a 0.95 ERA, and opponents are batting just .152 against him. He also was efficient in his last start, throwing 87 pitches over six innings. If there's been one problem it's hitting. Silva has spent the last six seasons in the American League and he injured his right wrist in his first at-bat of his last start Wednesday against the Mets. He says he'll be fine to face the Nationals, but don't expect him swinging too much.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan kept the Nationals in the game in his last start on Wednesday. However, he continued to have problems against left-handed hitters, who went 7-for-9 against him. Carlos Gonzalez had four of the hits, while Brad Hawpe had two and Jason Giambi collected a knock. Lannan threw 107 pitches. Asked why he has been having a tough time getting left-handers out, Lannan said his off-speed pitches are not working. If the pitches are not working, the left-handed hitters are not going to have problems getting on base.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny deserved better in his last start. Against the Mets, the lefty did not give up a hit until there was one out in the fifth. He retired the first 10 batters and should've been able to go deeper, but an error in the sixth led to two runs and that was it. For the game, Gorzelanny struck out seven. He has made only one start at Wrigley this year and that was April 17 against the Astros, when he was hit on the left arm by a line drive and knocked out after three innings.
away_pitcher_note: It was the long ball that did in Hernandez against the Rockies on Thursday. He gave up a homer to Miguel Olivo in the second inning and another to Ian Stewart five innings later. Hernandez lasted eight innings and gave up the two runs on five hits. Rockies manager Jim Tracy was impressed with Hernandez's performance. To Tracy, it looked as if Hernandez and catcher Ivan Rodriguez were playing catch in the backyard.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off a win over the Brewers in which he held Milwaukee to one run on seven hits over 7 2/3 innings. The right-hander did not face the Nationals last year, but does know Adam Dunn very well. Dunn has a .364 lifetime average against Dempster, including one home run. So far, Dempster has posted a better ERA on the road than at home. At Wrigley, he's given up six earned runs over 14 innings; on the road, he's been charged with two over 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Atilano became the 42nd player to make his Major League debut in a Nationals uniform, and it was a great first game for him as the Nats defeated the Dodgers, 5-1, at Nationals Park. Atilano, who was called up from Triple-A Syracuse to replace the injured Jason Marquis, pitched six innings, allowing one run on five hits. After the game ended, Atilano received two pies in the face -- one from John Lannan and a second one from Livan Hernandez. It was worth it, according to Atilano.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was solid in his first start off the disabled list, on Saturday against Milwaukee. The lefty threw six shutout innings, giving up three hits, and picked up the win. However, he was lifted after throwing 78 pitches because his back stiffened. Back problems forced him to delay his rehab starts, so it will be something to watch as the season progresses. This will be Lilly's first game at Wrigley Field this season. He was slowed following arthroscopic surgery on his left shoulder in November.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy and the D-backs were foiled his last time out by Phillies outfielder Jayson Werth. The right-hander allowed two runs over a career-high eight innings. Both of the runs came on homers from Werth and Raul Ibanez. Kennedy left with the game tied at 2, but Werth's solo homer in the ninth off Juan Gutierrez won it for Philly. In his previous start, Kennedy was victimized by a poor outing from the bullpen against the Padres. He worked five scoreless innings, striking out seven while allowing just two hits. He left the game with a 2-0 lead, but Arizona relievers allowed five runs in the seventh inning as the Padres rallied for a 5-3 win. He appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.

home_pitcher_note: Wells may want to move this game to Miller Park. The right-hander held the Brewers to two runs on seven hits in his last start, on Sunday, and has a 1.50 ERA lifetime in Milwaukee. He's shown no signs of a sophomore slump this year. What was impressive on Sunday was that the right-hander did not walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez has pitched well for the most part, but his last outing was not a good one. The right-hander allowed six runs on 10 hits against the Phillies at Chase Field. In his start prior to that he battled hard to get through seven innings and help rest a tired bullpen. He held the Cardinals to two runs on seven hits while walking four and striking out three in that game. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well.
