Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff early last decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.

home_pitcher_note: Silva has produced quality starts in each of his first four outings this season. He took the no-decision in his last start against Washington on April 26, allowing three runs on seven hits over seven innings. Silva has made six career appearances against the D-backs, but just one start, and that came back in 2004 while he was with the Twins, during Interleague play. He took the loss in the July 4 start, giving up four runs on nine hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has pitched well this year, but he has not been the dominant first-half pitcher the D-backs have grown accustomed to. One reason he said is that he is still working to get his fastball control where he wants it. In his last outing against the Rockies at Coors Field he allowed a pair of runs over eight innings and struck out 10. His start prior to that was a strange one. On the mound, the performance was less than stellar as he allowed seven runs on nine hits in just six innings against the Cardinals at Chase Field. At the plate, however, it was a different story. Haren went 4-for-4 and helped lead an offensive explosion that resulted in a 9-7 Arizona victory. Four of the seven runs he allowed came via a pair of homers by Ryan Ludwick and one by Albert Pujols. After allowing three runs in the fourth, Haren was able to retire the Cards in order in the fifth and sixth innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny continues to experience tough luck with the Cubs. He's surrendered two earned runs or fewer in each of his four starts in compiling a 2.45 ERA, but he has a 0-3 record to show for it. Chicago's offense has mustered just seven runs of support in those four games. Gorzelanny is 1-1 in four career starts against Arizona with a 5.09 ERA. He faced the D-backs in his final start of last season on October 2 at Wrigley Field and got hit around pretty good, giving up six earned runs in three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson would just as soon forget his last start. The right-hander was battered by the Rockies in Coors Field as he allowed 10 runs on 11 hits over 2 1/3 innings. It was the most runs he had allowed in his start in his career. Jackson said that regardless of whether he made good pitches or bad ones, whenever the Rockies made contact they seemed to be able to get hits. Jackson was not overly sharp in his start prior to that when he allowed three first-inning runs against the Cardinals at Chase Field. He was able to get through eight innings in that game however. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.

home_pitcher_note: The common theme throughout Maholm's five starts this year has been the left-hander's ability to battle. He has yet to give the Pirates a dominant start, though neither has Maholm struggled enough to keep the team out of striking distance. In a season where Pittsburgh starters have struggled immensely, Maholm's ability to go at least six innings in all but one of his starts has been huge. Maholm has been the Pirates' most consistent starter since the start of 2008. Though Maholm is 4-1 in nine career appearances against the Cubs, Maholm's ERA versus Chicago is 7.06.
away_pitcher_note: It may be better for Dempster to be on the road. So far, the right-hander is 1-0 with a 1.32 ERA in two road starts compared to 1-1 with a 3.68 ERA in three games at Wrigley Field. In his last outing at home against the Nationals, Dempster took the loss as he served up three runs on four hits over eight innings. Two of those hits were home runs. Last year against the Pirates, he was 2-0 with a 4.66 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton's last outing was certainly a step in the right direction, though the right-hander remains winless in five starts this season. He allowed six runs (three earned) in six innings last Friday in what was just his second start to go past the four-inning mark this year. Morton has to start keeping balls in the park -- he has allowed seven homers in 19 innings -- and he has to continue to stay aggressive and trust his abilities if Morton is going to turn things around. His numbers obviously haven't been good, but the Pirates don't have the starting pitching depth to replace him in the rotation. Morton is 1-2 with a 10.22 ERA in three career starts against the Cubs. That ERA is bloated, however, by the one-inning start last August in which he gave up 10 earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: In Lilly's last start, some of the D-backs players said it seemed as if the lefty's velocity was down. It was only his second start since coming off the disabled list and Lou Piniella said he expects the velocity to improve as Lilly builds up arm strength. In that last start, Lilly gave up six runs on seven hits over five innings. He didn't look as sharp as he did in his season debut on April 24 against the Brewers, when Lilly threw six scoreless innings. Last year, Lilly was 1-2 with a 3.60 ERA in three starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the last time the Pirates need to find someone to fill Ross Ohlendorf's spot in the rotation, and left-hander Brian Burres gets the call. Burres stepped into Ohlendorf's vacant rotation spot last Thursday and provided the Pirates with 5 1/3 scoreless innings. Burres wasn't dominant in the outing, but he made quality pitches when he needed to. In his previous start, Burres was knocked around for six earned runs in just four innings.  Burres' only previous appearance against the Cubs came in relief. In that outing, the left-hander allowed one run on three hits in an inning of work.
away_pitcher_note: Wells is coming off a win over the D-backs in which the right-hander gave up five runs on eight hits over six-plus innings. He has not walked a batter in his last two starts, both wins, while striking out 14 in that stretch. In his last start, Wells said he was forced to make some pitches he didn't want to because of the wind at Wrigley. It was blowing out at 18 mph during the game. "I made some mistakes and they made me pay," said Wells, who served up one home run. So far, he's posted better numbers away from Wrigley, compiling a 1.42 ERA in three road starts compared to a 6.57 ERA in two games at home.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey threw a career-high 121 pitches during a no-decision in a 6-3 loss to the Cardinals on Saturday. He pitched 6 2/3 innings with three runs (two earned) allowed on seven hits. He walked three and struck out six. His final batter was Albert Pujols and with a runner on second base and first base open, he was given the chance to pitch to him. Bailey missed his spot and Pujols  lined a 3-2 split-fingered fastball for an RBI double to left field that gave St. Louis a 2-1 lead.
away_pitcher_note: Silva was to get an extra day of rest between starts because the Cubs had considered giving him a cortisone shot in his right wrist. He's been bothered by a sore wrist injured during an at-bat in New York on April 21. But the Cubs decided he didn't need the shot, so he's staying on track. In his last start against the D-backs, he gave up five runs on eight hits over five innings, his shortest outing of the season. But he said the wrist wasn't a problem. Silva did strike out six but also served up three homers.

home_pitcher_note: Showing positive signs that he is still willing to be aggressive with his fastball and work ahead, Harang gave the Reds his second straight quality start on Sunday at St. Louis but still took the loss in a 6-0 game. Over six innings, Harang allowed three earned runs and seven hits -- he did not walk a batter and struck out six.  The nice outing was trumped by a superlative one by Chris Carpenter, who worked seven scoreless innings while giving up only two hits. "I feel like I've made some definite strides," Harang said. "I've been more aggressive with the fastball, moving the ball in and out and around the zone the way I want to."
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny finally picked up a win in his last outing against the D-backs. The lefty set a career high with 10 strikeouts, topping his old mark of nine, which he had done twice, including Sept. 21, 2009, at Milwaukee. The difference, Gorzelanny said, was his ability to control the fastball. In previous outings, when he tried to elevate it, he felt as if he was throwing over the screen. This time, he put it exactly where he wanted. He's posted three quality starts in his five games so far.

home_pitcher_note: Leake gave the Reds his fourth quality start in five big league games but did not get into the seventh inning for the first time. In a 3-2 Reds win over the Mets in 11 innings, Leake was solid with six well-pitched innings. Just one of his two runs allowed were earned, while he walked one and struck out four. He was at 100 pitches when lifted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the sixth.
away_pitcher_note:
Dempster took the loss in his last start against the Pirates, giving up three runs on eight 
hits over seven innings. The right-hander struck out seven, and now has 1,405 career Ks. 
Among the eight hits were two home runs, but the biggest problem was a lack of run support, as 
the Cubs stranded 11 in the loss. Maybe pitching in Cincinnati, where he once played, will help get him back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a win in his last start against the Pirates. The lefty gave up four runs on nine hits over six innings, including three doubles in a row. Very un-Lilly like, Lou Piniella said. Lilly is still building up arm strength after undergoing surgery last November, so he's still in Spring Training mode. The last start was only his third of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson once again cruised along early, then struggled a bit late in a loss to the Giants on Wednesday. The 32-year-old gave up two earned runs on six hits and one walk in 5 1/3 innings, but he cruised through the first five frames. Robertson allowed one run and needed only 52 pitches to get through the first five innings. In the sixth, however, he let the first five hitters reach base -- one on a dropped fly ball by Brett Carroll -- and gave up two runs to eventually suffer his third consecutive loss. Said Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez about Robertson's recent late-outing struggles: "We're going to sit down and put our heads together -- all three of us [along with pitching coach Randy St. Claire] -- and see what we can come up with, because that's not a guy that does that."

home_pitcher_note: Wells had his shortest outing as a starter in his last game against the Pirates and was mad at himself after the game about it, saying it was "terrible" and "unacceptable." Lou Piniella told him even Cy Young lost a few games. Wells lasted two innings, giving up seven runs, six earned, on five hits and three walks. He walked the first two batters he faced in the game and they were two of the five runs to score that inning. Wells had posted quality starts in three of his five previous starts, so the abbreviated outing was unexpected.
away_pitcher_note: Battling the rain, Nolasco left some balls out over the middle of the plate against the Giants on Thursday, but he still turned in a quality start, giving up three runs on five hits while striking out three and walking none in six innings. He has now turned in three quality starts in his six outings. But because the Marlins failed to score a run in the first five innings for the third consecutive game, Nolasco came away with the loss. It wasn't a great start, but it was an improvement over the 27-year-old's previous outing -- when he gave up five runs in a season-low four innings to the Nats. "He hasn't really been the Ricky we've seen, but today, three runs against a tough opponent ... and he gave us an opportunity to win the game," Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez said Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Silva picked up the win in his last start against the Reds, but it was a battle. The right-hander said he had some soreness in his neck and right shoulder -- nothing major, he said -- but it was uncomfortable. Part of the problem was a long fifth inning in which he faced eight batters and gave up four runs. Silva served up 10 hits over five innings and walked one. The good news is that his right wrist seems to be fine after he tweaked it during an at-bat in New York.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old will be making his seventh start, and for the first time since April 25, it won't be against the Nationals. Perhaps that isn't a good thing for Volstad. In his last two starts, he's faced and beat the Nationals, giving up three runs in 18 innings with 12 strikeouts. Volstad has made four career starts with no decisions against the Cubs. He has a 2.81 ERA vs. them.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny took the loss in his last start against the Reds, giving up three runs on nine hits over six innings. The final score was 14-2, as the Reds took advantage of two Cubs errors. Gorzelanny now has four quality starts and one win to show for it. He'll be facing his former team for the third time in his career. So far, the lefty is 1-1 with a 1.69 ERA against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Burres' last start earned him the opportunity to make another. The Pirates had to open up a spot in the rotation for Ross Ohlendorf, but Burres turned out to not be the one to give up that spot. The left-hander has pitched 12 1/3 combined scoreless innings in his last two starts - both Pirates wins -- after stepping into the rotation as a spot starter. Burres will continue to have to prove that he deserves to keep the rotation spot, though one bad start won't necessarily mean he's gone. Burres' last start -- which spanned seven scoreless innings -- came against the Cubs, who he is now slated to face again.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster was vying for his fifth straight quality start in his last outing against the Reds. He'd thrown 111 pitches over 6 1/3 innings and had a one-run lead. But Joey Votto hit his 112th pitch for a three-run homer and Dempster took the loss. He struck out seven over seven innings. Dempster faced the Pirates May 4 in Pittsburgh and lost, but didn't get much run support.
away_pitcher_note: The Maholm that showed up on Sunday was certainly not the Maholm that the Pirates are accustomed to seeing. In what was his shortest start since September 2007, Maholm was chased after just 3 1/3 innings. He had problems locating his sinker down, and those were only further exacerbated by a 54-pitch fourth inning. Maholm, who started off the afternoon with two clean innings, never found his command again. Still, the Pirates have no reason not to expect Maholm to bounce back. He had gone at least six innings in six of his other seven starts this year and has been as consistent a starter as the club has had these last few seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was cruising through the first five innings of his last start against the Marlins and did not give up a hit until Chris Coghlan doubled with one out in the sixth. There's one other pitch Lilly would like to have back and that was the first one to Ronny Paulino with a man on and one out in the seventh. Paulino homered to help lead Florida to a 4-2 win. Lilly struck out one in seven innings and looked better than he did in his two previous outings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf threw four innings in his return off the disabled list last Monday in what was viewed as a very successful return. After missing just over a month of action, Ohlendorf allowed one earned run on three hits and four walks in the outing. He did need 84 pitches to get that deep in the game, but part of that can be attributed to rustiness. Too, the game wasn't so much about results as it was Ohlendorf's ability to get through an outing healthy. The Pirates are hopeful that his return will better stabilize the rotation, and he shouldn't be on any sort of a pitch count in this next start.

home_pitcher_note: Wells showed he's a quick learner. On May 6 against the Pirates, he gave up seven runs over two innings. In his last start Tuesday against the Marlins, Wells notched his fourth quality start, going eight innings. He joked that he was happy to get an at-bat. He's made only one start against the Rockies and lost. He's also fared better on the road, compiling a 3.86 ERA compared to 5.31 at home.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has not pitched with the expected consistency through his first seven starts, but he is coming off a positive effort. Cook held the Phillies to three runs in six innings and kept the Rockies close in a matchup with Phils ace Roy Halladay. The Rockies won in extra innings. Although Cook has been able to fight his way through rough times with a four-seam fastball and a breaking pitch, he needs to get on a good streak with his sinker.

home_pitcher_note: Silva is on a roll. The right-hander notched his fifth quality start in his last outing against the Marlins. The last time he began a season this well was 2004 when he opened 5-0 with the Twins. The Cubs are 6-1 when Silva starts. The key? "He throws a lot of strikes," catcher Geovany Soto said.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching scoreless ball for his first 15 1/3 innings this season, Chacin gave up six runs in five innings against the Nationals on Thursday night. Five of the runs came on two Ryan Zimmerman home runs, and each of those came on poorly located sliders. In the fifth, he couldn't put the inning away with two outs. It was not the best day for Chacin, but for the most part he stayed in the strike zone and didn't become flustered when things went wrong.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer allowed four earned runs in 6 1/3 innings in a victory Friday over Milwaukee at Miller Park. Moyer has pitched fairly well this season. He has kept the Phillies in almost every game he has pitched, which accounts for his 5-2 record after seven starts. Moyer allowed three homers to the Brewers, giving him 501 homers allowed in his career. That is second in baseball history. Only Robin Roberts has allowed more with 505, but that is a mark based on longevity more than anything.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe being on the road will get Gorzelanny on track. The lefty has not won away from Wrigley Field yet but has a 2.50 ERA in his three starts. At home, he's 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA. In his last outing, which was at home, the lefty did not get a decision, giving up a season-high five runs on nine hits over five innings. He did strike out seven. Gorzelanny has made one start in his career against the Phillies and lost.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton looks at his 5.49 ERA and wonders how he got there. He actually has pitched better than his ERA has indicated. In Saturday's victory over Milwaukee at Miller Park, Blanton allowed five runs in seven innings. But he had allowed just two until Corey Hart hit a three-run home run with two outs in the seventh. If Blanton hadn't allowed that homer, he would be entering Thursday's start against the Cubs with a much improved 4.11 ERA. That said, he can't change that and hopes to have everything working Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster got off to a rough start in the first inning of his last game, against the Pirates. He threw 30-plus pitches in the first and ended up with the loss, giving up three runs on four hits over seven innings. It was the right-hander's fourth straight loss. However, three of those losses have been quality starts. So far this month, Dempster is 0-3 with a 4.71 ERA. He's 4-4 with a 4.99 ERA in his career against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis went 3-0 with a 3.80 ERA in his first four starts but is 0-2 with a 3.58 ERA in his past four starts. He lost, 5-2, against the Blue Jays on Sunday, allowing five runs in 5 2/3 innings. He gave up three hits and walked four. He has walked 21 batters in 51 innings. He walked 19 in 176 innings in Japan last year. Opponents are hitting .132 off him with runners in scoring position. Lewis has never faced the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a win in his last game, which was his 100th start for the Cubs, but he did notch another quality start. The lefty gave up three runs on six hits over seven innings against the Pirates. He's now gone at least seven innings in back to back starts for the first time since last Sept. 18-30. He's made 12 starts against the Rangers in his career and is 4-4 with a 3.63 ERA. The last time was June 21, 2007, when he did not get a decision in a 6-5 loss in Texas. In that game, Lilly gave up five runs on six hits, including two homers, over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Holland went 5 1/3 innings, giving up just three runs on five hits with two walks and three strikeouts in a 4-3 victory over the Angels on Monday. Since being recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City, Holland has won both of his starts. He didn't give up a run until the fifth inning against the Halos, running his season-opening scoreless innings streak to 10. He pitched six innings and struck out seven in his first start of the season, a 10-1 victory over Oakland. This will be his first career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells did not get a decision in his last start but should've gotten a "W." He gave up one run on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings against the Rockies. It was his fifth quality start. He now has given up one or no runs in three of his eight games. He did throw 116 pitches, which was a career high. It'll be interesting to see if that has an effect on him. Wells is 2-0 with a 2.75 ERA in three starts against the NL West. This will be his first start against an AL West team.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson pitched just 4 1/3 innings against the Angels on Tuesday, giving up seven runs on seven hits with five strikeouts. In his shortest outing of the season, Wilson saw his homerless innings streak stop at 87 2/3 as Torii Hunter's two-run home run to left field was the first he had given up since July 9, 2009, to Franklin Gutierrez of Seattle. Despite that, the Rangers still won for the sixth straight game started by Wilson. This will be Wilson's first career start against the Cubs. He's 0-0 with a 0.00 ERA and three strikeouts against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is the first Cubs pitcher to start 5-0 since Greg Maddux did so in 2006. This is the third time he's opened 5-0 (he also did so in 2004 with the Twins and 2002 with the Phillies, although the latter was as a reliever). He's never gone 6-0. The right-hander gives his family credit for their positive support. His wife, Maria, makes sure to text him before every game. But he's also benefited by pitching at Wrigley Field with the wind blowing in. That won't be the case in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster has lost four straight decisions, and did not get a decision in his previous start, against the Phillies. He's been roughed up this month, going 0-3 with a 5.00 ERA after compiling a 2.78 ERA over five April starts. He's 6-3 in his career against the Dodgers, including two wins last year.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw could have put himself into Pitcher of the Month consideration if it weren't for his first start in May, a 1 1/3-inning, seven-run disaster. Everything since then has been gold. He's allowed just two runs in 22 1/3 innings and struck out 23 in three starts, all wins. The key for Kershaw has been controlling his emotions early in the game. Opponents still have a .353 batting average against him through his first 15 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny had to leave his last start against the Phillies after getting hit on the left hand with a pitch. X-rays were negative and he was not expected to miss a turn. The Cubs do have an off-day Monday, which gives the lefty one extra day of rest. Against the Phillies, he threw 6 2/3 shutout innings, giving up three hits and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley, along with Clayton Kershaw, has given the Dodgers a one-two punch in their dominant May as the team has soared up the standings. Billingsley has gone at least seven innings in his last two starts, and he's allowed just one run and eight hits combined in that span. He has wins in his last three starts, and he's maintaining a strikeout-to-walk ratio better than two-to-one (44 strikeouts and 21 walks). Billingsley was an All-Star and incredibly consistent in the first half of last season, and the change he's made that seems to have him back on that path is a focus away from sinking his fastball. He said he was trying to be something he's not, and has gotten back to his bread-and-butter: his four-seamer and his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous start, against the Rangers on Friday night, Lilly pitched 6 2/3 innings while giving up two runs on six hits with four strikeouts in a 2-1 loss. In five career starts and one relief appearance against the Dodgers, Lilly is 3-1 with a 3.94 ERA. In three starts at home this season, he is 0-2 with a 5.68 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ely has been "found money" for the Dodgers in manager Joe Torre's eyes, and it's hard to argue. The rookie right-hander was called up at the end of April because the Dodgers were desperate for pitching, and all Ely's done is throw strikes. He went 89 batters without issuing a walk until the first inning of his last start, against the Tigers. That was his only walk in his last four starts. He went six innings, allowed two runs on eight hits and notched his third straight win. All five of Ely's starts have been six innings or longer. His velocity sits in the high-80s, but he's striking out batters too: 28 in 31 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note:
Wells did not get a decision in his last start against the Rangers but had a stellar outing. 
He gave up three runs on seven hits and went 8 1/3 innings, his longest outing of the year. 
Wells also struck out six. He's learning -- he was able to work quickly, get ahead of 
batters and the only mistakes were two pitches, which Vladimir Guerrero and Nelson Cruz both 
launched out of the Ballpark at Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter was let off the hook in his last start after allowing five runs, four earned, on eight hits over six innings against Anaheim. The team rallied for an extra-inning victory on a walk-off hit by Felipe Lopez, thus removing Carpenter from the decision. Two home runs spoiled Carpenter's outing, although he said afterward that his command felt good. He walked two and struck out four and has surrendered nine home runs so far this season after giving up only seven all of last year.

home_pitcher_note:
Silva is off to his best start ever at 6-0. He picked up his last win over the Rangers, 
giving up three runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. It was a short start, primarily because 
of the heat and humidity. The more Silva wins, the more confident he gets. He's already 
picked up more "W's" in his first nine starts than he did in 34 starts the last two years 
with Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: This is the spot that Kyle Lohse would normally occupy, but Lohse was placed on the 15-day disabled list on Thursday and will undergo forearm surgery on Friday in Los Angeles.  No timetable has been set for his return. Right-hander Adam Ottavino will be called up to make the start in Chicago. Ottavino last pitched on Monday for the Redbirds and picked up the victory after allowing one run over five innings. In eight starts with Memphis this season, Ottavino has gone 4-3 with a 4.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster will close the Cubs' six-game homestand and hopes to end the way he started it. Last Tuesday, he threw eight shutout innings and snapped a personal four-game losing streak in the Cubs' 3-0 win over the Dodgers. Dempster was able to avoid the one bad inning that has snuck up on him this season. Last year, he was 0-1 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts against the Cardinals. He's 6-6 with a 4.35 ERA in his career against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals will be looking for a little justice for Wainwright, who was a very hard-luck loser his last time out. Three times this season, Wainwright has allowed one or two runs in a start and the Cardinals have lost. He hasn't always pitched well at Wrigley, but he also hasn't made many starts there. There's no reason to think he can't succeed just as much at the Friendly Confines as he has everywhere else.

home_pitcher_note: Since Ohlendorf has been back from the disabled list at the beginning of May, he's had mixed results. He's coming off a solid performance Wednesday vs. Cincinnati when he allowed three runs on eight hits in six innings but took the loss, and against Chicago on May 16, he pitched six innings and gave up four hits and two runs. But he's also had a couple of rough outings as well. Ohlendorf hasn't won a decision this calendar year (0-3 in the regular season and 0-3 in Spring Training), so he'll look for a change of pace vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note:
Wells threw 16 pitches to six batters in the first inning of his last start on Friday against 
the Cardinals and was pulled before he retired anyone. All six Redbirds got hits. It was an 
"embarrassing" outing, Wells said. He was assigned to the bullpen on Saturday as a backup. So far, he's 1-2 with a 6.00 ERA at home and 2-1 with a 3.68 ERA on the road. He faced the 
Pirates on May 6, and was roughed up, giving up seven runs (six earned) on five hits in two 
innings. Pittsburgh scored five runs in the first.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens, who has made six appearances in long relief this year, will be making just his fourth start of the season after Charlie Morton was placed on the 15-day disabled list Friday with right shoulder fatigue. The right-hander's last start came in Milwaukee on April 27, when he gave up two earned runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings while striking out four and walking four. He recorded a no-decision in the Pirates' 7-3 win. Karstens has made four career appearances against the Cubs, starting three times and going 2-1 with a 5.06 ERA. He has given up nine earned runs off 19 hits in those four games while striking out eight and walking six.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly threw seven shutout innings in his last start against the Dodgers, giving up three hits and striking out five. But he did not get a decision as the lefty exited when the game was tied. The Dodgers felt Lilly tried to get an edge by positioning himself in front of the rubber a little bit and even asked the first-base umpire about it. But no fine was levied and there was no penalty. Expect the umpires -- and the Pirates -- to watch Lilly's footwork very closely in this game.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has lost five of his past six decisions after winning his first two, with the Pirates giving him little run support. He allowed just one earned run in his previous two starts, getting a win and a no-decision, before allowing 12 hits and seven runs over 5 1/3 innings in a loss Friday in Atlanta. Although Duke is 1-2 at home, he has a 3.57 ERA in his six starts at PNC Park this year, and he is the all-time wins leader there with a 27-26 record. Duke will be facing the Cubs for the first time this season. He has allowed 85 hits in 63 2/3 innings, including seven homers, while striking out 40 and walking 23.
away_pitcher_note:
This will be Zambrano's first start since April 20. The right-hander moved to the bullpen to 
make room in the rotation for Ted Lilly and also to give the team a potent setup pitcher. He was effective until May 14 against the Pirates, when he gave up three runs on four hits over one inning. Zambrano then said he wasn't comfortable in the role and wanted to go back to the rotation. Since that game against the Pirates, he has given up one hit over 4 1/3 scoreless innings. Big Z tuned up with a 73-pitch simulated game last Monday. In four starts, Zambrano was 1-2 with a 7.45 ERA. He's made 13 relief outings, including Saturday, when he needed just two pitches to get a double play and end the eighth against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino has started the season with seven consecutive losses, but it's not all because he's not pitching well. He has a respectable 4.40 ERA and has had the worst run support in the National League this season. Witness his most recent start Sunday against the Reds, in which Paulino threw eight scoreless innings and gave up four hits, four walks and struck out five batters. The game was tied at 0-0 before the Astros won in extra innings. In his Past three starts, he's allowed four earned runs in 20 innings. He's given up just two home runs all year in 59 1/3 innings, but walks continue to be a problem (34). Paulino faced the Cubs on April 16 in Chicago and took the loss, giving up six hits and five earned runs in six innings. He's 0-2 with a 7.82 ERA in three career games against the Cubs, including two starts.
away_pitcher_note:
This will be Zambrano's first start since April 20. The right-hander moved to the bullpen to 
make room in the rotation for Ted Lilly and also to give the team a potent setup pitcher. He was effective until May 14 against the Pirates, when he gave up three runs on four hits over one inning. Zambrano then said he wasn't comfortable in the role and wanted to go back to the rotation. Since that game against the Pirates, he has given up one hit over 4 1/3 scoreless innings. Big Z tuned up with a 73-pitch simulated game last Monday. In four starts, Zambrano was 1-2 with a 7.45 ERA. He's made 13 relief outings, including Saturday, when he needed just two pitches to get a double play and end the eighth against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his string of 10 consecutive quality starts to begin the season brought to an abrupt end in his previous start Monday when he was ejected in the third inning for what crew chief Gary Darling said was showing up an umpire. Despite piling up the quality starts, Oswalt has lost five of his past six decisions because he's received poor run support. In the start prior to his ejection, he threw eight scoreless innings at Milwaukee and got the win. Oswalt beat the Cubs earlier this year, firing seven scoreless innings and striking out six batters April 17 at Wrigley Field. He's 14-12 with a 3.67 ERA in 31 career games against the Cubs, including 30 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster threw a season-high 125 pitches in his last start Sunday against the Cardinals. The Cubs needed him to go deep because of an overworked bullpen. The right-hander said he didn't execute his pitches well, giving up six runs over 6 2/3 innings on nine hits, including two home runs by Albert Pujols. Dempster has lost five of his last six decisions. He did not get a decision against the Astros on April 18, giving up one run on four hits over 7 2/3 innings. He struck out eight in that game.

Wells pitched five shutout innings on two days' rest against the Pirates on Monday after failing to retire a batter in his previous start, a 7-1 loss on May 28 to St. Louis in which he allowed six hits on 16 pitches. Wells left the game against Pittsburgh with a 1-0 lead after tossing 90 pitches on a hot and very humid afternoon.

home_pitcher_note: A rainout between these two clubs Wednesday forced them to play on an off-day, and the Pirates are taking it as an opportunity to start the newly acquired Eveland without mixing up the rotation too much. Eveland threw two innings in an extended Spring Training game Thursday in Bradenton, Fla., and will look to erase any lingering memory of his last three starts with the Blue Jays, when he went just a combined 9 1/3 innings, giving up 17 earned runs off 23 hits while walking 10 and striking out just five. Eveland has pitched just 2 2/3 innings in three appearances against the Cubs, giving up two runs on two hits while striking out three and walking two.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is 7-0 in 10 starts for the Cubs after a win over the Cardinals on Saturday. He's the first pitcher in Cubs history to go 7-0 (or better) in his first 10 starts for the team.  The last Major League player to do that for any team was CC Sabathia for the Brewers in 2008 (8-0). Silva is coming off a win over the Cardinals in which he threw seven shutout innings, giving up two hits and striking out a career-high 11 batters.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is the only Brewers starter on a roll, going 6-0 with a 1.86 ERA in his past 10 starts after going 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his first two. In his last outing against the Marlins, he allowed one earned run and four hits in seven strong innings and hit a game-tying two-run home run to help the Brewers to a win. "I've been feeling good the whole year," Gallardo said. "The first few starts, I struggled a little bit with a lot of walks and command overall. That's something I still have to work on -- work on it every bullpen [session] and apply it to the following start."
away_pitcher_note: Lilly has fared slightly better on the road, posting a 3.08 ERA in four starts compared to a 4.15 ERA in four at Wrigley Field. In his last start on June 1 against the Pirates, he gave up three runs on six hits over 7 2/3 innings and lost, 3-2. Lilly was cruising and then served up a game-winning home run to Neil Walker in the eighth. The Cubs decided to push him back and miss the makeup game vs. the Pirates because Lilly is 0-2 in three starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers gave Wolf a choice: Start Wednesday on regular rest, or take an extra day, something all Brewers starters have been doing when the team encounters a day off. Wolf opted against the extra rest, thinking he would be more sharp on a set schedule, so he'll pitch Game 2 of a series between the Brewers and Cubs. Wolf's command has not been good of late; he averaged 1.7 walks per start last season but has walked at least four batters in three of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miller Park is one of Zambrano's favorite venues. The right-hander threw his no-hitter there in September 2008. This will be his second start since returning to the rotation. In his first, Big Z gave up three runs on six hits over 4 1/3 innings and took the loss against the Astros. He threw 84 pitches and the stadium radar gun showed his fastball was at 90-91 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was bumped from the rotation so lefty Manny Parra could start Sunday against the Cardinals and he found himself in a surprising relief spot. Bush got the call to relieve Parra with one out, the bases loaded and the Brewers clinging to a 3-2 lead in the sixth inning. He struck out pinch-hitter Skip Schumaker in a 12-pitch marathon, helping avoid a big Cardinals blow-up in a game the Brewers eventually won, 4-3, in 10 innings. Now he's headed back to the starting rotation. "I was going to throw a bullpen session after the game anyway, probably 20-30 pitches," Bush said. "So [the relief work] ended up being just about the same thing with warming up and that long at-bat."
away_pitcher_note: Dempster finally got some run support in his last start against the Astros as the Cubs scored eight runs. He struck out seven for the eighth time in 12 starts and notched his eighth quality start, giving up three runs on six hits over 6 1/3 innings. Dempster did give up two home runs, and now has served up 12 in 12 games. On the plus side, they were solo shots and he avoided any big innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wells' string of first-inning nightmares continued on Sunday in his start at Houston. The Astros rattled off five hits in a row, including a two-run homer by Carlos Lee, in the first inning en route to a 6-3 victory over the Cubs. It continued a disturbing trend for Wells; on May 6, the Pirates batted around against the right-hander, scoring five runs in the first. He lasted two innings in that start. On May 28, the Cardinals smacked six consecutive hits off Wells, who failed to retire a batter. He was pulled after 16 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy's last start was a lost duel against rookie Mitch Talbot. Despite going seven innings and only giving up two earned runs, Talbot gave up one fewer, and earned the win as the Indians held onto the win. Peavy struck out three while only giving up six hits. This is Peavy's first appearance against the Cubs, who nearly acquired him in a trade during the 2008 offseason before eventually being dealt the crosstown White Sox during the '09 season.

home_pitcher_note: Silva tossed seven innings in his last start in Pittsburgh on Monday, surrendering one run on four hits and got the win. He made history, becoming the first Cubs starter since Ken Holtzman, who went 9-0 in 1967, to open a season with eight wins and no losses. Silva joined some pretty special company, considering the last pitcher in the Major Leagues to do that with any team was CC Sabathia, who went 8-0 in his first 10 starts with the Brewers in 2008. He also became the first Cubs starter to begin his Cubs career 8-0 in 100 years. King Cole started 8-0 back in 1910.
away_pitcher_note: Buerhle only netted three innings and gave up six runs in his last start, but he was taken off the hook when his counterpart, Jake Westbrook, also gave up six runs and allowed Buehrle to sneak by with a no-decision despite his poor outing. Buehrle threw 95 pitches despite only going those three innings. Buehrle's outing was over as soon as Lou Marson, who had not homered before in the season, took Buehrle deep with two runners on base to bring his earned run total to six runs. Lifetime against the crosstown rival Cubs, Buehrle is 4-4 with a 4.58 ERA in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers. It was his sixth straight quality start -- and he has not earned a win in any of them. According to Elias Sports Bureau, Lilly is the second pitcher in Cubs history to go winless over six consecutive quality starts. The other was Sheriff Blake in 1926. Lilly struck out six Brewers, a season high, and gave up one run on Corey Hart's home run. Maybe this time, he'll get some run support.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd pitched well enough to win his last start, as he held Detroit to one run in six innings. He left the bases loaded in the second inning, and followed that up by leaving two on in the third. The only run was scored when Brandon Inge's single in the sixth knocked in Ryan Raburn, who led off the frame with a double. Unfortunately for Floyd, he didn't get the win, as the bullpen imploded in the seventh inning and the Tigers pushed across six runs. Floyd has one career start against the Cubs, and in that start he went seven innings, giving up one run over four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano gave up two hits in five innings in his last start against the Brewers but he also walked five. He was pulled after throwing 88 pitches. It was his second start since returning to the rotation after 13 relief appearances. The Cubs are hoping that with more starts, he'll improve his command. He has faced the Athletics once, and that was in 2004. So far this season. Zambrano is 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA at home and 2-3 with a 6.91 ERA on the road. Those numbers include his relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill turned in one of the finest performances of his career in his last start, a 6-1 win over the Angels. The 22-year-old right-hander tossed a career-high eight innings, allowing an earned run on six hits and a walk while striking out four. Since taking over for an injured Justin Duchscherer in Oakland's rotation, Cahill has proved to be one of the A's most consistent pitchers. He's thrown a quality start in each of his last six outings, going 4-1 with a 2.25 ERA in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster took the loss in his last start against the Brewers, giving up three runs on five hits over 5 1/3 innings. He threw 104 pitches -- and was pulled because the Cubs wanted to shorten him up, pitch count wise. Dempster is 2-3 with a 3.71 ERA at home, and has served up 13 home runs in 13 games. Last year, he gave up 13 homers in 17 starts in the first half. That's not a good trend. He also walked five against the Brewers. That's another bad trend.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez struggled with his control in his last start, a 6-2 defeat at San Francisco on Friday. Gonzalez was visibly upset with himself on the mound after issuing walks and exited after giving up a pair of two-run homers. He finished 5 1/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on six hits and four walks while striking out four. The start marked the third time all year Gonzalez gave up more than three earned runs and it was the first since May 12, a span of five starts. Gonzalez has never faced the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Wells had troubles in the first inning again. He did retire the first two batters he faced but then served up four straight hits, including RBI singles to Andruw Jones and A.J. Pierzynski in his last start. Opposing teams now are batting .357 off the right-hander in the first. Pitching coach Larry Rothschild has identified a mechanical glitch when Wells pitches out of the stretch, so it'll be interesting to see if he makes the adjustment this time. Wells' confidence level is down; he needs to get off to a good start from the first pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Braden was originally scheduled to start on Tuesday, but had it moved back to rest his inflamed left elbow tendon. Braden said he felt tightness in the area in the week leading up to his last start on June 9, specifically citing a bullpen session that may have caused his arm to tighten up. Braden said he felt the arm cramp up a bit during the third or fourth inning of the outing, which ended after he gave up five runs (four earned) on 11 hits and a walk, while striking out four in 5 2/3 innings. Braden said he had no history of injuries with his throwing elbow prior to this incident.

home_pitcher_note: Silva should be 9-0. In his last start, the right-hander gave up two runs on seven hits over seven innings, but one of the runs could have been prevented if his defense stepped up. Silva did throw a career-high 123 pitches, so the extra day of rest should help. He was quick enough in his last start to recognize that he needed to change speeds more to keep the White Sox off balance. It worked.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir's stuff was alive against the Dodgers, but too many deep counts didn't enable him to get past the fifth inning, yielding two earned runs on three hits and four walks while striking out five men. He threw 106 pitches, forcing his exit. He has given up only four earned runs in his past 17 innings, dropping his ERA from 6.34 to 5.26. Kazmir is making his Wrigley Field debut. He has faced the Cubs once, giving up one earned run in 4 2/3 innings with seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Lilly was "brilliant," as Lou Piniella said. The left-hander had a no-hitter through eight innings on Sunday and lost his bid when pinch-hitter Juan Pierre singled to lead off the ninth. Lilly was then pulled after throwing 108 pitches. The lefty got the win, which snapped a personal five-game losing streak. In three starts this month, he's 1-1 with a 1.52 ERA. In his career, Lilly is 5-4 with a 3.45 ERA in 10 starts against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is coming off a solid effort in a win against the Dodgers on Sunday at Dodger Stadium, yielding three earned runs on five hits and one walk while striking out seven across six innings. The slender right-hander has been among the AL leaders all season in strikeouts and was on top after his most recent effort with 96 in 87 2/3 innings. He has a 2.39 ERA in day games and has yielded three or fewer runs in 11 of his 14 starts. Weaver's 4-2, 4.44 in eight road tests. He will be pitching in Wrigley Field and against the Cubs for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano took the loss in his last start Tuesday against the Athletics, and it was an ugly game. The Cubs made four errors, so only two of the five runs off Zambrano were earned. He escaped a bases-loaded jam in the first, but wasn't so lucky in a four-run fourth. Zambrano went six innings, striking out four. And he even got a RBI single. Big Z admitted he was aiming for the building beyond the left-field bleachers in his last at-bat in the sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders returns to the road, to Wrigley Field for the first time in his career, and he probably welcomes it. His home struggles continued on Monday night against the Brewers, who cuffed him around for six earned runs on six hits, including a pair of homers and three walks in 5 2/3 innings. Saunders is 4-1 with a 2.45 ERA in six road assignments, but he has yielded 33 earned runs in 44 innings (6.75 ERA) while going 1-6 at home. Command of his two-seam fastball is imperative for Saunders, who didn't have it during a five-run third inning that included Ryan Braun's grand slam.

home_pitcher_note: If there's one complaint to have about Vargas this season, it's that high pitch counts often limit how far into games he can go. That wasn't an issue in his most recent start, in which he went 7 2/3 innings in a 2-1 win at St. Louis. That gave him 11 quality starts in 13 tries, tying him for sixth in the Majors, and he did it on 94 pitches with no walks.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster notched his ninth quality start in his last outing against the Athletics. He gave up two runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, throwing 120 pitches. It's the fourth time he's thrown at least 120. Dempster also struck out seven as he won for the third time in his past five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lee was nothing short of brilliant in a 1-0 shutout win against the Reds on Friday. He worked out of trouble in the first and cruised the rest of the way. His ability to avoid walks has been a major key to his success, as he's issued just four free passes while dealing 67 strikeouts. Only three other pitchers since 1900 have tallied as many strikeouts with so few walks (Bret Saberhagen, Greg Maddux and Ben Sheets) in a 10-start period, and Lee's the only one to do it in his first 10 outings of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Wells got back on track in his last start. He held the A's to two runs on seven hits over seven innings. The problem in his previous starts was that he was falling off the rubber. A couple of side sessions, some work with pitching coach Larry Rothschild, advice from Greg Maddux and a good look at video helped Wells figure it out. Wells has never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez has taken four of his past five starts through at least eight innings, and his most recent outing was his best yet. He followed up Cliff Lee's shutout with a one-run complete game, walking one and striking out nine. That was a point of pride for Hernandez, who wasn't happy about having to leave his previous start after 8 2/3 innings. To say the least, he and Lee make a formidable pair. There's just no telling how much longer it will last.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly struggled in his last start, giving up eight runs (six earned) on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Angels. It was the most runs he's served up since being charged with nine on July 20, 2009, at Philadelphia. Lilly gave up four runs in the first inning; he had given up one run in the first in his previous 10 starts combined. The lefty gave up multiple homers for the third time, and second this month.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy is set to take on the Cubs again. In his last outing against the Nationals, he was the Peavy who won the 2007 NL Cy Young Award, pitching a shutout. More impressively, he yielded just three hits and two walks for the duration of the game. Before the game, such an output would have been unexpected, considering he had a fluid buildup in his right shoulder. On Tuesday, Peavy said, "There's not tears or any significant injuries in there that you can make worse by pitching. That was the biggest thing with me, knowing we're structurally sound. Certainly I want to get out there and I want to be healthy enough to throw bullpens in between, really throw a baseball to work on things and not have to take the mound like we have the last couple times." Two starts ago, Peavy took on the Cubs, going seven innings and giving up two runs in a 10-5 White Sox win.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano did not face the White Sox in the team's first Interleague series at Wrigley Field. The right-hander is coming off his best outing since returning to the rotation June 4. Against the Angels, he gave up one run on eight hits over seven innings and struck out seven. The seven innings were a season high, and he picked up his first win at Wrigley since July 12, 2009. The right-hander will miss hitting at the American League ballpark. He had two singles and drove in a run in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia got another win in his last start, going seven innings and allowing three runs against the Nationals. Washington scored all three runs in a big third inning. In the frame, Cristian Guzman led off the inning with a triple, followed by Adam Dunn's RBI fielder's choice. After the game, Dunn admitted it was hard to pick up the ball out of Garcia's hand. "He had a lot of movement on all of his pitches," Dunn said. "He is really deceptive being a big guy. He hides the ball very well. He was tough to pick up. He was just tough today." Lifetime against the Cubs, Garcia is 4-0 in five starts with an anemic 1.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Silva was supposed to start Thursday against his former team, the Mariners, but the right hamstring tweak that got him pulled from his last start after 69 pitches forced the Cubs to juggle the rotation, so now Silva will pitch against the White Sox. Silva is coming off his second straight loss, but it was his team-leading 10th quality start. He won his first eight decisions with the Cubs and has dropped two in a row, although he has pitched well enough to win both. If he goes deep, he's tough. Silva has a 2.07 ERA when he throws at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Danks struggled early in his last start against the Braves, but he settled down quite nicely, at one point getting 10 consecutive batters out en route to putting up his third consecutive win. He did not allow another run, and only two singles after those rough first two innings. "My job tonight was to keep it at three," Danks said. "It was fortunate that these guys gave us nine. It made it a little bit easier on us." Lifetime against the Cubs, Danks is 2-0 in three starts, with a sparkling 0.90 ERA over those 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off a tough loss. He gave up two runs on five hits, including a homer, over eight innings, yet took the loss in a 2-0 defeat to Seattle. With the loss, Dempster is 2-1 with a 3.08 ERA in four starts this month. Dempster did not face the White Sox when the two teams met at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is looking for his first win since April 30. The right-hander is coming off a loss to Seattle in which he gave up six runs on 10 hits over six innings. He has gone winless in May and June, serving up 20 earned runs in 61 1/3 innings in those two months so far. He's 0-1 in two starts against the Pirates, including a loss May 6 when he gave up six earned runs on five hits in two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm would like to forget absolutely everything from his last outing, one which lasted a career-short one inning. The left-hander was missing with all his pitches, and when he wasn't walking hitters, the pitches were right down the middle. He faced just 15 hitters. Four of them walked and seven got hits. Still, the outing was an anomaly for Maholm, who has been the Pirates' most consistent starter all year. Prior to Wednesday, he hadn't allowed more than four runs in any of his first 14 starts this year. Maholm is 6-1 with a 6.29 ERA in 11 career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start June 24 against the Mariners. He gave up one run on five hits over six innings. He has only one win in his last 11 starts. The lefty is 0-2 with a 4.35 ERA in three games against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens battled through 5 1/3 innings in his last start, but was denied a third win when the Pirates' bullpen couldn't a two-run lead. Karstens wasn't lights out, but given that he was facing baseball's hottest team at the time, he did well in limiting Texas to two earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will replace Carlos Zambrano in the Cubs rotation. Gorzelanny began the season in the rotation but was moved when Zambrano didn't like his relief role. Gorzelanny has made six relief appearances, including last Friday when he went 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln's outing Friday was his fourth start of the season. His performance -- six innings, three earned runs, eight hits -- was similar to his others and only lowered his ERA from 6.50 to 6.00. Lincoln threw 107 pitches, 63 of them for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Silva had to leave his last start against the White Sox after six innings because of some tightness in his right hamstring. He will have to be cautious running the bases to avoid aggravating it. This will be a good chance to impress the NL All-Star coaching staff.
away_pitcher_note: Wood will make his Major League debut after Sam LeCure was sent down to Triple-A Louisville. A former second-round pick, Wood has started 15 games this year for Louisville, going 5-6 with a 3.12 ERA, 23 walks and 97 strikeouts in 98 innings.

home_pitcher_note: If Dempster can get through the first inning unscathed, he's OK. So far, he's given up 11 runs in the first in his 16 starts combined for a 6.19 ERA. Ouch. He is the workhorse and has thrown 120 pitches in five of his outings this year.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo lasted just five innings his last time out, but most of his struggles Sunday afternoon could be attributed to Cleveland's Shin-Soo Choo, who hit two home runs off Arroyo for the second time this season.  It was one of only two losses for Arroyo in his last 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is still having some mechanical issues. He also can't seem to get a win. Despite picking up his eighth quality start in his last outing, Wells has not won in his last 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto has turned in back-to-back dominant starts and has lost just one game since April 24. In wins over the Phillies and A's, he's gone a combined 15 innings and allowed one run. He relied on a strong Reds defense Monday, as he struck out none in the win.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly may not want to turn the calendar. He went 2-2 with a 2.57 ERA in six June starts. It was his lowest monthly ERA since a 2.08 mark in September 2009. He has gone at least seven innings in seven of his 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake was saved from his second loss on Tuesday by a ninth-inning home run. His start had been pushed back a few days to allow for more rest. He allowed a season-high six runs and has given up five or more in three of four starts. He's recorded a win just once since May 15.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy will be pitching on a ton of extra rest. The young right-hander last started on June 26 against Tampa Bay. Kennedy, who hasn't had many speed bumps this season, walked a career-high nine and used his extra time in between starts to iron out his mechanics.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since May 26, Gorzelanny threw 77 pitches over five scoreless innings vs. the Pirates. The lefty, who has taken over Carlos Zambrano's spot, faced the D-backs May 2 and picked up the win.

home_pitcher_note: Enright will make his second career start and, if it's a good one, will be the D-backs's No. 5 starter for the foreseeable future. On June 30 in St. Louis, the right-hander allowed one run in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Silva notched his 12th quality start in his last outing vs. the Reds with a season-high 7 2/3 innings. He hasn't won since May 29 because of a lack of runs. Silva has a 2.90 ERA in nine starts at Wrigley.

home_pitcher_note: Friday against the Dodgers, Jackson didn't have the best follow-up to his June 25 no-hitter, but he still ended up with the win. In five innings against Los Angeles, he allowed four earned runs. He said afterward that he was battling his mechanics on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Technically, Dempster had a quality start in his last outing, but it was ugly. He was charged with five runs, but only two were earned vs. the Reds. He struck out nine, matching a season high.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw's allowed more than three runs just twice this season and is pitching like a true ace. He wasn't able to finish six innings in his last start, but he let up just four hits and two walks, striking out eight. He's only faced the Cubs once his career, earning the win.
away_pitcher_note: Wells no-hit the Reds until the seventh inning in his last start, the second time he's done that in his career, and won for the first time since April 30. He's switched to a more compact delivery, and it's helped.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has gone six innings in his last two starts, allowing three total runs. After a rough April and an injured June, Billingsley is pitching more confidence now that he's not worrying about his pitch counts, which can still climb high, but the club has accepted it.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly was roughed up in his last start vs. the Reds, serving up a career-high 11 hits, including four home runs. The problem was location. In late May, he threw seven shutout innings vs. the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Ely's last start, a 2 2/3-innings, five-earned run performance against the Marlins, was a regression after he had gone seven innings and allowed one run in each of his last two starts. The rookie, who relies on control, needs to show consistency. He's 1-4 in his last five.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has pitched quite well since rejoining the rotation on June 30. Most recently, on Monday in Arizona, he yielded three runs to the D-backs over five innings. Walks -- he issued a season-high six -- cost him a chance at pitching deep into the game.

home_pitcher_note: Until recently, Padilla's designation as the team's Opening Day starter hasn't carried much weight. But Padilla, since returning from a nerve problem in his right arm, has been magnificent his last three starts, letting up five combined runs in 20 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Silva has thrown seven straight quality starts. He was bothered by lingering leg soreness in his last start, Tuesday against the D-backs, but allowed just two runs on four hits over six frames. He'll be seeking to finish his first-half with another 'W.'

home_pitcher_note: In his final start of the season's first half, Dempster allowed three D-backs runs on eight hits and fanned six over five innings. He threw just 98 pitches, but that was by design: Lou Piniella said it was the prudent thing to do, given the righty's long lay-off.
away_pitcher_note: A year ago at this time, left-hander Jamie Moyer's spot in the Phillies' rotation appeared shaky at best. That proved true as right-hander Pedro Martinez replaced him in August. But Moyer has done a better job, solidifying his spot in 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly has struggled in his last two starts, giving up 16 runs over 10 1/3 innings. He's having issues with his mechanics and his pitches are flat and over the center of the plate. It's not a good combo.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Joe Blanton had a disappointing first half. He started the season on the disabled list with a strained right oblique, and has struggled for most of the season. The Phillies will need a much improved Blanton in the second half if they hope to catch the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Wells has had success vs. the NL East, posting a 1-1 record and 1.80 ERA in three starts. He seems to have bounced back from a rough June in which he was winless in five starts. His home/road ERA numbers are identical.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Cole Hamels had a rough April, but has looked like the second half of the 1-2 punch the Phillies hoped they could team up with right-hander Roy Halladay before the season started. If Hamels keeps it up, few teams can boast two pitchers like the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny is coming off a win against the Dodgers in which he struck out seven over six innings. It was his third start since returning to the rotation and he's looked better each outing.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Roy Halladay has lived up to the billing. He has thrown a perfect game. He has third-best ERA in the National League. The only thing that has held him back is run support. If the offense picks up in the second half, Halladay should win a lot of games.

home_pitcher_note: Silva's last start ended after 1 1/3 innings when he was ejected by umpire Brian Runge for arguing a close play at first. Silva had some soreness in right calf but has had plenty of rest.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez lost his first game in three starts, but he still pitched good enough to earn the win his last time out. He gave up three runs, all on a homer by Cardinals left fielder Matt Holiday in a 4-2 loss. He has regained his 2009 form after a tough start to the season.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster opened the second half on strong note, striking out nine Phillies. He's now five Ks away from reaching 1,500 in his career. But he's also served up 17 home runs; he gave up 22 in 200 innings last year.
away_pitcher_note: Wright will make the first start of his Major League career after Felipe Paulino suffered a recurrence of right shoulder tendinitis during his side session Friday. The 25-year-old has made six relief appearances for the Astros this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly rebounded from two bad starts to strike out 10 Phillies over seven innings in his last outing. He made some mechanical tweaks and they worked. His starts are being watched by teams looking for help.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is one of 53 pitchers since 1920 to begin a season with 19 straight starts of six-plus innings. Dan Haren did the same last year, and Myers can be the first to make it 20 in a row to start a season since Pedro Martinez and Mark Buehrle in 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is 1-1 with a 1.66 ERA in three July starts. He's made some mechanical adjustments and been able to cut down on the walks. He grew up in Cardinals country so any game vs. the Redbirds is big.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan is doing what he's been asked to do, keeping the Cardinals in games. He hasn't been great, but he's made one significant improvement from his time as a Brewer. Suppan has been much more effective with runners on base, which is keeping him out of big innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has won his past three starts, posting a 3.06 ERA in that stretch. He's done so in workmanlike fashion and has 16 strikeouts over 17 2/3 innings. In his last start, the lefty even got a hit off Roy Halladay.
away_pitcher_note: Hawksworth suffered his first stumble of any kind since he was moved to the rotation his last time out, and even then he wasn't too bad. Hawksworth has been a revelation as a starter for the Cardinals, and he'll try to keep it going at Wrigley.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster walked four over five innings and gave up eight hits, but a big error led to three unearned runs. He didn't pitch poorly, just didn't get much help behind him. He's 2-1 with 4.30 ERA in July.
away_pitcher_note: For the first time all year, Carpenter is not just pitching well but feeling good about how he's getting results. He's happier with his delivery than he's been all season. That bodes ill for the National League, since he was already having a very nice year.

home_pitcher_note: Wright's performance last Tuesday against the Cubs was enough for him to earn another start. In his first career start, Wright gave up five runs but they were all unearned after an error in the fifth derailed his four scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Silva failed to get past the first inning in his last start, the second straight game in which he's not gone beyond two innings. He is being given an extra day to work on the side with pitching coach Larry Rothschild.

home_pitcher_note: Myers pitched his 20th consecutive start of six or more innings last Wednesday against the Cubs. He gave up one run over seven innings and had eight strikeouts in a no-decision. Myers will look to extend his streak of quality starts to five games.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly just faced the Astros in his last start and will try to have similar results. He held them to one run over 7 1/3 innings while striking out six. He's been hot topic at trade deadline.

home_pitcher_note: Norris didn't factor in the decision his last start against the Reds, giving up four runs over six innings. This season he has held opposing team's leadoff hitters to a .131 average which is the lowest among MLB starters.
away_pitcher_note: Wells has turned things around in July. In his last four starts, he's given up four earned runs over 28 2/3 innings for a 1.26 ERA. He's thrown more than six innings in his last seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched five strong innings before exiting for a rain delay on Sunday against the Phillies, striking out six and giving up two runs in a 4-3 loss. He's started five games against the Cubs, notching an 8.77 ERA without a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster notched a quality start in his last outing but also served up a game-tying home run to Albert Pujols. Dempster is 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two starts vs. NL West teams.

home_pitcher_note: After an extended stretch without a loss, Hammel has taken defeats in his last three outings. He's given up 12 earned runs in 19 2/3 innings over that span but is 1-0 with a 5.40 ERA in one career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning to the rotation, Gorzelanny is 4-0 with a 2.83 ERA in five starts. The lefty has fared better on the road, posting a 2.25 ERA in 10 games (six starts).

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa gave up two first-inning runs, but wound up holding the Pirates to three runs and six hits in seven innings. He struck out eight and has fanned 16 in 13 innings over his last two starts, although he lost both.
away_pitcher_note: Silva picked up the win in his last start against the Astros, an improved outing after not being able to go past the second inning in his previous two games.

home_pitcher_note: Wells did not pitch poorly in his last start vs. the Astros, but did fall behind hitters and also walked a season-high five over 5 2/3 innings. He needs to get re-focused.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers timed Gallardo's return from the DL so he would appear in this series, but he's coming off a bad start against the Reds in which he allowed five earned runs in 2 2/3 innings, matching the shortest start of his career.

home_pitcher_note: This would have been Ted Lilly's spot, but instead the Cubs will call up Diamond from Triple-A Iowa. He was 5-4 with a 3.16 ERA in 21 starts for the Minor League team. This will be his Major League debut.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson took a 2-0 lead into the sixth inning of his last start but didn't retire any of the three batters he faced in a Reds rally that denied the left-hander his ninth win. The Brewers are 8-9 in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster walked five in four-plus innings in his last start, his shortest outing of the season. He started well, then admitted he lost his "aggressiveness."
away_pitcher_note: Parra has met the definition of quality start -- six or more innings, three or fewer earned runs -- in only one of his past six outings. He is 0-1 with a 5.84 ERA in two starts and two relief appearances against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny pitched well enough to win in his last start but did not get a decision as the Rockies won on Carlos Gonzalez's walk-off homer. Gorzelanny gave up five runs and nine hits over 6 1/3 innings. He finished July 4-0 with a 4.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo gave up just one earned run in seven innings in his last outing, shutting down the Braves to record his first win in 15 days. Arroyo has gone five or more innings in six straight starts, not allowing more than three earned runs in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: Wells struggled in his last start against the Brewers, giving up seven runs on 10 hits over four-plus innings. In the fourth inning, he gave up six straight hits. Execution of pitches was the problem.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez struggled with his control for the third consecutive start, walking five, but came away with his second win since his return from Tommy John surgery. He struck out six, needing 96 pitches (just 55 strikes) to get through five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Diamond struck out 10 in his Major League debut Tuesday against the Brewers. He's the first Cubs rookie to do that in his first start since Mark Prior fanned 10 May 22, 2002, vs. the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is coming off a seven-inning, two-hit outing against the Pirates on Monday, his second scoreless start. The 23-year-old has gone at least five innings in his last five starts, good for an ERA of 1.91.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner had the shortest outing of his big league career in Coors Field Wednesday, lasting four innings and two batters against an explosive Rockies lineup. He yielded four runs on nine hits and a walk and was hampered by an elevated pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's first start since that fateful June 25 game when he threw a tantrum, was sent home, and eventually underwent treatment for anger issues. He will be limited to 75-80 pitches. His velocity has been better.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Braves, Lincecum yielded two home runs for the first time in more than two years, taking his first loss since July 2. He allowed three runs on six hits, striking out seven in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster picked up the win in his last start against the Brewers, giving up three unearned runs over six innings. It was his 10th start in which all of the runs were unearned, and first since Sept. 3, 2009, vs. the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Zito pitched brilliantly in his last start, allowing two runs on four hits while striking out 10, but once again didn't get enough run support to earn a decision in a Giants' 10-inning win. Zito has a 2.02 ERA since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Gorzelanny gave up three runs over seven innings for his ninth quality start. The Cubs, however, were shut out. The lefty has received two or fewer runs in 10 starts, including no runs four times.

home_pitcher_note: A three-run fourth inning in his last start against the Braves gave Cain his first loss since the All-Star break, as the right-hander allowed six runs in five innings. Cain is 5-2 with a 2.41 ERA in eight career starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells gave up three runs over seven-plus innings against the Reds in his last start and took the loss. He's now given up three or fewer runs in seven of his past nine games. The loss was his third straight.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook has pitched well since he joined the Cardinals two games ago, yet he's still looking for his first victory. He gave up two runs in six innings against the Astros in his Cards debut, then allowed three runs in seven innings vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Diamond didn't get past the third inning in his last start, against the Reds. He struggled with fastball location. The hope is he can get his second pitch, his changeup, to be more effective and help him go deeper.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is coming on strong, with quality starts in all six of his games since the All-Star break and a 1.79 ERA in that span. The Cardinals have won all six of those starts, and they're 19-6 on the year when Carpenter takes the mound.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's second start since returning to the rotation. In his first outing against the Giants, he walked seven over five innings. The problem was too much movement on his pitches. He needs to have better command.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse will make his return to the rotation on Sunday. He last pitched in the Majors on May 22, undergoing forearm surgery soon after. Lohse was superb in his last rehab start, giving the club confidence to reinsert him in the starting five.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster picked up the win in his last start against the Giants despite sloppy play behind him. He gave up four runs (three earned) on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings. He is 0-1 in two starts vs. the Cardinals this year.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny seems to have trouble with one inning. In his last start, against the Giants, it was the first, as he gave up three runs. He's 3-4 with a 4.02 ERA at home, where teams are hitting .254 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Don't let Correia's line in his last start against the Pirates fool you, as he took a shutout into the seventh inning before four runs scored. Correia struck out seven and buried his fastball down in the strike zone better than he has all season.

home_pitcher_note: Suffice to say, Wells has had a rough August. The righty got shelled for six runs his last time out, and another six runs on Aug. 2 against the Brewers. He has given up six homers over his last four starts, a number he must cut down.
away_pitcher_note: Garland won his 11th game of the season in his last start, holding the Bucs to one hit over six shutout innings. He's allowed three or fewer runs in each of his last four starts. He's walked 10 over his last two starts but has minimized the damage.

home_pitcher_note: On the heels of Thomas Diamond's consecutive rough starts, Lou Piniella is turning to Coleman and will give him a shot in the rotation. It will be the rookie's first big league start after four appearances out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Richard lasted six innings on Friday vs. the Giants, allowing two runs on six hits. Since lowering his ERA to a season-low 2.71 on June 13, he has an ERA of 5.20, but he's 6-2 in that span. He's won six of his last seven decisions.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's first start at home since his tantrum June 25. He's pitched in two games on the road. He's done well at Wrigley Field. In 15 road games, he has a 6.70 ERA, while he has a 3.00 ERA in 12 home games.
away_pitcher_note: Latos gave up one run on five hits over six innings in his last start. He's allowed one run over his last 12 innings and is 7-1 in his past 11 starts. He's in the middle of a Cy Young-type season that could also lead to the postseason.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is on a roll. He's 3-0 with a 1.40 ERA in his past three starts, including a win Sunday over the Cardinals. He faced the Braves in the second game of the season, gave up one run on three hits over six and lost. That's how it's been.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has won five of six decisions in the nine starts he's made since ending a two-month stint on the disabled list. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his three starts this month.
