home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has gotten two or fewer runs of support in 11 of his 18 starts. In his last outing, he threw a season-high 120 pitches over 6 1/3 innings. He's gone at least six innings in seven-straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson has gone winless while allowing one earned run or fewer in his past five starts. According to Elias, he is the first Major League pitcher to do this since the AL and NL began recognizing earned runs as an official stat in 1913.

home_pitcher_note: Wells deserved better in his last start. He gave up one run in the first inning, then held the Padres scoreless over the next six but took the loss. He now has a 2.22 ERA in his 10 starts when he's gone at least seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Minor has been impressive during the first two starts of his career. The only runs he surrendered in Tuesday's six-inning stint against the Nationals came courtesy of a pair of two-out, sixth-inning RBI doubles.

home_pitcher_note: His last time out, Hernandez lasted seven innings and allowed two runs on nine hits. He was given a 2-0 lead in the top of the third inning, thanks to RBI singles by Roger Bernadina and Ryan Zimmerman, but he would lose the lead in the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Coleman's second Major League start and sixth big league game. The rookie had a tough 37-pitch first inning in his last outing vs. the Padres, but then settled down. His goal is to go deeper in the game.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lannan was solid for 5 1/3 innings, and that proved to be enough as the Nationals defeated the Braves, 6-2. Lannan blanked the Braves over the first five innings and picked up eight ground-ball outs in the win.
away_pitcher_note: In his three starts since coming off the restricted list, Zambrano is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA, giving up five earned runs over 16 2/3 innings. But he's also given up 15 hits and walked 15 in those games. The walks will hurt.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis had his best outing of the season on Friday, pitching his first five-inning game of the season and allowing a run on four hits and four walks. He never had a clean inning but did enough to lower his ERA from 14.33 to 11.39.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster matched a season high by going eight innings for the fourth time in his last start against the Braves but did not get a decision. He did serve up his 22nd homer, matching the total he gave up in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Coming back from his seven-game suspension (one missed start), Cueto was too strong and had control issues. He was overthrowing and hitting 96-97 mph, instead of his more effective 93-94 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny picked up a win in his last outing, against the Braves. He's now 7-7 with a 3.82 ERA in his 19 starts. The lefty has thrown 120 pitches in back to back outings, so it will be interesting to see how durable he is.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had another money start Sunday, going seven innings to help the Reds win a series over the Dodgers. It gave him victory No. 100 of his career. Arroyo has worked seven or more innings 16 times this year, including five of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wells admitted he made stupid mistakes in his last outing, and it cost him against the Braves. The right-hander served up a season-tying seven runs and career-tying three homers to the Braves. He's trying to snap a five-game losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: After winning four consecutive starts, Wood surrendered seven runs over four innings in his last start, on Tuesday at AT&T Park in San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Coleman comes off his first Major League victory over Washington on Tuesday. The righty allowed a run on three hits in 6 1/3 innings. The second-generation hurler, son of ex-Major Leaguer Joe Coleman, isn't overpowering but is building confidence.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano is coming off one of his best outings, having given up one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings vs. the Nats. But he's also been dealing with personal matters and flew to Venezuela after that game to see a nephew who is seriously ill.
away_pitcher_note: Winless in his last four starts, Maholm is looking for his third victory in as many starts against the Cubs this season. In his last start at Wrigley Field, on June 28, Maholm held the Cubs to one run on seven hits in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster wasn't happy about being pulled after 79 pitches in his last start, vs. the Nats. But it worked, as a pinch-hitter got on and the Cubs won. Dempster is 4-0 with a 1.31 ERA in five starts in August.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens had his last start skipped because of arm fatigue, but he's expected to not miss any more time. Karstens has already exceeded his 2009 innings total, so the Pirates are going to watch his workload during this final month.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny wasn't happy with his last start and for good reason. He gave up six runs on seven hits to the Reds, including two of three homers that night by Jay Bruce. The lefty will be happy to turn the calendar. He was 1-3 with a 5.46 ERA in August.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald appeared headed for his third win with the Pirates in his last until things imploded for him in the seventh. His defense hurt him, and by the time McDonald's outing ended, he was charged with six earned runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wells couldn't get a grip on his changeup but held on long enough for the win in his last start against the Reds. He went 1-4 with a 5.91 ERA in August after posting a 1.83 ERA in July. He needs to show more consistency.
away_pitcher_note: The knuckler is dancing again for Dickey, who rebounded from a rare poor start to hold the Astros to one run over seven innings at Citi Field. In doing so, he qualified for the ERA title, ranking amongst the likes of Josh Johnson and Ubaldo Jimenez.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano is 3-0 with a 1.84 ERA in his past five starts, beating the Bucs on Monday. He fanned seven and is four K's away from tying Kerry Wood for third on the team's all-time strikeout list. He also hit his first homer and the 21st of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Following a stellar outing at Triple-A Buffalo, Mejia earned the call for his first Major League start at Wrigley Field. Prior to his eight-inning gem in Buffalo, Mejia had produced a 2-0 record and 1.32 ERA over six starts with Double-A Binghamton.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster posted his shortest outing of the season on Tuesday, giving up seven runs in three frames vs. the Pirates. His next win will make him the fourth Canadian born pitcher with 100.
away_pitcher_note: Niese's last outing went from mediocre to poor in a hurry when David Ross hit grand slam off the lefty in Atlanta. Niese allowed a total of 25 runs in August, including 15 over his last two starts, after giving up 19 runs in June and July combined.

home_pitcher_note: Coleman is coming off a game vs. the Reds in which he gave up a season-high eight hits and four runs. The rookie was able to escape a jam in the sixth, which should help down the road.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is 8-2 with a 1.65 ERA over his last 13 starts. He has the second-lowest ERA of any National League starter since June 24. The veteran lefty is 5-4 with a 3.98 ERA in 15 career starts against the Cubbies.

home_pitcher_note: Silva makes his first start since Aug. 1. He came out of that game after four batters because of an abnormal heart rate and has since undergone a procedure to correct that. In his last rehab outing, he threw 78 pitches for Class A Peoria.
away_pitcher_note: Figueroa has posted a 1.96 ERA in four starts for Houston since moving into the club's rotation on Aug. 17. The veteran righty has pitched five or more innings in each outing. He is 1-5 with a 4.12 ERA in 12 career games (six starts) vs. Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Wells was mad at himself after his last start, against the Mets, because of bad execution on some pitches. He had trouble in the first inning again, and he's given up 21 runs in that frame alone. If the Astros get to him early, they have a chance.
away_pitcher_note: Myers was again solid Friday. He allowed three runs in six frames and has pitched at least that many innings in 28 straight stars, a franchise record to begin a season. Myers extended the streak without a feel for his curve. His start was "a battle."

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers are just 10-17 in Bush's starts but he leads the team with 17 "quality starts," outings of six or more innings with three or fewer earned runs. He's 2-9 lifetime against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano has won three straight starts for the first time since July 12-22, 2009. He's 4-0 with a 1.98 ERA in six outings since returning to the rotation. Big Z has moved into sole possession of third on the Cubs' all-time strikeout list.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf's only start against the Cubs this season was a forgettable one, a June 9 loss in which he allowed eight earned runs on nine hits including five Chicago home runs. The five homers tied a dubious Brewers record.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster struggled in his last start, giving up a season-high-tying seven runs on nine hits and four walks over 4 2/3 innings. It was the third time he's failed to go at least five innings. He's now 99-100 in his career, looking for that 100th win.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo breathed a sigh of relief after limiting the Cardinals to two runs on four hits in seven innings on Labor Day. In his three starts before that one, Gallardo had an unsightly 12.27 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Coleman grew up a little in his last start, vs. the Astros. He was roughed up for four runs in the second inning but settled down after that. He didn't get the win, but did get kudos for lasting at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia's last start was his ugliest in quite a while, and he remains a bit unpredictable. Just as he seems to fall into a funk, he'll get hot again. Just as he seems to be on a roll, he'll hit a speed bump. He has a 1.65 ERA at home, though.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Samardzija's first start of the season. He was with the big league club on Opening Day but appeared in four games before going to Triple-A Iowa, where he was 11-3 with a 4.37 ERA in 35 games (15 starts). He's subbing for Carlos Silva.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright bounced back his last time out, showing the form that made him a serious Cy Young contender before a four-start slump. He's been brilliant at home, and now that he's righted there's no reason to think he won't keep rolling.
away_pitcher_note: Wells is 1-6 with a 5.85 ERA in his last nine starts, dating to July 28, and opponents are batting .282 against him in that stretch. That's not good. A St. Louis area native, he'll be making his first career start at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is coming off a rough outing, but it's been an excellent second half for the former Cy Young winner. He hasn't walked a batter in his past two starts, and he's given up four homers in his last 11 starts. Keep doing that and he'll be fine.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano is 5-0 with a 1.60 ERA in his last seven starts since returning to the rotation Aug. 9. In his last start against the Brewers, he had three hits, including an RBI single, and held Milwaukee to three hits over 8 2/3 innings. Nice symmetry.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie will be coming off his five-game suspension and returning to the rotation. Sanabia was suspended for his involvement in the Sept. 1 altercation with Washington. He comes off a win over Washington on Sept. 10.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster picked up his 100th career win in his last start against the Brewers. He's 8-4 on the road this season and knows the Marlins' ballpark well, having pitched there from 1998-2002.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is now the most experienced Marlins starter remaining with Josh Johnson and Ricky Nolasco shut down due to injuries. Sanchez has thrown a career-high 172 innings. He is 4-3 (2.45 ERA) at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Coleman's sixth start. The rookie showed improvement in his last outing as he held the Brewers to one run on five hits over six innings. He avoided that one big inning that has been a problem in other games.

home_pitcher_note: Back-to-back losses to the Phillies inflated the Miller's statistics. He had a rough two starts, giving up 12 earned runs (14 total) over nine innings. He hasn't thrown more than five innings in any of his six appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija picked up his first win as a starter, throwing 5 2/3 scoreless innings against the Cardinals. He struck out one and scattered six hits, walking four. The Cubs want to get a good look at the right-hander to determine where he fits in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano has been a lights-out pitcher since returning to the starting rotation. Over his past seven starts, he is 6-0 with a 1.37 ERA, including holding the Cardinals to one earned run in six innings in his last outing.
away_pitcher_note: Cain continued his second-half dominance against the Dodgers, throwing seven shutout innings to improve to to 6-2 with a 2.71 ERA since the Midsummer Classic. Cain also reached the 200-inning plateau for the fourth straight season.

away_pitcher_note: Coleman beat the Cardinals in his last start, holding them to three runs on five hits over seven innings. The Cubs have been impressed with the rookie's poise. Yes, he did give up a double to Albert Pujuls, but also struck him out.

away_pitcher_note: Zambrano is 7-0 with a 1.27 ERA and 55 strikeouts in his last 10 starts. He's held opponents to a .187 average in that stretch. His mother showed up for his last start in San Diego, finally getting a visa from Venezuela. She'll be in Houston, too.

away_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer had a 7.36 ERA in May before a strong outing at Yankee Stadium on Friday. Dickey struck out six and allowed one run -- a Mark Teixeira homer -- in six innings. The Cubs rocked him for seven runs in his start against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: The Red Sox had the edge in Davis' last start as he fell behind hitters. He served up eight hits and walked three over 3 2/3 innings. The good news is he's healthy -- just looking for that first "W."
away_pitcher_note: Correia heads back on the road, where he is 5-1 with a 2.79 ERA. He's finished at least six innings in eight of 10 starts and beat the Cubs in Chicago on Opening Day. Correia allowed two earned runs in six hits that day.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Wells' first start since April 4. He's been on the DL with a strained right forearm since then and has made two Minor League rehab starts. In his last outing, he threw 68 pitches over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ignore Maholm's record because it has everything to do with run support. Maholm continues to be competitive each time he takes the mound, but the Pirates have scored just 13 runs in the 61 2/3 innings he has been on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster posted his fourth quality start in his last five games against the Mets, giving up one run on seven hits over seven innings. He's doing better at home, picking up back-to-back wins for the first time since July 15-Aug. 4, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: All questions about whether Karstens will stay in the rotation have ceased. In his best start yet, Karstens allowed the Tigers just three hits and one run in six innings on Friday. He retired the first 14 hitters and threw only 75 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez will make his first start since being acquired from Atlanta on May 26. He was 6-1 with a 2.59 ERA in nine starts for Triple-A Gwinnett and has a 4.85 career ERA in the Majors. Lopez, 35, throws four pitches but won't overpower hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez registered career highs with six innings and five strikeouts as Houston beat the Dodgers, 2-1, Wednesday. He has allowed just three runs in his last 11 1/3 innings, but lacks a winning decision this season.

home_pitcher_note: Big Z picked up his first win at home in his most recent start with a win over the Mets. He's now 1-1 with a 3.94 ERA in five starts at Wrigley Field. Zambrano beat the Astros in Houston on April 13.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles is expected to make his Major League debut with Wandy Rodriguez headed for the DL. The 20-year-old righty was the Astros' Minor League Pitcher of the Year in 2010 and is 3-3 with a 3.20 ERA at Triple-A Oklahoma City in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was unable to go five innings for the second straight start in his last outing against the Pirates on Friday, walking six over 4 2/3 innings. Davis needs to throw more strikes inside against right-handed batters.
away_pitcher_note: All four runs Myers surrendered Friday against Arizona were courtesy of first baseman Juan Miranda, who smashed two home runs. Myers left with a 6-4 lead but the Astros lost, 7-6. Myers doesn't have a winning decision in May.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia gets an extra day to rebound after an extremely difficult last start. He threw more than 100 pitches in fewer than four innings in Denver, and admitted he was never quite the same after a 48-pitch first.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster is 3-1 with a 3.08 ERA in his last six starts after going 1-3 with a 9.58 ERA in his first six. He has five quality starts in his last six. Against the Cardinals, Dempster is 7-7 in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Nobody's going better than Lohse, who has allowed seven runs in 36 innings over his past five starts. He's throwing tons of strikes, keeping the ball down, and generally looking like it's 2008 all over again.
away_pitcher_note: Wells threw a lot of pitches (92) in a short period of time (four innings) in his first start off the disabled list Saturday against the Pirates. He'll be pumped to pitch in St. Louis, near his hometown of Belleville, Ill.

home_pitcher_note: Not everything is going well for Carpenter, but this is worth noting: In his last three starts, he has 19 strikeouts and two walks in 19 1/3 innings. If he keeps that up, some good results will surely soon follow.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano gave up one run over eight innings against the Astros but did not get a decision. He's 4-0 with a 2.62 ERA when he works at least six innings. It's been a tough year. He needed two tries to break his bat over his knee after striking out.

home_pitcher_note: Leake got off to a rough start against Milwaukee on Wednesday. He gave up a home run and triple to the first two batters he faced. But after a two-run first, he surrendered just one run on four hits before coming out for a pinch-hitter in the sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is expected to be activated from the DL before this game, for his first start since May 17. He's been sidelined with a bone contusion in his right elbow. This will be Garza's third start this year vs. the Reds. So far, he's 0-1 with a 3.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez went to Triple-A Louisville to regain his fastball command. He needed to refine his mechanics to create a more compact delivery, and in two starts, he was 1-0 with a 1.88 ERA. He walked six in 14 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis notched his first quality start in his last outing against the Astros, his first since April 24, 2010. He's 6-3 with a 3.31 ERA in his career against the Reds and 4-2 at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo was able to keep the ball in the park on Friday, and that proved to be the difference in winning a 2-1 pitchers' duel against the Dodgers. The right-hander has served up 14 homers this year, the second most in the Major Leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster's first start in June was more like his bad April than his 3-1, 3.08 ERA May. He gave up eight hits over five innings, including homers to Lance Berkman and Albert Pujols. He lost to the Reds on May 8 but notched a quality start that outing.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing on June 4 in Pittsburgh Kendrick got the spot start for the Phils, tossing five innings in a 6-3 loss to the Pirates. He allowed four runs on eight hits and was tagged with the loss.
away_pitcher_note: If not for 95-degree heat and Albert Pujols, Wells might have gone deeper in his last start. He gave up three hits -- two to Pujols -- over 5 2/3 innings and did not get a decision. This will be his third start since coming off the DL.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning NL Cy Young winner pitched well enough to stop the Phillies' losing streak in his last outing on Sunday in Pittsburgh. Halladay pitched seven effective innings as Philly snapped a season-high four-game skid.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano was denied a win on Sunday in his last start when the Cardinals rallied for a 10-inning win. He criticized his teammates after the game. It will be interesting to see how they -- and he -- respond.

home_pitcher_note: Lee returned to his dominant self in Monday's 3-0 victory over the Dodgers. He allowed seven hits, one walk and struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings. Lee got knocked around in his previous start against Washington, but had no problems Monday.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Garza's second start since coming off the disabled list. He threw 81 pitches over four innings against the Reds in his last outing, giving up six hits and walking three. He was hitting 94 mph on the radar gun, a good sign.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had one of his worst starts of the season Tuesday in a loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers. He allowed eight hits, four runs, two walks and struck out one in six innings. He had allowed four or more runs just one other time.
away_pitcher_note: Davis is still winless in five starts. He's made eight career starts against the Phillies and is 2-2 with a 3.71 ERA. In his last outing, he gave up seven hits over 4 1/3 innings, and the leadoff batter got on in four of five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster wasn't sure he'd make his last start because of a right hip strain, which he felt during warmups. He may want to re-think getting it fixed. He threw 113 pitches over six innings and got the win against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had no-decisions in his past three starts. He's surrendered 12 hits and five earned runs during this three-game span, but also pitched 19 innings and struck out 15 batters.

home_pitcher_note: Wells' last start was cut short after 2 1/3 innings because of rain. Another problem was pitch count: He threw 53 in the abbreviated outing. This will be his first game against the Brewers since Cactus League play on Feb. 28.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo's six-start winning streak ended with a thud Thursday, when Gallardo allowed 10 hits and threw 96 pitches in four-plus innings of a loss to the Mets. He's 3-1 with a 3.61 ERA in eight starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano had to go deep to give the bullpen a breather in his last start and threw 128 pitches over 6 1/3 innings. He says he's strong enough to handle it. What he also needs to deal with is not walking as many; he walked seven against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: So much for the calls to remove Narveson from the Brewers' rotation. He pitched eight shutout innings against the Cardinals on Friday in a big series-opening win and contributed to the team's eighth shutout this season.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Garza's third start since coming off the DL with a sore right elbow. In his last game against the Phillies, he gave up two runs (one earned) on five hits over six innings. He lost to the Brewers on April 9.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is on a roll. The Brewers are 7-1 in his starts, Greinke has won six straight decisions and he's delivered five quality starts of at least six innings with three or fewer earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis threw 108 pitches over five innings in his last start against the Phillies and walked five. He admitted he made things harder on himself by trying to be too picky with his pitch selection. He can't afford to do that vs. the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia bounced back from a 1 2/3-inning outing against Boston to pitch 6 2/3 strong innings in a win Sunday against Cleveland. He is holding opposing hitters to a .231 average with runners in scoring position on the season.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster pitched a gem in his last start against the Brewers, throwing seven shutout innings. He also struck out seven. Dempster is 0-2 in three career starts against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett went 7 2/3 innings, giving up just one run on five hits in a 1-0 loss to the Indians in his last start. It was his third outing allowing just one run, and he has not been the winning pitcher in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: Wells did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers, giving up three runs on eight hits over six innings and striking out two. This will be his fifth start since coming off the disabled list, and first ever against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia followed the trend of bouncing back after a rough outing against Boston and held Texas to four runs over seven innings in his last start, his fifth win in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander gets the honor of starting the first game of the BP Cup competition against the Cubs, coming off a complete-game loss at Target Field. Floyd allowed four runs on 11 hits, striking out six and walking two in the 117-pitch effort.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano is 5-4 in 14 games (12 starts) against the White Sox. The last time he pitched on the South Side was when he yelled at his teammates in the dugout after a four-run first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Nobody has done it better among AL pitchers against NL competition than Buehrle, who has an Interleague record 24 victories, with five of those coming against the Cubs. Buehrle gave up just one run over seven against the Twins on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Garza discovered how different Wrigley Field is when the wind is blowing out in his last start against the Brewers. He gave up two homers, one wind aided. He's 2-4 with a 3.63 ERA when he goes six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Returning from his second stint on the DL this season, Peavy makes his first start since straining his groin June 5. He struck out nine while giving up just two hits over six scoreless innings in his only rehab start.
away_pitcher_note: Davis picked up his first win of the season and first since May 5, 2010, in his last outing. Manager Mike Quade said the lefty "confounded" the Yankees, holding them to three hits over 7 1/3 scoreless innings, his longest outing of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Out since May 6 with a lat strain, Chen will be activated for this start. He made three rehab starts and figures he's good for at least 100 pitches. Chen gives KC's rotation a veteran lefty with a variety of pitches, arm angles and speeds.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster walked a season-high six batters in his last start, against the Yankees, and took the loss. He's now 3-2 with a 3.22 ERA in his last six starts. He's faced the Royals once -- on June 12, 2002, at Kansas City -- and won.

home_pitcher_note: Duffy's eight start for the Royals since being called up might be his last for a while. Kyle Davies is due back from the disabled list and Duffy likely will return to Omaha to work on his command. Last Sunday at St. Louis, he left with a leg cramp.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Z's second straight start at an AL park, which means he can't hit. He'll probably try to talk Mike Quade into letting him bat somehow. In his last game vs. the White Sox, he struck out five in eight innings and picked up the win.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar again started strong before suffering a mild collapse. He retired the first 11 batters he faced and gave up one hit through 4 2/3 innings. But he allowed five runs over his last 2 1/3 innings and took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Wells did not get a decision in his last start against the Yankees. He gave up four runs on five hits and four walks over six innings. He did throw 101 pitches, the most since he's come off the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Garza did not get a decision in his last start against the White Sox, because it was interrupted by rain. He gave up two runs on four hits over five innings and struck out four. This is a makeup game, necessary because of a rainout on April 27.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin took a no-decision in the Rockies' win over the Indians on Tuesday despite surrendering just one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings. He struggled with command, though, walking six.

home_pitcher_note: Davis took the loss against the White Sox in his last start, going five innings and allowing four runs, three earned. He allowed eight hits, walked two and struck out two, as the Cubs lost, 4-3.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong picked up his fifth win Wednesday by allowing one run over seven innings and snapping the Giants' five-game losing streak. The righty retired the first 12 batters he faced and has allowed two runs or fewer in each of his last nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez has just one start for the Cubs this season, giving up six runs in 4 2/3 innings on May 30 against Houston. Since then, he's given up four runs on nine hits in nine combined innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zito will make his first Major League start in more than two months after a lengthy stint on the disabled list with a right foot sprain. The lefty was nearly untouchable in his last rehab start for Triple-A Fresno, throwing a two-hit shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster took a no-decision in the Cubs' 6-4 win over the Royals on Friday. He went six innings, giving up four runs (two earned). He only ran into trouble in the fourth, giving up a two-run homer and an RBI single.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum returned to form Thursday, striking out 12 (including nine of his last 12 batters) while allowing three hits and two walks in seven innings. It was Lincecum's fourth game this year -- the 30th of his career -- with double-digit strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano wasn't dominant, but still effective in a no-decision against the Royals. He gave up just two runs on eight hits, and worked out of a bases-loaded, one-out mess in the fifth inning. Just one of the hits went for extra bases.
away_pitcher_note: Cain tossed seven shutout innings in a win over Cleveland on Saturday, allowing four hits, a walk and a hit batter while striking out six. Cain at one point retired 14 straight, and he moved within five strikeouts of 1,000 for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Wells got blitzed for four runs in the first inning of a 6-3 loss to Kansas City last Sunday. He allowed hits to the first five batters and walked another before registering an out. He finished six innings, allowing six earned runs on 10 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Despite going at least six innings in each of his last five starts, Jackson is 0-1 with four no-decisions, one of which came in his last start when he tossed seven shutout innings and struck out eight against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is still learning the nuances of Wrigley Field, like when the wind blows out, keep the ball down. He did not get decision on June 21 vs. White Sox as rain interrupted start. He was cruising and had 72 pitches over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Humber carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning of his last start, but eventually picked up the loss after giving up a two-run homer in the seventh inning of a 2-1 loss to the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Lopez's third start for the Cubs. In his last outing against the Giants, he gave up one earned run on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings. His other start was May 30. He did throw 96 pitches; that's about his max.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd picked up a no-decision against the Rockies on Tuesday, allowing two runs over seven innings, in an eventual 13-inning White Sox loss. His 69 strikeouts  rank second on the team behind Edwin Jackson.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann capped off a phenomenal June by recording his club-record 11th straight quality start in Anaheim, but it was wasted by the Nationals' lack of offense. Washington has given him a total of 12 runs in his last seven outings.
away_pitcher_note: This was supposed to be Ryan Dempster's start, but he's been scratched because his back tightened up. Coleman is 2-1 with a 3.90 ERA in five starts with Triple-A Iowa. In his last start, he gave up three runs over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Davey Johnson indicated that Detwiler, a left-hander who is now with Triple-A Syracuse, is the leading candidate to pitch Tuesday. Detwiler pitched two shutout innings on Saturday against Indianapolis before being pulled from the game.
away_pitcher_note: This would've been Carlos Zambrano's turn, but he is on the disabled list with lower back soreness. Ortiz, 38, was 6-3 with a 4.26 ERA in 16 starts at Triple-A Iowa. This will be his first MLB start since May 19, 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny lasted seven innings on Friday, allowing one unearned run on six hits. Pittsburgh scored its lone run in the third, thanks to some shoddy defense from the Nats. It was smooth sailing after that for Gorzelanny.
away_pitcher_note: Wells was cruising through six innings in his last start, including a three-pitch sixth, but then served up four runs in the seventh and took the loss against the White Sox. He's 0-for-3 in seven starts since coming off the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had to be nearly perfect on Saturday to win against the Pirates, but he ended up with a no-decision. His only blip came in the first inning, when he allowed two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off a complete-game loss to the White Sox on Saturday. He allowed just one run on four hits and struck out seven while taking a no-hitter into the sixth. Said A.J. Pierzynski: "That's the best I've ever seen Matt Garza throw."

home_pitcher_note: McDonald has not allowed more than three earned runs in a start since May 13, and has lowered his ERA from 6.20 to 4.40 since. In his last start, against the Nationals on Saturday, he allowed two runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez threw seven shutout innings against the White Sox in his last start, giving up two hits and striking out three. He also was efficient, throwing 75 pitches. If Lopez can get ground-ball outs, he's effective.

home_pitcher_note: Correia picked up his 11th win Sunday and is tied for the most victories in the Major Leagues. He accounts for 25 percent of the Pirates' 44 wins.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster skipped a turn Monday against the Nationals because of discomfort in his stomach and core. He threw on Thursday, and is good to go. This will be his last start before the break and a chance to enter the second half on a positive note.

home_pitcher_note: After a string of hard-luck losses to begin the season, Maholm has won four of his last six decisions. Against Houston on Monday, he allowed three runs (one earned) in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first Major League start since May 19, 2010, Ortiz gave up three runs (two earned) on seven hits and struck out seven over six innings. He is the 10th different starter Cubs have used this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garza's last two starts were total opposites. He threw a complete game against the White Sox and lost on July 2, and followed that with his second shortest outing on July 7 against the Nationals, which the team won.
away_pitcher_note: Florida's most consistent starter in the first half, Sanchez often pitched in hard luck, as he last won on June 10 vs. Arizona. He has struggled his last two starts, allowing 12 runs in 7 2/3 innings. He is 1-2 (6.91 ERA) in three starts vs. Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start in nine days, Dempster gave up three runs on seven hits over five innings against the Pirates, and felt that he should have done more. He argued with manager Mike Quade about being lifted after 87 pitches, but they've made peace.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco finished up his first half with a complete-game win over Houston. He struck out eight. He has two complete games in his last three starts. With 60 career wins, Nolasco is now eight behind Dontrelle Willis for most in franchise history.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano has been on the disabled list since July 1 with lower back soreness. He threw four innings in a rehab start with Class A Peoria on July 8. He has done better at home, posting a 3.83 ERA at Wrigley this season.
away_pitcher_note: In two July starts, Vazquez is 1-0 with a 1.38 ERA. The right-hander has allowed just two earned runs in 13 innings. Opponents are hitting .235 in those games, as he's struck out seven and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is looking for a reset button to erase the first half. His only win came in his first start on April 4, and then he went on the DL after that with a strained forearm. In his last outing on July 6, he struggled against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad opens the second half having won three of four starts. The right-hander is coming off a win over the Astros, in which he gave up three runs in six innings while striking out six and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez is 1-1 with a 4.03 ERA in five starts with the Cubs. In his last outing before the break, he gave up three runs on eight hits over six innings against the Pirates. He did face the Phillies earlier but that was in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is making his first start since pitching two perfect innings in last week's All-Star Game. The extra rest figures to help deep in the season, as he leads the league in innings pitched. He threw seven scoreless innings June 10 against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Garza deserved better in his last start against the Marlins. He threw seven shutout innings and left with a lead, but the bullpen imploded. Garza now is 3-1 in his last five home starts with a 2.62 ERA, including a complete game.
away_pitcher_note: Looking for his 10th win, Lee is the beneficiary of extra rest after pitching two innings in the All-Star Game. He allowed one earned run on four hits with seven strikeouts in eight innings in his only other outing against the Cubs this year.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster opened the second half by throwing eight shutout innings vs. the Marlins, striking out nine. There was no arguing, either, with manager Mike Quade over how long he would pitch. Dempster is 4-2 with a 1.82 ERA in his last eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Worley has been producing far more than the Phillies could have hoped when injuries to Roy Oswalt and Joe Blanton pinched the rotation. Worley hasn't allowed more than one earned run in any of his five starts since returning last month.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's second start since coming off the disabled list. In his first start against the Marlins, his velocity was good, but his command was off, and he gave up a season-high eight runs on seven hits over 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his most recent start, against the Pirates, Norris allowed four runs for the second time this month after doing so just once in June. He also surrendered three home runs, but the Astros won, 6-4. Norris hasn't lost a decision in July.

home_pitcher_note: Wells has not won a game since his first start of the season April 4. He's been inconsistent, and his last start was no exception, as he gave up three runs in the first, then settled down. He's struggling with his offspeed pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a season-high 11 batters in his previous start, against the Pirates, despite allowing four runs in an Astros loss. He has allowed four runs or more in each of his starts in July.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has been the tough-luck starter for the Cubs. He has 10 quality starts, yet only four wins. He should've gotten the "W" in his last outing against the Phillies when he threw seven-plus innings and gave up one run.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles tossed 8 1/3 innings in his most recent start, allowing just three hits through his first eight frames, yet he is winless after his first nine Major League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson watched his two-run lead slip away in Arizona after an early call to the bullpen, but he has a good matchup on deck, as he's 5-0 with a 3.38 ERA in 11 appearances (four starts) against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster failed to rebound from a 2-0 first-inning deficit in his last start, lasting just three innings against the Phillies. He gave up six runs on seven hits and three walks in the abbreviated start, throwing 86 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Two fastballs spoiled an otherwise solid start in Arizona, but Greinke may finally be in a groove. Each of his last three outings has been a "quality" start, including his loss on Thursday, which was decided by two D-backs home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano picked up his first win since returning from his stint on the disabled list on Friday against the Astros. The right-hander threw six innings, giving up two runs on nine hits and fanning three.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum credited a between-starts mechanical adjustment for his seven-inning gem against the Giants on Friday. He shortened his delivery to actually reduce the movement on his fastball, aiding his command.
away_pitcher_note: Wells earned a victory for the first time in over three months as the Cubs defeated the Astros on Saturday, 5-1. Sidelined by an injury for almost two months, Wells has struggled for the majority of the season but has shown signs of finding form.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson will make his first start in a Cardinals uniform and his second against the Cubs this year after being traded to St. Louis on Wednesday. The right-hander has won three of his last four decisions, including a win over the Cubs on July 1.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's record does not reflect how well he's pitched. In his last outing vs. Astros, it was the sixth time he left the game with a lead and didn't factor in the decision. He's given up two earned runs or less in 10 starts but is 1-3.

home_pitcher_note:
Lohse allowed two runs on four hits in five innings of work on July 24, taking a no-decision in St. Louis' loss to the Pirates. He struck out four and walked none, throwing just 64 
pitches in his first start since coming down with a finger ailment.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez has thrown three quality starts in a row and has given up four earned runs over 19 2/3 innings. He's been the surprise ace lately, throwing six innings or more in his last three games. His last win was over the Phillies and Roy Halladay.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook's sinker has been working in his last two starts as the right-hander has induced a total of 31 ground-ball outs over 14 innings en route to a pair of wins. He was tagged for five runs in 2 1/3 innings against the Cubs on May 11.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster posted a quality start in his last outing against the Brewers, giving up three runs over six innings. He lost to Cardinals on June 3, giving up six runs on eight hits over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: On a night when the Pirates needed a lengthy outing, Maholm stepped up with a 109-pitch, seven-inning start last time out. He allowed one run and has now allowed one or fewer in six of his last 10 games. He's been especially strong at home.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano didn't get much offensive support in his last start against the Brewers, a 2-0 loss. He faced the Pirates in his first start on April 2, but did not get a decision. Zambrano has two wins in his past 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Only two of Correia's wins have come at home, but he is coming off a bounce-back start. After allowing 15 earned runs in 14 1/3 July innings, Correia ended the month with a 6 1/3-inning performance in which he allowed only one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: Wells had a tough time with Ryan Braun in his last start as the Brewers outfielder had three hits off him, including a homer. He gave up four runs on eight hits over six innings. Wells has not faced the Pirates this season.

home_pitcher_note: Morton needs to rediscover the sinker that helped him be so successful early in the year. Lately, he's been knocked around hard. He has a 7.18 ERA in his last eight starts and has not pitched six innings in any of them.
away_pitcher_note: Garza finished July 0-2 with a 3.82 ERA, with four quality starts and no wins to show for his efforts. He was roughed up in his last outing against the Cardinals on Friday, giving up six runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald suffered his first loss in nine starts on Saturday and lasted just five innings in the contest. He gave up a season-high 10 hits, largely because he was around the zone so much in an effort to limit his walks.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez took the loss in his last start against the Cardinals, although that was his first in 12 days. He had trouble getting a feel for his changeup, which may be because of the layoff. He wasn't sharp, giving up six runs on eight hits over 4 1/3.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has been hurt by home runs in his last two starts, allowing five in 11 1/3 innings. But the Braves won all five of the games he started in June. In his last start, he allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is 0-4 with a 12.27 ERA in his past four games, and has struggled to get a feel for his offspeed pitches. What the Cubs want him to avoid doing is trying to muscle his pitches over the plate. He's still learning.

home_pitcher_note: In two starts since returning from Triple-A, Jurrjens has allowed three runs in 13 1/3 innings. He came within an out in his last start of recording back-to-back quality starts for the first time since last July.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad has been pitching at Triple-A Iowa since opening the season with the Cubs and going 0-6 with a 7.46 ERA in eight starts. In eight starts at Iowa, he was 2-3 with a 4.44 ERA, giving up 25 earned runs on 59 hits and 12 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado has been inconsistent, and the four starts he made since his last win on June 6 have been no different. He has pitched beyond the fifth just once in those four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm pitched a gem in his last start, giving up four hits over 8 1/3 innings. He struck out six and ended an eight-game winless streak with the win. The difference? He was able to use his curve and slider more effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Minor allowed at least four runs for the third start in a row Saturday, but manager Fredi Gonzalez said he thought Minor had taken a step forward in his win over the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Garza had to battle the heat in his last outing, lasting 5 1/3 innings against the Astros. He will miss Wrigley Field. He's 2-1 with a 2.50 ERA in six home starts. He struggled with his slider, and needs to keep the pitch count down.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets considered skipping Santana's final start before the All-Star break, resting his surgically repaired shoulder. But with Santana coming off eight shutout innings in L.A. and feeling strong, he will wrap up his first half vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wood has won his past three starts and has not given up a run in 18 2/3 innings, the longest stretch by a Cubs lefty since Ted Lilly had a 19-inning scoreless streak Sept. 10-20, 2008. Wood also has not given up a home run in 28 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Defensive errors, more than his own mistakes, cost Gee in Sunday's loss to the Dodgers. He still pitched around them to record a quality start, saying he felt much better than he did in his prior outing vs. the Cubs, who knocked Gee out after five.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Samardzija found his split-finger pitch, and the result was a career-high 11 strikeouts against the Braves. He gave up four hits over seven innings for the win, which helped to erase a dismal 0-4 June.

home_pitcher_note: Niese allowed just one run against the Phillies Tuesday -- a second inning homer to Carlos Ruiz -- and made his third straight quality start. In his last three starts, he is 3-0 and has combined to allow just four earned runs over 21 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster will return from the DL to finish the first half. He won his last three starts before being sidelined and has a scoreless inning streak of 22, the longest by a Cubs pitcher since Carlos Zambrano's 22-inning stretch in May 2004.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm won his final two starts of the first half, giving up one run on 12 hits over 14 1/3 innings. The left-hander has definitely thrived at Wrigley, posting a 4-2 record and 3.26 ERA at home.

Dempster came off the DL and extended his scoreless inning streak to 27 innings against the Mets. His start Sunday was his first off the DL, and he cruised through five innings. He's also won four straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is making his first start since being placed on the disabled list on June 23. He felt tightness in his shoulder and could not get loose for his start on June 22. Saunders stared an Arizona League game last Sunday in preparation for return.

home_pitcher_note: After opening the season strong, Garza has stumbled, and his season has been a roller-coaster ride. In his last start before the break, he lasted four innings vs. the Braves, giving up three homers. On the plus side, he's 2-1 with a 2.50 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill won his last start before the break, holding the Dodgers to three runs over seven innings. He has made just one career start against the Cubs and at Wrigley Field. In that game, he allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wood won his last four starts leading up to the break, giving up three earned runs over 26 2/3 innings. It's an encouraging trend after posting a 5.94 ERA in his first three games. He's faced the Marlins once and lost, lasting 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After an up-and-down first half, Sanchez seeks his first win since June 27, when he beat the Cards. He is coming off back-to-back no-decisions. The righty was on the hook for a win in St. Louis on July 8, but Miami lost in the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija finished the first half with a loss to the Mets, giving up three runs on seven hits over seven innings. He's been able to make in-game adjustments, not get rattled and impressed the staff with his maturity.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson matched his career high of 11 hits allowed in his last start, a loss to Washington. On April 17, Johnson faced the Cubs in Miami, settling for a no-decision. He gave up two runs in seven innings that day.
summary: 2012-07-18 - Miami Marlins @ Chicago Cubs (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Maholm stayed in a groove on Friday against Arizona, allowing one run in seven innings to earn his third straight win. The southpaw has surrendered two runs in his last four appearances (three starts), spanning 22 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Make it four straight starts in which Buehrle has gone at least seven innings and struck out at least seven. The lefty has given up three earned runs over 28 2/3 innings in that stretch. On April 18, he beat the Cubs in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse surrendered just two runs on eight hits in his last start, but the Cardinals lost and the right-hander was awarded a no-decision. He has gone at least five innings in every one of his 19 outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster's career-high scoreless innings streak is at 33, the most for a Cubs pitcher since Ken Holtzman in 1969. He hasn't allowed a run since May 30, spanning five starts, and has lowered his ERA to 1.86.

home_pitcher_note: Two eighth-inning runs left Westbrook to shoulder a loss in his last outing, which was otherwise a fairly strong outing. All four runs he allowed came with two outs, and Westbrook pitched into the eighth inning for just the second time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off a win over the D-backs in which he threw seven shutout innings. He's fared much better at Wrigley, posting a 3-1 record and 2.12 ERA, compared to a 2-6 mark and 5.67 ERA in 10 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Despite not picking up the win, Lynn was dominant in his last start. Pitching seven innings against the Brewers, Lynn struck out 10 and surrendered just one run while not allowing a walk for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wood's four-game win streak was snapped in his last start, as the Fish roughed him up. The lefty gave up a career-high-tying eight runs in 4 2/3 innings, including two homers. He stopped throwing offspeed pitches, and can't do that to be effective.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard came out of the 11-day layoff surrounding the All-Star break sharp on Tuesday, holding Colorado to two runs in the longest (6 2/3 innings) of his last six starts. Remarkably, a sixth win would match his most since 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija needs to keep his pitch count down. In his last start against the Marlins, he was pulled after throwing 97 pitches over five innings. He has one win in his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: After not giving up more than three runs in any of his first 16 starts, McDonald has allowed four-plus in three of the last five. He hasn't had his putaway slider of late, but he has become a fierce competitor who doesn't give in.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm, who pitched seven seasons with the Pirates before signing with the Cubs this offseason, makes his second start in Pittsburgh this year. He took a no-decision on May 26, but is riding a four-game winning streak in which he has an 0.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The righty, who could win only on the road last season, has a superior record (4-3) at PNC Park. Correia will try to add on to his career-long streak of five straight wins. But he has needed support for that: He has a 4.05 ERA across the stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster's scoreless-innings streak was snapped in an eight-pitch span in the first inning vs. the Cardinals on Friday as they scored three quick runs. He recovered, and gave up three hits after that. He's 0-1 vs. Pirates this year.

home_pitcher_note: This would've been Matt Garza's spot, but he's being skipped after coming out of his last game with cramping in his right elbow. Wood lost to the Cardinals on Sunday, giving up six earned runs over six innings, including back-to-back homers.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn is 3-0 with a 0.94 ERA in three outings against the Cubs this season. He threw six shutout innings against Chicago on Sunday -- his fourth scoreless start of the season -- and he's allowed one earned run in his last three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off his best outing, in which he held the Pirates to one hit, an infield single, over eight innings. He had good command, mixed his pitches well and kept his pitch count down. Let's see what he does for an encore.
away_pitcher_note: Despite turning in six straight quality starts, Kelly is 1-3 over that span. He's allowed an unearned run in each of his last four outings, but homers haven't helped his case, either. Kelly's given up three-run jacks in two of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm is on quite a roll. He's posted five straight starts of at least six innings in which he's given up one or no runs. That's a first by a Cubs left-hander since 1918. He's also won all five. And he loves pitching at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright outdueled Clayton Kershaw to earn his eighth win on Tuesday. His 7 1/3-inning effort was his longest since tossing a complete game on May 22. Wainwright has pitched well for most of two months now but has run into his share of lousy luck.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Red Sox for cash considerations on July 19, Germano will be making his first start for the Cubs in his second appearance for the team. He pitched three innings in relief on July 21. He was starting at Triple-A Pawtucket.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard held the Cubs to one run on two hits during his last start, throwing seven stellar innings without being rewarded with a win. He threw 113 pitches in the outing, his most in a start since August 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Coleman gets the call in place of the departed Ryan Dempster, who was traded to the Rangers earlier on Tuesday. This will be Coleman's first start of the season, after he started 17 times for Chicago last year.
away_pitcher_note: The 13-year veteran just keeps rolling along; a 13th win would match the second-most of his career, with two months of the season to go. His 14 quality starts do not include his May 25 turn vs. the Cubs; he blanked them, but only for 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals roughed up Wood in his last start as he became the first Major League pitcher to give up home runs in five consecutive innings. In his last five starts, Wood is 2-3 with a 7.36 ERA, and he has given up 10 home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has had a wicked breaking pitch through a recent hot stretch, using it primarily to notch 29 strikeouts in his last 34 innings. Trying to close out another strong July (2-0, 2.67) after posting a 2.06 ERA in five starts in July last season.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley dismissed the notion that two weeks off to rest his elbow has turned around his season, but he has delivered two of his better starts after suffering through a five-game losing streak.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija notched his 11th quality start in his last outing, but did not get a decision. He is 2-1 with a 1.91 ERA in his last five starts, giving up seven runs over 33 innings in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw showed what makes him special by rebounding from one of his worst starts of the season in St. Louis with his second shutout of the year, this one against the Giants to complete a sweep.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad was called up from Triple-A Iowa after Paul Maholm and Ryan Dempster were traded. He's still looking for that first Major League win since July 10. In his last game for Iowa, he scattered four hits over eight shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton makes his Dodgers debut after being traded from the Phils on Friday, as Aaron Harang's start is moved back to Tuesday. Six of Blanton's last eight outings have been quality starts, including a July 16 win over the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Germano picked up the win in his first start for the Cubs Monday, giving up two runs on four hits and two walks over five innings vs. the Pirates. It helped that the Cubs scored nine runs in the fifth. He's 0-4 with a 5.93 ERA in six games vs. L.A.

home_pitcher_note: Stults has not made a start since June 3 thanks to a stint on the DL with a strained lat, followed by time spent as the Padres' long reliever. He is 1-2 with a 3.26 ERA in five starts, and takes the released Kip Wells' spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Wood lost his last start on a pitch he threw and another he didn't, as he served up a homer and another run scored on a balk. He's lost four straight after winning four in a row. With Ryan Dempster and Paul Maholm gone, the Cubs need Wood to step up.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf struggled in his last outing, yielding six runs in just 1 2/3 innings against the Reds. Prior to that, he had made three straight quality starts, but has a 6.07 ERA in six starts this year. Ohlendorf turns 30 Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Raley's MLB debut. A sixth-round pick in 2009, he was the Cubs' Pitcher of the Month for July after posting a 2.12 ERA (seven earned runs over 29 2/3 innings). He walked 12 and struck out 28, holding opponents to a .254 average.

home_pitcher_note: Padres manager Bud Black didn't think Richard had his best stuff Friday, which is telling, given that Richard gave up just one run in seven innings. He has 13 quality starts this year, and he is among the NL leaders in innings pitched (152 2/3).
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija had a 1.91 ERA in five games in July but gave up five runs in his last start against the Dodgers. He didn't have good command of his split-finger, which has been his out pitch, and it showed.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad is winless in his last 21 starts, but his last outing against the Dodgers was his best with the Cubs. He threw with conviction and mixed his pitches well. The tough part was he was matched up against Clayton Kershaw.
away_pitcher_note: While he didn't earn the win, Leake tossed a successful outing Saturday against Pittsburgh, allowing four runs on six hits through six innings, striking out seven. He allowed multiple home runs for the sixth time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Germano scattered three hits over 5 1/3 innings in his last start, then ran out of gas after 77 pitches. He didn't walk a batter and struck out three, all encouraging signs. This is his chance to make a good impression for next year.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey has given up 10 earned runs over 8 1-3 innings in his last two starts. He's given up 18 hits and three walks in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has lost five straight starts but his last outing was a quality start against the Padres, his first since July 6. He gave up two runs on five hits over six innings and escaped some jams. This will be his first start against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: Home runs hurt Arroyo in his last start. He gave up three in one inning to the Brewers. Last year, he allowed a Major-League leading 46 homers. This year he's given up 20 in 22 starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his debut, Raley gave up seven runs over four innings. He'd given up just seven runs over 29 2/3 innings in five starts in July, which earned him honors as the Cubs' Minor League pitcher of the month. The Cubs can only hope the jitters are gone.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto had his five-game winning streak snapped in his last start, when Milwaukee's Mike Fiers took a perfect game into the seventh. Cueto was solid against the Brewers, allowing six hits and three runs in seven innings while fanning nine.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija gave up one run over seven innings vs. the Padres in his last outing, but that wasn't good enough for a win as the offense struggled. He's 2-3 with a 2.58 ERA in his last seven starts. He lost to the Astros May 23, despite a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga struggled in his last two outings, walking 13 total batters. The 30-year-old has pitched into the sixth inning in all three of his starts with the Astros, but hasn't been able to get out of the inning.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad tossed his second consecutive quality start his last time out, but once again didn't earn a win -- increasing his winless streak to 22 starts. The good news? He's improving, and facing the team he last beat: Houston on July 10, 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell, who leads the National League in innings by a rookie, has been the Astros' most reliable starter this season. He's given up two or fewer runs in each of his last six starts, going 2-2 over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Germano didn't get much help from his defense in his last start, against the Reds, giving up six runs (four earned) in 5 2/3 innings as he took the loss. He has a 4.50 ERA and has yet to complete six innings in three starts with the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: After his ERA spiked to 5.33 on July 20, Norris has been better in his last four starts, posting a 3.46 ERA in that span. He's struck out seven in three of his last four starts, and averages 9.2 strikeouts per nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo lasted eight innings for the third time this season Saturday, holding the Cubs to two runs on five hits for his eighth win. He had allowed nine earned runs in his previous 11 1/3 innings, but is now one win shy of matching last season's mark.
away_pitcher_note: Wood gets another chance to beat his former team after the Cubs' bullpen blew his chance last weekend. In that outing, Wood tossed seven innings of one-run ball and tied a career-high with eight strikeouts. He also allowed five hits and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was stellar again Sunday, hurling eight shutout innings and allowing just three hits for his 15th win. He may get the call for the early half of the doubleheader Saturday, as he's 10-0 with a 1.55 ERA in 12 day games this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his previous start, Samardzija matched his career K high, with 11. He held the Astros to four hits over seven innings and finally got some offensive support. He can only hope he gets the second game; he's 5-4 with a 2.57 ERA in 11 night outings.

home_pitcher_note: Redmond will be recalled from Triple-A Louisville to start Game 2. Even though he's been called up three previous times, it will be his MLB debut. Since being traded from the Braves organization in July, Redmond is 2-3 with a 3.41 ERA in five games.
away_pitcher_note: Raley was recalled from Triple-A Iowa after being resigned Monday. Raley lost to the Reds in his second Major League start Sunday in Chicago, throwing six solid innings, giving up three runs on five hits, two of which were homers.

home_pitcher_note: Latos continued his hot August, silencing the Mets through seven innings, giving up five hits in a no-decision outing Tuesday. The righty hasn't lost in a month and is 1-0 with a 0.43 ERA in three August starts.
away_pitcher_note: The wait continues for Volstad, who now has gone 23 consecutive starts without a win. He lost his last outing to the Astros, giving up four runs on eight hits over five innings. He struggled with command and his pitches weren't very "crisp."

home_pitcher_note: Searching for the first win of his career, Rogers is coming off a five-run, seven-hit performance against the Rockies. Still, for the third time in four starts, he was in line for the win before the bullpen blew a save.
away_pitcher_note: Germano posted his first quality start of the season on Wednesday, giving up two runs over 6 1/3 innings vs. the Astros. Opposing teams keep calling him a "crafty right-hander." Germano won't overpower hitters, but he does keep them off-balance.

home_pitcher_note: Winless in 15 starts and six relief appearances this season, Estrada has been frustrated with his last two trips to the mound. He gave up four runs and didn't make it past the fifth inning in either outing.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin will make his Major League debut against the Brewers. He had a 2.63 ERA in his first five starts at Triple-A Iowa, scuffled in June, but rebounded, and has given up four earned runs over 18 2/3 innings in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Ron Roenicke said Gallardo's curveball was the best it's been this season on Friday, when he allowed one run on four hits in seven innings against the Phillies. He's given up just six runs in his last 28 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wood gave up six earned runs in five innings Friday in Cincinnati, after holding the same Reds club to one run in seven innings less than week earlier. He is looking for his first win since July 6 and has allowed six or more runs in four outings over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off a loss to the Reds in which he gave up four runs over five innings. He will be happy to be back at Wrigley, where he's 4-3 with a 3.36 ERA in 10 starts. This has been a tough month: He's 1-3 with a 4.07 ERA in August.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz battled through four innings and 76 pitches without good command Sunday, his fifth straight start of four innings or more.  He allowed just two runs (one earned) on three hits and four walks (one intentional) while striking out three.

home_pitcher_note: Raley is coming off his first Major League win, holding the Reds to four runs over 5 1/3 innings on Saturday. He posted a quality start in his only outing at Wrigley Field on Aug. 12.
away_pitcher_note: White gave up one run on just three hits to the Mets on Monday, but a 29-pitch first inning led to his departure after just four innings and 83 pitches. White has lowered his season ERA by nearly a point since rejoining the Rockies on Aug. 2.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad's winless streak now has reached 24 straight starts. The right-hander has a career 2-3 record and 5.64 ERA against the Rockies. This month, he's posted his lowest ERA at 4.88, giving up 13 earned runs over 24 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up just one run against the Mets on Tuesday in his return from the DL, his first start since May 1. He demonstrated total control over his fastball -- which he lacked earlier in the year -- and gave up just four hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Germano will face the Brewers for the second straight game. In his last start, he gave up seven runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings and took the loss. He's done better at Wrigley, posting a 3.18 ERA in four games.
away_pitcher_note: It took 16 starts, but Estrada finally earned his first win of the year on Tuesday against the Cubs. It was arguably his best outing of the season, as he tossed six shutout innings, surrendered two hits and struck out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Wood lost to the Brewers in his last start, but drew praise from Ryan Braun, who said the lefty threw a cutter "that's tough to differentiate." Braun did hit an RBI double and home run off Wood, so he figured him out.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo threw seven innings for the fifth straight game on Wednesday, when he allowed just two solo home runs against the Cubs. The 26-year-old righty is 5-0 with a 2.02 ERA since Zack Greinke was traded at the end of July

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija looks to extend his string of deep outings after going seven more innings in three of his last four outings. In his last start against Colorado, Samardzija burned through 60 pitches in three innings but made it through seven.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers 6 2/3 inning, three-run effort in Pittsburgh was a bounce-back after he allowed 12 runs over seven innings in his previous two starts. He also logged his first Major League hit, a bunt single that snapped an 0-for-22.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Raley's fifth big league start, and the Cubs are going to monitor his innings. Don't expect him to go more than five. In his last start, he gave up two runs on five hits against the Rockies. He has a 4.09 ERA in two home games.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum looked sharp in his return from a two-month stint on the disabled list before coming unraveled after an error in the fifth inning at Pittsburgh. The Brewers would like to trade him before Aug. 31 if they can.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad doesn't have to worry about the streak any more. He ended a 24-start winless streak in his last game, picking up the win over the Rockies as he threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings. He has a 3.82 ERA in five starts in August.
away_pitcher_note: Usually dominant at home and not one to give free passes, Bumgarner walked four as he allowed four runs in 6 1/3 innings in the Giants' 7-3 loss to the Braves in his last start. He is 1-1 with a 2.08 ERA in two career starts at the Friendly Confines.

home_pitcher_note: Germano will be glad to be finished with the Brewers. He lost to them in back-to-back starts, giving up 12 runs over 9 2/3 innings combined. He's had trouble getting through the batting order the second and third time as teams are figuring him out.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum searched for his rhythm in his last outing, allowing three runs in five innings against the Braves. He allowed two runs in a 32-pitch first inning, and he has now allowed 25 first-inning runs in 27 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wood posted his 11th quality start on Tuesday, yet also suffered his eighth straight loss. He is 0-8 with a 6.66 ERA in his last nine starts but has given up three runs or less in five of his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: After winning just once in eight starts between June 24 and Aug. 6, Cain has gone 3-0 with a 1.82 ERA in his last four outings. He threw 118 pitches in his last start, his most in any start since he logged 125 in his June 13 perfect game.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler won his last start, Wednesday in Miami. He lasted 5 2/3 innings and allowed three runs on four hits. Detwiler was 3-2 in August with one no-decision. He'll face the Cubs, against whom he is 1-1 with a 4.35 ERA in 10 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija picked up his team-leading 15th quality start in his last outing against the Brewers, striking out 10 without allowing a walk. He has thrown a career-high 158 2/3 innings so far, and will be watched closely as the season wraps up.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson was brilliant in his last start, allowing one unearned run over eight innings of four-hit ball in a series-opening win over the Cardinals. He finished with 10 strikeouts, giving him 139 this season and and 29 over his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Rusin's second big league start. He made his ML debut on Aug. 21 against the Brewers, giving up one run on one hit and two walks over five innings. At Triple-A Iowa, the lefty was 8-9 with a 4.55 ERA over 25 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez tossed the first shutout of his career in a 10-0 win Friday over the Cardinals. The lefty allowed only five hits while striking out eight and walking three, lowering his ERA to 3.10, third among Nationals' starters.
away_pitcher_note: After going 24 starts without a win, Volstad has won two in a row. He picked up a win against the Giants on Friday, giving up two runs over 5 2/3 innings. He's walked three or fewer in each of his 15 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann surrendered a career-high eight runs in his shortest start of the year Saturday, lasting only 3 2/3 innings in a 10-9 loss to the Cards. He attributed his struggles to leaving too many pitches over the middle of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Germano has lost three in a row. He gave up five runs over five innings to the Giants in his last outing at Wrigley Field, although most of the damage came in a four-run first inning. He has yet to win on the road in two starts (0-2, 6.92 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Burnett shrugs off the possibility, but he has to win his last five starts, beginning with this one, to reach 20 for the first time in his career. He comes off his first quality start of the last five, but is winless in last three.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is looking for his first win since July 6. He's 0-8 in his last 10 starts, but has not given up more than three earned runs in six of his last seven outings, dating to Aug. 1.

home_pitcher_note: The good McDonald is scheduled to show up, as he has alternated great-ghastly starts for the last month. He was rocked for a career-high four homers in only 2 2/3 innings in last outing, in Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija threw seven innings in his last start, a one-run, seven-hit gem against the Nationals on Sept. 3. He ultimately earned a loss as the Cubs fell, 2-1. With his innings count at 165 2/3, the Cubs could soon shut down Samardzija.

home_pitcher_note: Locke hopes for more consistency in his second start than he had against Houston on Monday, when he started off 18 of 23 batters with strikes but allowed five runs in five innings. Left-handed hitters are 4-for-8 off the southpaw.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin, a 25-year-old rookie, made his second career start on Sept. 4 against the Nationals, when he allowed five runs on eight hits in just one inning. After the game, manager Dale Sveum lamented Rusin's lack of a solid breaking ball.

away_pitcher_note: Gee had been improving in increments before taking a sizable step backward Tuesday in St. Louis, giving up six runs (five earned) on nine hits in four innings. He was 1-1 with a 3.46 ERA in two starts last year against the Cubs.

away_pitcher_note: Samardzija returns to PNC Park, where he won on Opening Day. In that game, he whiffed nine and held the Bucs to two hits in eight shutout innings. He didn't get another win, though, until his last start vs. the Rockies. His splitter is his key pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo felt that he wasn't pinpoint sharp in his previous start, vs. the Phillies on Saturday, but he was definitely effective, with 22 of 29 first-pitch strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman has been one of the game's best pitchers during his last five outings. He has tossed five consecutive quality starts, during which he's 4-0 with a 1.27 ERA and .192 average against, and has allowed one earned run in his last 19 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Garza was limited to 80-90 pitches in his '13 debut, his first start since July 21. He looked sharp over five innings, giving up one hit and striking out five. His fastball hit 95 mph on the gun.

away_pitcher_note: Samardzija notched another quality start in his last outing but once again went without a win. He held the Pirates to three hits in seven innings, striking out eight. He is 0-2 in four games (one start) against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Sale is determined to take the mound against the Cubs, after having his last start skipped because of a bout of mild tendinitis in the back of his pitching shoulder. He has thrown 23 straight scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson gave up four runs on six hits and struck out six over three innings in his last start but his outing ended early because of rain. He's 1-4 vs. the White Sox, who he pitched for from 2010-11.

away_pitcher_note: It was a great first step for the left-hander, who allowed three runs on four hits over six-plus innings Friday in his first start since May 19, 2012. Danks struck out five, didn't issue a walk and threw 56 of 76 pitches for strikes vs. the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Wood's streak of quality starts ended in his last start. The lefty had gone at least six innings and given up three runs or fewer in nine straight games to open the season, but the Reds ended that. He admitted to not executing in his final frame.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander recorded his 14th career complete game and seventh with the White Sox, missing a shutout by two outs, when Derek Dietrich went deep to tie the game. Peavy has fanned at least five in all nine starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garza was frustrated after his first start when he only lasted five innings. In his last outing against the Reds, he was pulled after throwing 92 pitches over four innings. He did strike out seven, but also gave up four runs in one frame.
away_pitcher_note: Miley was touched up for seven runs in just 3 2/3 innings his last time out, against the Padres, matching the shortest start of his young career. All of the runs charged to the southpaw came with two outs as he lost his third consecutive game.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off his first shutout, a two-hitter against the White Sox. He struck out eight and was efficient, throwing 108 pitches. He altered his mechanics and made a slight adjustment to his hands, which has helped his fastball command.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy had his last start pushed back due to a cut on his right index finger he suffered while washing dishes. In his last outing, Kennedy surrendered four runs (three earned) in six innings vs. the Rockies.

away_pitcher_note: Corbin has won each of his last six starts and delivered quality starts in all 10 of his outings this season. His only other career appearance against the Cubs came last July, when he tossed one perfect inning against them.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver will make just his second start since returning from a fractured left elbow. In his return from the disabled list, the Angels ace allowed one run on five hits in six innings.
