home_pitcher_note: Vargas has been the Angels' best pitcher of late, going at least seven innings and giving up no more than two runs in each of his past four starts. Dating back to April 23, the 30-year-old is 5-1 with a 2.48 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Garza found himself in his third start of the season, holding the D-backs to two runs in seven innings. He pounded the zone and let his defense work, something he didn't do in his previous two starts. He hasn't faced the Angels since 2010.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano set a season high with 11 strikeouts and just one walk over six innings in Saturday's loss to Cincinnati. He dominated the Cubs on May 22, turning in seven shutout innings and allowing just two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija followed an eight-inning shutout of the Pirates on Opening Day with seven innings of one-run ball in a hard-luck loss on May 22. He struck out 11 -- including six straight -- in 6 1/3 innings in his last outing against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett could not keep the ball in the yard on Monday, surrendering three home runs for the first time since he was with the Yankees. He struck out 10 Cubs on Opening Day, his only other meeting with Chicago this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson is 1-7 with a 7.87 ERA in nine career starts at Wrigley Field after losing his last outing one week ago to the D-backs. He gave up 12 hits, walked three and was charged with four wild pitches in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Locke struggled with his fastball his last time out, using his off-speed stuff to escape a number of high-stress situations. He needed 103 pitches, one fewer than his season high, to get through 5 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Bailey avoided major trouble against the Rockies on Tuesday, limiting Colorado to three runs, all of which were scored in the second inning. He proceeded to retire 13 a row and put himself in line for the win before the Reds blew a 4-3 lead.

home_pitcher_note: Garza did not get a decision in his last start against the Angels, giving up four runs over 6 1/3 innings. This will be his second start vs. the Reds. He lasted four innings May 26 in his second start since coming off the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Cingrani is back in the bigs after Johnny Cueto returned to the DL. Cingrani struck out 41 batters and walked nine in 33 innings over six starts in April and May. He allowed three earned runs in his first three tarts and nine in his last three.

away_pitcher_note: Leake hasn't allowed even a single run in four of his last 10 starts and has allowed just two earned runs in three others. His last outing -- three runs on six hits in five innings against St. Louis -- was his worst start sine April.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija fell behind in the count a lot against the Pirates in his last start, lasting six innings before exiting. He gave up four earned runs, snapping a streak of 10 straight starts at Wrigley in which he allowed three or fewer.
away_pitcher_note: In 20 starts since an 8-5 loss to the the Cardinals on Aug. 24, 2012, Latos has gone 10-0 with a 2.65 ERA. His streak of 20 straight regular-season starts without a loss is a Reds record.

away_pitcher_note: Jackson is coming off his first win at Wrigley Field, and his fourth quality start of the season. He gave up four hits over seven innings in his longest outing of the season. He's 1-2 with a 4.40 ERA in five career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Niese returned to the rotation against the Marlins after skipping a start because of shoulder soreness. He pitched 6 2/3 innings against Miami on Sunday, giving up three runs (two earned) on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman has had enough of the Reds. He fell to 0-2 with a 7.94 ERA vs. Cincinnati after his last start. He gave up five runs in six innings in his second non-quality start in his last nine outings. He's 1-1 with a 4.63 ERA vs. the Mets in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hefner took the loss on Tuesday despite allowing just one earned run. The defense didn't help him, as a Daniel Murphy error at first base led to five unearned runs. Hefner lowered his ERA to 4.11.
away_pitcher_note: Garza served up a career-high nine runs over five-plus innings in his last start vs. the Reds. He has one win in his five starts since coming off the DL. The problem? He tends to "gorilla pitch" -- a Sveum-ism -- and then loses command.

home_pitcher_note: Miller struck out 10 on Wednesday but lost when the five hits he allowed turned into four runs. Of the 18 runs he has allowed this season, eight have scored in the first inning, a frame that habitually gives him trouble.

away_pitcher_note: Samardzija was roughed up by the Reds in his last start, giving up five runs on 10 hits in six innings. He struck out six, and ranks among the NL leaders in Ks. The righty is 3-2 with a 4.95 ERA in 16 games (five starts) against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook threw five innings in his first start back from the DL, allowing five runs (three earned) on eight hits. The righty said he felt good enough to pitch much better than he did, but expects better in the future.

away_pitcher_note: Feldman was outstanding in his last start, going seven innings and giving up just one run on two hits with six strikeouts and a walk against the Mets. It was one of his best starts of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Matt Garza had one of his best outings of the season in his last start against the Mets, throwing seven scoreless innings and allowing three hits, but took a no-decision after Carlos Marmol couldn't nail down the win.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel's been absolutely electric this month, sporting a 1.96 ERA and striking out 13 in three starts. The lefty has proved durable too, failing to toss at least six innings just once in his last eight outings.

away_pitcher_note: It's been a Jekyll and Hyde scenario for Norris this year when it comes to home and away starts. He's been splendid in Houston, but has a 5.40 ERA in six road starts while allowing 35 hits in 31 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Lyles has snuck up on the AL, quickly becoming one of baseball's best young arms with a 2-0 mark and a 1.69 ERA in June. He logged seven innings his last time out, shutting down Milwaukee in seven innings of one-run work.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers and Cubs played a pair of series in April, and Gallardo managed to miss both of them. He'd rather pitch; in 14 career starts against the Cubs, he is 7-2 with a 2.95 ERA and 105 strikeouts in only 88 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman may want to check the schedule and avoid NL Central teams. In his last start, he walked four and gave up six hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Cardinals. He now has a 6.65 ERA and 0-4 record against the NL Central.

away_pitcher_note: Garza has given up one run over his past 15 innings in two starts. In his previous outing against the Astros, he set season highs in innings pitched (eight) and strikeouts (eight). He has not faced the Brewers this season.

away_pitcher_note: Wood has posted a quality start in 13 of his 14 starts, but doesn't have much to show for it. He ranks among the top 12 NL starters with a 2.85 ERA. He has never faced the Mariners, and is 2-3 with a 4.01 ERA in eight starts vs. AL teams.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has been consistently inconsistent of late. In his last six starts the 35-year old has pitched two shutouts, but he's also been knocked out of the game before the sixth inning three times.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros were aggressive against Samardzija on Sunday and didn't give him a chance to throw his patented splitter much, but he adjusted and picked up the win in his 10th quality start.

away_pitcher_note: Jackson was roughed up by the Brewers in his last start, giving up six runs over 4 2/3 innings. He is 3-0 in his career against the Mariners, which includes a 2-0 record at Safeco Field.

away_pitcher_note: Rusin was 2-3 with a 6.37 ERA in seven starts with the big league team last season. At Iowa, he was 7-7 with a 3.27 ERA in 17 games (16 starts), including a complete game shutout on June 17 against Omaha.

home_pitcher_note: Straily is scheduled to be recalled from Triple-A Sacramento on Thursday to make his 13th start of the season. He currently has a career-high three-game winning streak despite allowing eight runs in eight innings over his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wood has posted quality starts in 15 of 16 outings, yet doesn't have the wins to show for it. He's winless in his last five starts after a solid effort against the Mariners in which he gave up two runs on three hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija got a no-decision in his last start against the Mariners, but did post a quality start and did make an in-game adjustment that was key. Seattle was aggressive, and he switched his approach to throw them off.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano had a superb June, allowing just nine earned runs in 37 2/3 innings. He went at least six innings in each of those six starts and has allowed two runs or fewer in all but two of his 10 outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson scattered seven hits over six-plus innings in his last start against the Mariners, and picked up his third win in his last five starts. One of those wins came against the Pirates June 9 when he held them to one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton was chased from his start against the Brewers on Sunday after two innings because of a two-hour rain delay. Since coming back from Tommy John surgery, he's allowed 11 runs (five earned) in 18 innings over four starts.

away_pitcher_note: Garza had his best outing of the season, holding the A's to four hits over eight innings Wednesday. He didn't seem to mind that the lineup was stacked with left-handed hitters. His name has been mentioned in trade rumors since Spring Training.

away_pitcher_note: Blanton has just two wins on the season, but has pitched better lately. Three of Blanton's last four starts have been quality starts. The right-hander has also notched six or more strikeouts in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija couldn't control his stuff in his last outing on Friday against the Pirates, allowing five earned runs in a game for the third time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Although his four-game win streak was snapped Friday with a loss against Boston, Wilson allowed just one earned run in 6 2/3 innings. The lefty leads the Angels rotation in wins, ERA and strikeouts (104).

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander's last two stats have been promising. While Jackson hasn't proved to be the innings-eater he was signed as, Cubs manager Dale Sveum wants Jackson to focus on throwing six quality innings in his starts.
away_pitcher_note: Although Westbrook didn't strike out a batter in his last outing vs. Miami, he made up for it by inducing 18 outs on the ground. He surrendered a one-run blast but allowed just two other hits and no walks in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva was limited to 69 pitches in his most recent outing, against the Pirates, his first start since May 14. He will likely be stretched out more against the Cardinals as he steps in for Scott Feldman, who was traded on July 2.
away_pitcher_note: In his second start of the year, Kelly held Miami to four runs on five hits and three walks in six innings, but gave up two homers in a no-decision. He remains in the mix as a long-term option for the fifth starting spot.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has given up four earned runs over 37 innings in his last five starts. He has given up five hits or fewer in six of his 10 starts this season. The subject of trade rumors, could this be his last start for the Cubs?
away_pitcher_note: Lynn became the third National League pitcher to reach 11 wins with a two-run, seven-hit performance against the Marlins in his last outing. He fanned seven batters and walked one over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wood pitched his 17th quality start Tuesday against the Angels and is the first Cubs pitcher with that many before the All-Star break since Greg Maddux did so in 1988. This will be Wood's final tuneup for the All-Star Game.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa will try to keep a surprising run of dominance from the starting staff going beyond the All-Star break, as Colorado's starters boast a 2.23 ERA over their last eight games.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio looked like a new man in his first start back from Triple-A, allowing just three hits in a season-high seven innings. Notching his first win since mid-May, he struck out three in the 3-0 win over the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood closed out the first half with his best start this year, needing only 98 pitches to pitch a one-run complete game. Chatwood, one of the Rockies' most reliable young arms, gave up four hits and struck out four.

away_pitcher_note: With Matt Garza reportedly dealt, the Cubs will send left-hander Chris Rusin to the mound to take his spot tonight against the D-backs.

away_pitcher_note: For just the second time this season, Wood failed to notch a quality start. He gave up a season-high 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings against the Cardinals July 14 to close the first half with a Major League-leading 17 quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off the second-shortest outing of his season, Miley returns home to face the Cubs. Chicago roughed him up for seven runs in seven innings on May 31. He has struggled at home, going 3-2 with a 4.91 ERA in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva's career-long struggles against the Rockies continued his last time out, as he allowed seven earned runs in four innings. He didn't record a strikeout and walked four, including the opposing pitcher.

away_pitcher_note: Jackson turned in another strong outing Sunday, surrendering four runs (three earned) and five hits over seven innings but still picking up the loss. He attacked the strike zone with his fastball and slider and walked only two.

away_pitcher_note: Wood failed to notch a quality start in his last outing for only the third time this year. The lefty gave up four runs over 5 2/3 innings against the D-backs. It's the most runs he's given up since May 25 when Wood served up five to the Reds.

away_pitcher_note: A win over the Padres evened Lohse's win-loss record for the first time since late April, and he registered his team-leading 13th quality start. He lowered his ERA to 3.37, and over his last 11 starts, he is 6-1 with a 2.49 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: In three starts, Bailey has blown four leads already and has been unable to get beyond five innings. He allowed four homers during a no-decision to the Pirates Monday. The bright side? There were no walks and nine strikeouts.

away_pitcher_note: Arroyo will be making his fourth start of the year. He was roughed up in his last outing against the Mets, allowing nine runs in 3 1/3 innings. Arroyo was limited during Spring Training by a bulging disc in his back.

away_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched well enough to win last time out against the Mets, but his offense could not get the job done. McCarthy allowed three runs in 5 2/3 innings. In two career games (one start) at Wrigley Field he has a 2.45 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Wood came within five outs of his first shutout in his last start Saturday in San Diego. Over his last two starts, he has allowed four runs on five hits and five walks in 14 1/3 innings. He went 20 batters between hits vs. the Padres.

away_pitcher_note: Wood did not get a decision in his last start, giving up two runs on four hits over five innings. He walked a season-high five batters. However, he did help himself by hitting a two-run homer and driving in another run on a fielder's choice.

home_pitcher_note: Over his last five starts, Latos is 2-0 with a 2.48 ERA. The right-hander beat the Cubs on June 25, allowing one run on five hits while walking none and fanning five over seven innings. He is 6-2 with a 2.66 ERA in 10 career starts against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Axelrod pitched well despite taking a no-decision in his Reds debut on Aug. 17, allowing two runs on seven hits, walking one and striking out seven against the Rockies. He will be making his first career appearance against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta will miss Wrigley Field. He improved to 3-1 with a 1.86 ERA at home with a win over his former team, the Orioles, in his last start. He beat the Reds June 24 at Wrigley, giving up two runs over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miller was long gone before St. Louis' 12-inning win in Philly on Saturday, but he left with a lead after allowing three runs in six innings. He incorporated a sinker into his repertoire and used the new pitch effectively.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks' streak of six consecutive quality starts ended due to a lengthy rain delay in his last outing. He's allowed just 10 runs in 50 2/3 innings since debuting on July 10.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson is pitching for his rotation spot, as he has allowed four-plus runs in four of five starts since joining the organization. Masterson has worked to simplify his mechanics, and success will continue to ride on the effectiveness of his sinker.
away_pitcher_note: In his last Minor League rehab outing with Double-A Tennessee, Doubront gave up three earned runs on five hits over 4 1/3 innings. He threw 95 pitches, 59 for strikes, striking out five. He's been on the DL since he was acquired by the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales will be called up as the "26th man" to start the nightcap of the doubleheader. Gonzales went 4-1 with a 3.35 ERA in eight Triple-A starts after making three starts - none longer than five innings - with the Cards earlier this summer.
away_pitcher_note: Wada held the AL East-leading Orioles to one run on one hit over 6 1/3 innings in his last start, striking out eight. The 33-year-old lefty is making a case for staying with the Cubs next season. He doesn't overpower hitters but has late movement.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey has made five starts since joining the Cardinals and he has finished seven innings in three of them. He's been the workhorse the club wanted and he has allowed two or fewer earned runs in four of five appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Wood will be looking to win back-to-back starts for the first time since June 10-15. He's 1-6 with a 5.00 ERA in his last 13 starts. In his last outing, the lefty ended a 12-start winless streak with six shutout innings against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Turner threw 66 pitches over 3 2/3 innings in his first start for the Cubs on Wednesday in Cincinnati. The plan is for Chicago to get a look at the right-hander, acquired from the Marlins, in the final month and continue to stretch him out.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson, optioned to Class A in a paper move that opened a spot for relief help, will "return" to make his first career start against the Cubs. He faced them twice in relief last year, working two scoreless innings each time.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta didn't have his command in his last start vs. the Reds, and he threw 96 pitches over four innings, matching his shortest outing of the year. He gave up six runs for the second time this season. The Reds also stole six bases against him.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo was in line to win after working six hard-fought innings against the Padres last week, but a lead escaped Francisco Rodriguez in the ninth inning. He's 9-3 with a 3.00 ERA in 18 career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks finished August 4-0 with a 1.69 ERA in six starts. This will be his second outing vs. the Brewers, who he held to six hits over 7 1/3 scoreless innings on Aug. 12. In his last start, he held the Cardinals to two runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander returns for his first start since Aug. 3, when he strained a left rib-cage muscle in a start at St. Louis. Garza last pitched in a three-inning simulated game, so his pitch count will be limited.

away_pitcher_note: Worley earned his first win as a Pirate in Wrigley Field, going 6 2/3 innings in a 5-3 victory over the Cubs on June 21. He continues to rely on pinpoint control, having yet to issue more than two walks in any of his 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wada has settled in nicely at Wrigley Field. The lefty is 4-1 with a 2.83 ERA in six starts at home, holding opponents to a .203 batting average. He took the loss in his last start, giving up three earned runs over six innings against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start for the Cubs last Saturday in St. Louis, Doubront picked up the win, giving up one run over seven innings. It was his 11th start this season, and the plans are for the lefty to stay in the rotation for the final month.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander is glad to put August behind him: He was winless in the month, despite five quality starts out of six. In fact, he has gone 2-3 since the All-Star break, with a 2.78 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wood is 1-1 in three starts against the Pirates this year. He's coming off a no decision against the Cardinals in which he failed to finish the fifth inning. The lefty is 3-4 with a 3.89 ERA at home, 5-7 with a 5.68 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: By all accounts, Cole made only two bad pitches among the 94 in his last start, but they cost him in a 5-4 loss to the Cards. Three starts into his comeback from a sore lat, "he is in a good place," manager Clint Hurdle says.

home_pitcher_note: Stroman is 2-0 over his last two starts with a 2.63 ERA after going winless in his previous four outings with an 8.66 ERA over that span. He is coming off an outing in which he threw just 76 pitches, at least in part due to a 30-minute power delay.
away_pitcher_note: Turner was able to put some of the lessons from pitching coach Chris Bosio to use in his last start against the Brewers. The goal is to be smarter in terms of his game calling, and it paid off. He gave up one run over 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle is coming off his best start of the second half after allowing just five hits and one walk over eight scoreless innings vs. the Rays. He took a no-decision, but it marked his fifth scoreless outing of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta gave up one run over six innings in his last start against the Brewers, and got the win. He's 3-2 with a 6.00 ERA in six career games (five starts) against the Blue Jays. He has not fared well in Toronto, posting a 1-2 record and 7.31 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hutchison struggled early, but ended up having a strong start during his last outing against the Red Sox. He battled through six innings and allowed three runs on six hits and two walks while striking out six in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: It was a struggle for Hendricks his last outing as he didn't have his best stuff. Yet, he still got the win, holding the Brewers to two runs over 5 2/3 innings. He was named NL Rookie of the Month for August after posting a 4-0 record and 1.69 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cole was backed with great run support in his last start, as the Bucs finished off a sweep of the Cubs in a 10-4 victory Sunday. Cole struck out eight and gave up three earned runs in six innings, and he also hit his first career Major League homer.
away_pitcher_note: Wada had to leave his last start after 3 2/3 innings because of cramping in his left leg. It was most likely caused by dehydration and the 88-degree temperatures. This will be his second straight start vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Locke retired the first 10 and final 10 he faced in a win against Philadelphia on Monday. All three hits and the lone run against the left-hander came in a four-batter span during the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Doubront's high pitch count cost him in his last start vs. the Pirates. He needed 64 pitches to get through three innings, and he admitted he had trouble with his command in the third inning, though he did last five.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez got his second consecutive no-decision Tuesday, after leaving with six innings and 92 pitches under his belt. The veteran righty wanted to stay in the game longer, but he still has a 2.18 ERA in his last 14 starts and is 7-1 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Turner took the loss against Toronto the last time out, going six innings while allowing seven hits and four earned runs. Turner is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts with the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander had his start pushed back a day following a rough outing against the Pirates in which he lasted 1 2/3 innings. Instead of having him face Pittsburgh again on Sunday, he'll start the series opener against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Simon earned just his second win of the second half by allowing two runs on five hits over seven innings against the Cardinals last Wednesday. The All-Star right-hander is 3-0 with a 1.40 ERA in four starts against the Cubs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta carried a lead into the seventh against the Blue Jays on Tuesday, but was saddled with a no-decision despite tossing his 16th quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto tossed eight scoreless innings to beat the Cubs last Thursday, and is 3-0 with a 1.17 ERA in his last three starts. In two starts against the Cubs this season, the All-Star right-hander is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off a loss to Blue Jays in which he gave up four runs over 5 2/3 innings. It was only the second time in his 11 starts that he's served up that many runs, and first time since his MLB debut on July 10 against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Corcino earned another start with a solid two-run, two-hit performance over six innings Friday vs. the Brewers. Said manager Bryan Price: "He impressed me a great deal. No. 1, he threw the ball over the plate consistently."

home_pitcher_note: The Bucs found holes against Wada in his last start, and he gave up four runs over 4 1/3 innings. It was only the second time in 11 starts that he served up more than four runs. He lost to the Dodgers on Aug. 2, giving up two runs over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke did it all in his last outing, twirling six scoreless innings and chipping in a two-run homer in the Dodgers' 17-0 rout of the Giants. Thursday will mark his first start against the Cubs this year.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Jackson's first start since Aug. 20. He's been on the disabled list since then with a right lat strain. In that last start, he gave up seven runs over 2 2/3 innings to the Giants, which isn't how the Cubs want him to end the season.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw fortified his NL MVP resume by limiting the Giants to two runs in his seventh consecutive outing of at least eight innings. He's riding a five-game winning streak, bringing his victory total to a Major League-best 19.

home_pitcher_note: Doubront is coming off a solid outing against the Pirates in which he threw six shutout innings. The lefty felt he was able to apply what pitching coach Chris Bosio has stressed, and that is to throw with conviction and get ahead in the count.
away_pitcher_note: After beginning his Dodgers career with three quality starts in his first four outings, Hernandez hasn't lasted more than 4 1/3 innings in each of his last three starts. Six of the 16 hits he's surrendered over that span have left the yard.

home_pitcher_note: Turner cruised through the first four innings in his last start vs. the Bucs, but the first two batters in the fifth got on base, and ignited a six-run inning. He ended up with the loss. He faced the Dodgers in May in Los Angeles and took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Last September, Wright started a bullpen game for the Rays and allowed a leadoff home run, the only score in 1 1/3 innings and 36 pitches. It was his first start since 2007, and he hasn't started since.

home_pitcher_note: Wood scattered three hits over six scoreless innings in his last outing vs. the Reds, which was a big improvement after allowing seven runs over 1 2/3 innings in his previous start. He was miffed because he walked three.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is eyeing a second 20-win season and will carry a four-start winning streak into this outing. He has allowed two runs over his last three starts, of which two were complete games.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is going for his ninth quality start in 13 outings. He's allowed a combined three earned runs and 12 hits in 12 1/3 innings over two starts vs. the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Miller was hit in the right shin near the end of his last start, though he doesn't expect that to affect him on Tuesday. Miller has been sharp in September, allowing three runs (two earned) in 26 innings.

home_pitcher_note: For the third time this season, Arrieta took a no-hitter into the seventh, but again came up short. He did notch his first complete game shutout in a 7-0 win, holding the Reds to one hit. It was an impressive outing as he fanned 13.
away_pitcher_note: After having his start pushed back three days while dealing with a dead arm issue, Lackey made his best start as a Cardinal on Friday. He was efficient through 7 2/3 innings and scattered six singles.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson is stepping in for Matt Garza, who was scratched because of shoulder tightness. Nelson is 2-7 with a 4.38 ERA in 11 big league starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Jokisch's first big league start. The lefty has made three relief appearances since he was called up to the Cubs in early September. At Triple-A Iowa, he was 9-10 with a 3.58 ERA in 26 starts, striking out 143 over 158 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off consecutive seven-inning gems, Peralta has a chance to join Yovani Gallardo (2011) and Chris Capuano ('05) as the only Brewers pitchers since 1992 to win at least 17 decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Wada thought he was done after his outing Sept. 18, but the Cubs will give the lefty one more start. Wada beat the Brewers on Aug. 13 at Wrigley, giving up two runs over 6 2/3. The team needs to decide whether to pick up his option for 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Burned by back-to-back Reds home runs in his most recent start, Fiers will get a chance to author a positive finish to a tremendous bounce-back season that thrust him back into the Brewers' future plans.
away_pitcher_note: Rookie Kyle Hendricks was slated to start the season finale but the Cubs decided the right-hander had reached his innings limit for the year, so Turner will get one more start. This will be his sixth start with the Cubs and first since Sept. 21.

home_pitcher_note: Wood scattered seven hits over 4 2/3 innings against the Rockies in his first start of the season. The lefty spent most of Spring Training working on sharpening his offspeed pitches in hopes of rebounding from an 8-13 season in 2014.
away_pitcher_note: In his first big league start since July 19, 2013, Marquis started out shaky last Friday vs. the Cardinals. After relaxing and making a delivery adjustment, Marquis retired 12 in a row and turned in a quality start.

away_pitcher_note: Wood is coming off his first win, in which he threw seven scoreless innings, holding the Reds to three hits. The key was being able to locate his fastball. He's 5-7 with a 4.28 ERA in 14 games vs. the Pirates.

away_pitcher_note: Hammel has been consistent in his two starts, allowing three runs in six innings against the Rockies and four runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Padres. He does have three hits, including a double.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has improved in each of his three starts but does not have a victory to show for it. In his last start, he was saddled with a complete-game loss vs. St. Louis, despite giving up just two earned runs on four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is still searching for his first Cubs win. This will be his first start ever at Great American Ball Park, but his second vs. the Reds in '15. He did not get a decision April 13 at Wrigley, giving up six runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: He held the Brewers to two hits over eight scoreless innings in a 6-1 victory on Monday, extending his streak of shutout innings to 15. In three starts, he is 2-0 with an 0.86 ERA and 16 strikeouts against four walks.

away_pitcher_note: Worley limited the Cubs to one unearned run over 5 2/3 innings en route to a win on Wednesday. It was a windy, snowy affair in Pittsburgh. Worley battled through it, working around six hits and two walks while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Wood did not get a decision in his last start, giving up three runs over five innings against the Pirates. He beat the Reds at Wrigley on April 15, holding them to three hits over seven innings. The lefty is 3-5 with a 2.69 ERA vs. his former team.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates have won each of Locke's first three starts. Commanding offspeed stuff has been behind early season effectiveness, resulting in an up-tick of missed swings. Will be his first Wrigley Field start since June 9, 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Lester will get a chance to face another NL Central team when he meets the Brewers. The lefty is still looking for his first win with the Cubs, but he was encouraged by his last outing, when he struck out 10 over six innings vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has given up 32 hits, but walked only six batters, over his first 25 innings. Chicago's Starlin Castro and Anthony Rizzo are a combined 22-for-48 (.458) with seven home runs vs. Peralta.

away_pitcher_note: Fiers has almost twice as many hits and walks allowed (36) as innings pitched (18 2/3). Anthony Rizzo of the Cubs was 5-for-6 with a home run and a double off Fiers last season.

away_pitcher_note: Wood did not walk a batter and posted a quality start in his last outing, a victory over the Pirates. He also struck out a season-high nine batters and showed much-improved fastball command compared with last season when he struggled.

away_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off a rare wild outing, during which he matched a career high with three walks against Pittsburgh. He'll be going for his first win of the season against the Cardinals, against whom he has a 3.06 ERA in three career starts.

away_pitcher_note: Lester is coming off his first win with the Cubs, a 1-0 victory over the Brewers. The lefty was sharp with much better fastball command. He scattered three hits over seven innings, his longest outing this year.

away_pitcher_note: Arrieta's streak of consecutive quality starts was snapped in his last outing, a loss to the Brewers, when he gave up four runs over five innings. The right-hander beat the Cardinals on April 8 at Wrigley, throwing seven scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson has been the Brewers' most consistent starting pitcher despite an extremely unfavorable schedule. This is the third straight occasion on which he's faced the same team in consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a rematch for Hammel, who did not get a decision in his last start vs. the Brewers at home. He gave up three runs over six innings and battled a cracked nail on his right middle finger. He's 5-0 in seven career starts vs. the Brewers.

away_pitcher_note: Wood is coming off a rough outing against the Cardinals. He gave up six runs on six hits over five-plus innings, including a grand slam to Mark Reynolds. This is his fourth start on the road. He's looking for his first win away from Wrigley.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has been better in his last three outings, meeting the definition of quality start each time. But he has surrendered five home runs in those games and won only one of them.

away_pitcher_note: Wood gets the ball after having his start pushed back three days because of irritation in his left triceps from hitting, which didn’t stop him from striking out 13 in his last start.

away_pitcher_note: Kazmir has been a bit unpredictable this year. Two starts back he walked seven. Next time out he fanned 12. He won his lone career Wrigley Field start.

away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger last pitched eight days ago, allowing two runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Reds. He had been on standby for long relief since then.

away_pitcher_note: The 19-year old rookie left-hander will make his second Major League start. The Dodgers' No. 1 prospect made his debut on Friday in New York against the Mets, lasting just 2 2/3 innings and allowing three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey had an impressive May. The righty was 2-1 with a 2.09 ERA and 40 whiffs. He finished it with a win over the Phils, giving up one run in seven innings. It was his fourth start in which he went at least six innings and gave up one or zero runs.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off the best outing of his young career. He gave up three runs in 7 1/3 innings against San Diego, striking out nine, after being recalled from Triple-A Reno. He is facing the Cubs for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel is expected to make this start despite leaving his last outing after two innings due to right hamstring cramps. In that game, four Cubs relievers followed Hammel with seven perfect innings to set up a win over the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Escobar struggled in his first career start last time out against the Astros. The left-hander gave up eight runs (seven earned) on 10 hits over 3 1/3 innings in a loss. He's in the rotation until Shelby Miller returns from an injury.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs will try to start a new winning streak for Arrieta, who did not get a decision in his last outing, a loss to the Dodgers. He finished May 4-0 with a 2.08 ERA. He beat Arizona on April 10, giving up three runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin is coming off his worst start of the year, after he allowed seven runs in just 3 1/3 innings against the Astros at Chase Field. He has been a much better pitcher on the road (2.68 ERA) than at home (7.94).

home_pitcher_note: Morgan was solid through five vs. the Nats last time out, but he got rocked for four runs on two homers in the sixth. He failed to record a quality start for the fifth time in seven starts. Morgan will be tested to limit the long ball vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lester went the distance in his last outing, vs. the Dodgers, holding them to four hits and striking out 10. It was his 28th career double-digit-K game. He’s 5-0 with a 1.71 ERA in seven career starts against the Phillies, including a win on May 27.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has been the Phillies' hard-luck pitcher this season. He’s made seven of 11 quality starts but has only two wins to show for it; the Phils have averaged 2.58 runs per nine innings while he's been on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: One start after throwing a complete game vs. the Phillies, Hendricks went eight innings vs. the Dodgers. He's going to hate to leave Wrigley Field. The right-hander has a 1.99 ERA at home, having given up nine earned runs over 40 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has lasted fewer than five innings in each of his last three outings. His biggest problem is high pitch counts, as he hasn’t pitched more than six innings since striking out 16 in a three-hit shutout against the Padres on April 19.
away_pitcher_note: The 37-year-old right-hander has continued his late-career resurgence early in 2016. Over his last two starts, Lackey has given up just one run in 13 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Norris earned another start courtesy of the strong effort he provided in Monday's emergency start against the Dodgers. The veteran right-hander threw 91 pitches in what was his first start since April 27.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel (7-1, 2.14 ERA) is coming off a win against the D-backs, going seven innings and allowing two runs on only one hit and two walks. He is 1-3 with a 7.58 ERA in six career appearances against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Wisler has shown great promise and now he’ll have to show he’s capable of bouncing back from Sunday’s ugly start against the Dodgers.  The young right-hander’s problems stemmed from a lack of confidence he had in his secondary pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta suffered his first loss since July 25 of last season in his latest start against the D-backs, but he still struck out a season-high 12 batters in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gant will make his first Major League start in place of Williams Perez, who was placed on the disabled list earlier this week. In seven starts this year with Triple-A Gwinnett, Gant posted a 3-0 record with a 3.14 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lester enters his start against the Braves on a 16-inning scoreless streak. The last run he allowed came in the first inning two starts ago. Since, he finished a complete game against the Dodgers and held the Phillies scoreless for eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer faces the Cubs away from Wrigley Field for the first time in his career. He is 1-1 with a 3.75 ERA in four career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks looked solid but was pulled after only five innings and 81 pitches in his last start against the Phillies, as Joe Maddon searched for offense off the bench. He’s now gone four straight starts giving up two runs or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez hopes to snap a personal four-game losing streak. During that stretch, he has allowed 21 runs in 22 2/3 innings with 31 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey threw seven shutout innings in his last outing against the Phillies. He beat the Nationals at Wrigley Field on May 6, giving up two runs over seven innings. The right-hander has not allowed a run over 13 2/3 innings in two starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg did not face the Cubs during the four-game set at Wrigley Field in early May. He has not faced the Cubs since Aug. 22, 2013. In that game, he allowed four runs in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel didn't pitch poorly in his last outing; the Braves' Bud Norris just pitched better. Hammel allowed 3 runs in 5 1/3 innings. Hammel did not get a decision when he faced the Nationals on May 7 at Wrigley Field, giving up 3 runs over 5 frames.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano took a step in the right direction Saturday, allowing four runs (one earned) while striking out eight over six innings. He induced 17 swinging strikes, his highest total in a month, but still walked three batters.

home_pitcher_note: Lester is on a roll. He has won his last four starts, and he has not walked a batter in his last three. Lester has given up two earned runs over 30 1/3 innings in his last four games. He's 1-1 with a 0.73 ERA in two starts vs. the Pirates this year.
away_pitcher_note: Niese's month-long roll screeched to a halt against the Cardinals on Sunday, when he allowed eight runs on 11 hits and two homers in 5 1/3 innings. The Cubs scored six runs on nine hits and five walks against him on May 3.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks shut down the Nats over five, but had trouble locating his fastball in the sixth. He said that's something he needs to work on during his side sessions. He'll be happy to be back at Wrigley Field, where he's 3-1 with a 1.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off an eight-inning gem against the Mets, Taillon looks to build on his first career win on another big stage, against the Cubs at Wrigley Field on Sunday Night Baseball.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the third time Lackey will face the Cardinals this season. So far, he's 1-0 and has given up three earned runs over 14 innings. He did not get a decision in his last outing against the Nationals, but he did post a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia fell to 0-2 in June on Tuesday, when he gave up eight hits and four runs (three earned) over 6 1/3 innings vs. the Astros. He remains inconsistent in 13 outings, with five quality starts and six appearances of five innings or less.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel had his best fastball command in his last outing against the Nationals, giving up one run over seven innings. He is 2-0 vs. the Cardinals this year, giving up two earned runs over 13 1/3 innings in two starts at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright continues to improve in his starts. He threw seven shutout innings and gave up four hits in his last outing, against the Astros, but took a no-decision. His ERA has dropped more than a full point, to 4.78, over the past month.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta threw six shutout innings against the Pirates in his last start, and now is 11-0 with a 1.20 ERA in his last 13 starts against NL Central teams. He faced the Cardinals May 25, and served up four runs over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha lost his seventh straight decision in his last start. He went 7 2/3 innings vs. Texas and only gave up one run on six hits in his second-longest outing of the season to drop his ERA to 4.56.

home_pitcher_note: Chen was battered by the Rockies his last time out, surrendering six runs over a career-low 2 1/3 innings. On a positive note, he didn’t allow a home run after yielding seven over his previous two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lester has earned wins in five straight starts. Last time out, he allowed a season-high 11 baserunners, but gave up only three runs in six innings to earn a win against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler embodied the term 'effectively wild’ in his last start against the Rockies. The right-hander issued a career-high six walks but held Colorado to two hits over six scoreless innings for the win.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks struck out a career-high 12 batters and walked none in his last start against the Pirates. He has 73 strikeouts this season and only 19 walks.

away_pitcher_note: Lackey had a gutsy outing in his last start against the Cardinals. He needed 57 pitches to get through the first two innings but was able to go six in a 3-2 loss. He's made 10 straight quality starts and has a 1.97 ERA in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: After winning nine straight starts, Fernandez has encountered some tough luck. In his last two starts, he has given up four runs in 12 2/3 innings. His record at Marlins Park is 23-1 with a 1.48 ERA. He has never faced the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel had trouble against the Cardinals on Tuesday, giving up a season-high four runs over 5 2/3 innings. He is 2-4 with a 4.09 ERA in 10 career games against the Marlins. Expect him to be paired with rookie catcher Willson Contreras.

away_pitcher_note: Lester served up two home runs in his last start against the Marlins, the first time he's done that this season. He's 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two starts against the Reds this year, including on April 22 in which he gave up one run over 7 innings.

home_pitcher_note: During a no-decision on Friday vs. the Padres - his second big league start - Reed lacked the command and sharpness from his debut. He allowed five runs, throwing 104 pitches in five innings, often finding himself behind in counts.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off a strange start. He gave up one hit over five innings against the Marlins, but it was a grand slam. He also tied a career high with four walks, and he gave the Marlins credit for not swinging at some borderline pitches.

away_pitcher_note: Lackey struggled in his previous outing, his shortest of the season at 4 1/3 innings, when he gave up seven runs vs. the Marlins. He's 2-0 with a 1.98 ERA in four career starts against the Mets.

away_pitcher_note: Hammel took the loss in his last start, although he pitched well, giving up two runs over six innings against the Marlins. He's 0-3 with a 4.91 ERA in five career starts vs. the Mets, and he lost to them last year in Game 4 of the NLCS.

away_pitcher_note: Arrieta's struggles continued vs. the Reds as he gave up a season-high five runs and five walks over five innings. Arrieta still has a 2.10 ERA, but he's walked 20 in his last 40 innings, and four of the five runs he allowed Monday reached on a walk.

away_pitcher_note: Lost in a crazy 15-inning game, Lester had another solid outing against the Reds on Tuesday. After a two-out hit in the first, Lester held the Reds hitless until Billy Hamilton homered in the eighth, including retiring 14 straight at one point.

home_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see if Hendricks feels any different after throwing a season-high 117 pitches in his previous start. The right-hander beat the Reds on June 29, giving up two runs over 6 2/3 innings. He's 4-1 with a 1.93 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Reed never allowed seven earned runs in a game as a professional until Wednesday’s 9-2 loss to the Cubs when he gave up seven earned runs over four innings. He’s struggling early in counts and his fastball has been hit hard.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey apparently is comfortable at Wrigley Field, where he's gone 4-2 with a 2.01 ERA this season. He's 1-1 with a 5.84 ERA in two starts vs. the Reds this season, although both of those games were in April.
away_pitcher_note: Lacking command of all his pitches, namely his fastball and slider, Finnegan endured the shortest and worst start of his brief career vs. the Nationals on Thursday -- 2 1/3 innings with eight earned runs -- including two homers.

home_pitcher_note: This will be a spot start for Warren to give the other pitchers a breather. He began the 2015 season in the Yankees' rotation and was 6-6 in 17 starts. He's been valuable in the bullpen for the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, DeSclafani worked into at least the seventh inning -- something the Reds rotation hasn’t had much of this season. He’s had no issues with the oblique injury that put him on the disabled list most of this season.

away_pitcher_note: Harrell received an unexpected promotion on Saturday and delivered six strong innings against the Marlins.  The veteran, who hadn’t pitched in the Majors since 2014, has recently gained more confidence in his cutter.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano picked up a win at Oakland on Sunday, allowing three runs on six hits over five innings. In two starts vs. the Cubs this season, he's 0-2 with a 10.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl "competed his face off," catcher Erik Kratz said, in a no-decision against the A's on Saturday. Pitching without his usual command down in the zone, the rookie tossed six innings of two-run ball in the Pirates' 4-2 win.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is coming off the shortest outing of his career, in which he lasted just 1 1/3 innings against the Mets. He served up a season-high eight runs on nine hits, including three homers. He's 2-1 with a 1.96 ERA vs. the Pirates this year.

home_pitcher_note: Niese went 5 2/3 innings and allowed one run in a win over the Cardinals on Monday. He's lost both starts he's made against the Cubs this season, with an 8.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is one win shy of matching his career high, and the way the right-hander is pitching, it should be easy for him to top that. He is 5-1 with a 1.67 ERA in nine games at Wrigley Field, including a two-inning relief outing on July 7.
away_pitcher_note: Perez was enjoying a strong finish to the first half until he ran into the Red Sox in his last start. Hurt by erratic defense, he allowed 11 runs, seven earned, over four innings in an 11-6 loss at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel is coming off a no-decision against the Braves that he had to leave early because of cramping in his right hand. He felt great in the outing, giving up three hits over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish, who threw two rehab starts earlier this month and a bullpen session on Wednesday, is expected to be activated from his second DL stint of the year (right shoulder discomfort) and make his fourth start of 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey did not get a decision in his last outing against the Pirates in the first-half finale. He did go deep, which was needed because the bullpen had run out of gas. Lackey has not won a game since June 8. He's 4-3 with a 2.60 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: He was 4-0 with a 1.51 ERA in June but has allowed 10 runs in 8 1/3 innings in two starts in July. He is 6-1 with a 2.09 ERA in nine starts on the road. This is his first start at Wrigley Field since throwing a no-hitter with the Phillies on July 25.

home_pitcher_note: Lester had his worst and shortest outing of his career against the Mets on July 3 in New York, giving up eight runs on nine hits over 1 1/3 innings. He served up three home runs. Lester is 4-2 with a 2.32 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Matz opens the Mets' series in Chicago. Since being diagnosed with bone spurs, Matz’s slider usage has been almost nonexistent, but he brought the pitch back in a start vs. the Nats in which he allowed 3 runs over 7 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta did not pitch in the All-Star Game, and he will be seeking his first win since June 27. He lost to the Mets on July 2, giving up four runs over 5 1/3 innings. If his fastball command is on, he'll be fine.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets gave Syndergaard the last spot in the rotation out of the All-Star break. They want the young righty, dealing with bone spurs, to get as much rest as possible before he begins his second half -- firmly planted in the NL Cy Young race.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is on a roll. He is 6-1 with a 1.50 ERA in 10 home games this season. The Cubs are 5-0 in his past five starts, including a win over the Rangers in his last outing, in which he gave up three hits over six scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Colon opened the Mets’ second half by retiring the first 13 Phillies he faced. Perfect through 4 1/3, Colon said he got tired in the fifth and sixth innings, exiting after 5 2/3 and allowing three runs to score (all unearned).

home_pitcher_note: Nelson was 0-4 with a 5.14 ERA over seven starts in June and July before beating the Reds with seven scoreless innings in his last outing. Can he repeat that performance against the Cubs, whom Nelson blanked over 7 1/3 shutout frames on May 18?
away_pitcher_note: Hammel snapped a four-game losing streak in his last start, giving up one run on three hits against the Rangers. He lost to the Brewers on May 19, giving up four runs over six innings. In 10 road games, he's 4-4 with a 3.81 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Davies has a 2.95 ERA over his last 13 starts. In his most recent start against the Reds, he pitched seven scoreless innings, retiring 16 of the final 17 batters he faced, including the last 11 in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey will miss pitching at Wrigley, where he's compiled a 2.84 ERA compared to a 4.70 ERA on the road. He's 0-4 in his last seven starts, and hasn't won since June 8. He didn't get a decision vs. the Brewers on May 18, giving up one run in 6 IP.

home_pitcher_note: Nine of Guerra's 14 starts have met the definition of "quality," including his six-inning, two-run performance in Pittsburgh on Tuesday. Opponents are hitting .204 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lester got off to a good start in the second half by holding the Mets to one run over 7 2/3 innings. He will miss pitching at Wrigley Field, where he's posted a 2.17 ERA in nine starts. He's 2-2 with a 2.22 ERA in four career starts vs. the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has won once in his past seven starts and is coming off a no-decision in his most recent outing. Gonzalez had a quality start, allowing three runs in six innings against the Mariners, but the White Sox bullpen blew a lead in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta looked like his Cy Young self in his last start against the Mets, striking out eight and giving up one run over seven innings. He is 3-1 with a 3.82 ERA in six starts against the White Sox, including a complete-game victory last year.

home_pitcher_note: Shields has looked more like himself lately. Despite taking the loss in his last start, allowing two solo homers vs. the Tigers, he's 2-3 with a 2.09 ERA in his past five outings. Shields is 1-0 with a 3.72 ERA in three career starts vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks can only hope he feels as good pitching on the south side as he does at Wrigley. The righty threw 6 1/3 scoreless innings vs. the Mets in his last outing, and has a 1.36 ERA at home. He's given up three earned runs in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel beat the Brewers in his last outing, but he'll be happy to be back at Wrigley. He's 4-1 with a 2.70 ERA in eight home starts. He has not faced the White Sox since 2013, and is 1-2 with a 4.01 ERA against them in nine games (four starts).
away_pitcher_note: Jacob Turner struggled in two starts for the White Sox, so Ranaudo, who replaced Chris Sale when he was put on the suspended list, gets the call against the Cubs. Ranaudo was 1-0 with a 17.18 ERA with Texas, but this will be his White Sox debut.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey is looking for his first win since June 8. Since then, the right-hander is 0-5 with a 5.73 ERA in eight starts, giving up 10 homers over 48 2/3 innings. He's 4-4 with a 2.84 ERA at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Sale was scratched from his start Saturday and suspended five games for insubordination, violating team rules and destroying team equipment. Sale’s last start came on July 18 in Seattle when the five-time All-Star allowed one hit over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lester, who is 1-1 in his last six starts, returns to Wrigley Field, where he's 5-2 with a 2.18 ERA in nine outings. Against the Mariners, he's 5-4 with a 3.52 ERA in 12 career starts, and has not faced them since 2014.
away_pitcher_note: The 35-year-old has gone 10-2 with a 3.69 ERA over his last 12 starts, helping hold the rotation together during injuries to Felix Hernandez and Taijuan Walker. He’s faced the Cubs once, taking a no-decision with four runs in eight innings in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta did not get a decision in his last outing against the White Sox. He gave up four runs over six innings, including three on a home run by Todd Frazier. He's now 1-2 with a 6.14 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has a career-high 5.23 ERA in 18 starts, but is coming off a solid six-inning outing at Toronto when he allowed two runs on four hits in a 2-0 loss. He’s 3-1 with a 3.89 ERA in five career starts vs. the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Matusz's first start for the Cubs. He signed as a free agent in June and was pitching at Triple-A Iowa. The Mariners know him. His last outing in the big leagues was May 17, when he gave up four earned runs over 1 2/3 innings vs. Seattle
away_pitcher_note: The ace has allowed nine runs and 19 hits in 12 2/3 innings in two starts since coming off a two-month DL stint, though Seattle won both games. His only game vs. the Cubs came in 2010, when he gave up two runs in nine innings in a 13-inning loss.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks will be happy to be back at Wrigley Field, where he's 7-1 with a 1.36 ERA. He's coming off his first loss since June 13, when he gave up three runs over 5 2/3 innings against the White Sox. He has 29 Ks over his last 35 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Conley went 3-0 with a 1.82 ERA in five July starts. The lefty hopes to carry that over into August, but on the road he has a 3.88 ERA to go with a 3-2 record, compared to a 4-3 mark with a 2.88 ERA at home.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel will be vying for a career-high 11th win. He's posted a 2.35 ERA in his last four starts and is coming off a solid outing against the White Sox. He struck out seven, one shy of his season high. He has a 2.50 ERA at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: In a rarity, Fernandez was hit hard at home by the Cardinals his last time out. In just five innings, he surrendered five runs, including two home runs, the most he’s ever allowed in one start at Marlins Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey held the White Sox to one run over six innings in his last outing and picked up the win, his first since June 8. The right-hander is comfortable at Wrigley Field, where he's 5-4 with a 2.73 ERA in 10 games.
away_pitcher_note: If his last two starts are any indication, Koehler is helping solidify the rotation. He has given up three runs (one earned) in 14 innings in wins over the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Overton has had trouble in his first taste of the bigs, giving up at least three runs in each of his four starts and finishing six innings just once. His struggles were apparent on July 30 versus Cleveland, when he gave up five runs in 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester picked up his 11th win in his last start, matching his win total last season. He'll be happy to be pitching at Wrigley Field, where he's 6-2 with a 1.99 ERA in 10 games. All have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: After improving in June with a 3.23 ERA, Gray’s July was a struggle. The right-hander went 2-4 with a 7.79 ERA, giving up seven runs three times and allowing fewer than three runs just once.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs have lost Arrieta's last five starts, but he hasn't pitched poorly. He gave up two runs over seven-plus innings in his last outing, against the Mariners. He'll miss Wrigley Field, where he has a 1.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Manaea’s stuff seemed to be working against the Angels on Tuesday, but a pair of home runs late in the southpaw’s start soured things quickly. He holds a 2.51 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off his third career complete game and second shutout. He will miss Wrigley Field, where he has a 1.19 ERA. The right-hander got an extra day before this start, which should help since he threw a career-high 123 pitches.

away_pitcher_note: Marquez struck out nine in five innings in his last start. Problem was, two mistake fastballs led to two-run homers, and he yielded five runs total in a loss to the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Butler's first game against his former team. He's 2-0 with a 2.63 ERA in his three home starts this year. His next win will be a career high -- he's matched his best of three set in 2015 with the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman earned more opportunities in the rotation by holding the Padres to three hits and one run and a career-high nine strikeouts in seven innings before an offensive substitution ended his day at 89 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: There's no place like Wrigley Field for Arrieta. He's 3-0 with a 3.04 ERA in four home starts this season. In his last outing against the Marlins, he shrugged off a 34-pitch first and held them to two hits over six-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela gave up two runs on five hits, walking three and striking out four over six innings against the Cubs on May 9. The rookie has given up seven runs over his past two starts (5.56 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: deGrom has an 8.82 ERA in his last three starts. Location issues have been a problem, as opponents are hitting .338 against him in that stretch, and he has given up five homers over those 16 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey isn't afraid to challenge hitters, but it may have cost him in his last start, when he served up two home runs in the Cubs' 6-5 loss to the Marlins. In his last four starts, he's given up six home runs over 23 innings, and is 0-3.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler continued his solid start by allowing one earned run over seven innings against the Rangers last Wednesday. He has given up three or fewer runs in nine of his first 11 starts and has struck out 21 batters in his last 24 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is one win shy of No. 150 of his career. He fell short in his bid in his last start, losing to the Rockies. He's now 0-2 in his last three starts and has given up 13 earned runs over 14 1/3 innings in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Harvey was dominant in his last start against the Braves, going five scoreless innings and only surrendering four hits. Home starts haven’t been kind to him this year, as he has gone 2-1 with a 6.11 ERA in 28 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery will get his second chance to start this year while filling in for the injured Kyle Hendricks. A big question for the lefty will be how he can manage his pitch count -- Montgomery allowed several three-ball counts in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: Williams labored in his last start against the Marlins on Saturday, allowing five runs on six hits in just four innings. He surrendered two earned runs on five hits in five innings during two relief appearances against the Cubs earlier in the season.
away_pitcher_note: Butler will make his seventh start of the season on Friday. He's coming off a loss to the Rockies in which he gave up three runs over five innings. He needs to keep his pitch count down and go deeper in games.

home_pitcher_note: Nova struck out four batters and only gave up one hit in six scoreless innings against the Marlins in his last start on Sunday. He has earned a quality start in 11 of his 13 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta will try to get back on track, making his second start of the season against the Pirates. He's been bothered by a small cut on his right thumb, which isn't a big deal, but it has limited the amount of throwing he's done between starts.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon scattered five hits in five scoreless innings in his first start since being diagnosed with testicular cancer in early May. He produced a quality outing in his last start against Chicago, limiting the Cubs to one run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a bad outing against the Mets in which he served up three home runs over five innings. He's given up 11 homers in his last six starts, and 19 already this season. He's 3-3 with a 5.40 ERA on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lester picked up his 150th career win in his last start, striking out 10 over seven innings against the Mets. Manager Joe Maddon called the outing "effortless." He'll be glad to be back at Wrigley Field, where Lester is 3-1 with a 2.65 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, the veteran left-hander came within a two-out, two-run double in the ninth from the Padres’ first shutout since September 2014. Richard pitched for the Cubs in 2015 and 2016, posting a 4.47 ERA in 48 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery did not get a decision in his last start vs. the Mets, but he was able to go deeper, throwing 88 pitches in five innings. This will be his third start subbing for Kyle Hendricks, who is sidelined with tendinitis in his right hand.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin seeks his third straight winning decision when he faces the Cubs for the first time this year. He's had difficulty against Jon Jay and Anthony Rizzo in the past, who are hitting .300 (3-for-10) and .500 (4-for-8) against him, respectively.

home_pitcher_note: Butler had a more pitch efficient outing in his last start against the Pirates, but admitted he started to run out of gas at the end of his 5 2/3-inning stint. He's done better at Wrigley Field, posting a 3.38 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Diaz gave up a pair of homers to the Brewers in his second career start Friday. But the 22-year-old right-hander showed progress, extending his start to 3 1/3 innings, striking out five and issuing just one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Locking down innings has been a struggle for the left-hander. Ten of the 11 runs he has allowed in four starts have come with two outs. Locke still seeks his first win after coming off the disabled list on June 1.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Arrieta couldn't finish the fifth. The problem this time was his pitch count and the Pittsburgh humidity, which made him sweat so much, he couldn't grip the ball. He has to hope the roof is closed in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Urena has won four straight decisions in his last six starts. His last three outings, he's 2-0 (2.65 ERA). His line is a bit uneven over the six starts. He's worked five innings in five of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a solid outing in which he held the Pirates to two hits over six innings. One of those hits was a home run, and Lackey now has served up 20 this season. He gave up 23 in 2016. He's 4-3 on the road so far.

home_pitcher_note: Nicolino showed signs of rust in his in his first start off the disabled list. In a three-inning no-decision vs. the Nationals, he yielded six runs (three earned) on seven hits, two of which were home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Lester received a no-decision in his last outing against the Padres, but did post his eighth quality start of the season. He'll miss Wrigley Field, where he has a 2.68 ERA in nine home starts. He's 1-3 with a 5.85 ERA in six road games.

home_pitcher_note: It's been an up-and-down June for Volquez. In his first two starts -- including a no-hitter -- he allowed three hits with 18 K's in 16 scoreless innings. In his last two starts, he's allowed 10 earned runs in 8 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery had an extra day between starts before his last outing, and it helped. He threw six scoreless innings against the Padres and picked up his first win of the season. So far on the road, the lefty is 0-2 with a 2.76 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez is off to his best start since 2012, his first season in Washington. He enters this game ranked sixth in the National League in ERA in what has been a strong bounce-back season. He is one strikeout away from 1,500 in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Butler had trouble with his command in his last outing against the Padres, and it resulted in a high pitch count. He threw 92 pitches in four-plus innings before he was pulled. He's 1-1 with a 5.63 ERA in three road starts so far.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer was the victim of one of the toughest losses of the year last time out, as he struck out 11 and gave up just two hits in eight innings but allowed two unearned runs. He has recorded double digit strikeouts in six consecutive games.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta is coming off his best outing of the season, in which he held Miami to one run over seven innings and threw an efficient 82 pitches.  His last start vs. the Nats was May 8, 2016 (no decision).

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg struggled his last start, giving up five runs on eight hits in five innings. He has not made it out of the sixth inning in any of his past three outings. In four career starts against the Cubs he owns a 1.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has posted quality starts in his last two outings. He's also fared better on the road, going 4-4 with a 4.40 ERA. However, he hasn't had much luck vs. NL East teams this year, going 0-3 with a 5.32 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ross is still searching for some consistency during his uneven 2017 campaign, but he is coming off a start in which he threw seven innings of one-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Lester notched his third straight quality start in his last outing, beating the Marlins. He gave up three first-inning runs, then settled down and scattered four hits over seven innings. He hasn't faced the Nationals since 2015.

away_pitcher_note: Montgomery is coming off a loss to the Marlins in which he gave up three unearned runs in the first inning, then didn't allow another. Montgomery went six innings, matching his longest outing of the season, and threw a season-high 91 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Stephens will be the eighth Reds pitcher and the fifth starter to make his big league debut this season. In 15 appearances, 14 starts, with Triple-A Louisville this season, Stephens is 4-4 with a 4.97 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Adleman has allowed three or fewer runs in six of his last seven outings. He faced the Cubs once already this season, allowing two runs in six innings on April 21 at Great American Ball Park.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta has been inconsistent. On June 22, he held the Marlins to one run over seven innings and was efficient. In his next outing against the Nationals, he walked six over four-plus innings. He's 4-6 with a 5.04 ERA in 11 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lester posted his fourth consecutive quality start in his last outing, holding the Nationals to one run over six innings. He has a 2.42 ERA and 28 strikeouts over 26 innings in his last four games.
away_pitcher_note: Archer had a quality start Thursday at Pittsburgh, but came away with the loss after allowing three runs on eight hits in six frames. Archer came to the Rays in a 2011 trade with the Cubs. He has one career start against the Cubs, which came in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey had trouble executing his pitches in his last outing vs. the Nationals, and gave up eight runs over 5 1/3 innings. He hasn't had much success at home this season, going 1-4 record with a 5.13 ERA. Teams are batting .281 against him at Wrigley.
away_pitcher_note: Snell endured a four-run, 36-pitch first frame Wednesday in a loss to the Pirates. His line showed six runs with five walks on 98 pitches (42 balls). Opponents are hitting .211 against him the first time through the lineup.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery was put into the rotation because of an injury to Kyle Hendricks and has been consistent. Joe Maddon says the lefty needs to work on his fastball command, adding, "when it shows up, heads up, because his other stuff is really good."
away_pitcher_note: Davies started off shaky in his last start, allowing four runs in the first three innings. But the right-hander bounced back by tossing three straight 1-2-3 innings, which manager Craig Counsell said were his best innings of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Butler cruised through the first three innings of his last start and then lost control. He gave up four runs in 3 2/3 innings and took the loss. He did not get a decision vs. the Bucs on June 16, going 5 2/3 innings. He's 2-1 with a 3.18 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Williams has seen the Cubs three times but just once as a starter (this June) when he allowed three runs on four hits, walked two, and struck out three across five innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is coming off possibly his best start of the season in which he held the Reds to one hit over seven scoreless innings. The right-hander had good command of his pitches. He's 3-0 with a 3.86 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Nova has faced the Cubs twice in his career, allowing four earned runs in 12 1/3 innings (2.92 ERA). He last pitched against Chicago on June 17, allowing three runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lester served up six runs to the Rays in his last start, the most he's allowed at Wrigley Field since Aug. 19, 2015. He's 3-2 with a 3.19 ERA in 10 home starts. He faced the Pirates on April 16, throwing seven shutout innings at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Replacing Jameson Taillon -- who has flu-like symptoms -- Chad Kuhl goes on just two days' rest after throwing 95 pitches over seven innings Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: A big inning chased Gausman out of the game after four innings in Minnesota. He allowed six runs (five earned) off nine hits, while recording seven strikeouts. Gausman has notched at least seven strikeouts in four of his previous five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery opens the second half, making his seventh start. The lefty went 2 1/3 innings in his last start vs. the Brewers and pitched in relief Sunday vs. the Bucs. He's only pitched in relief vs. the O's. He's 0-4 with a 4.58 ERA vs. the AL East.

home_pitcher_note: Miley ended the first half of the season on a positive note against the Twins. He finished one out shy of his first quality start since June 1, as he allowed one run off eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta will make his second career start against his former team and first since Aug. 22, 2014. The righty had an inconsistent first half with eight quality starts in 18 outings. He's given up 14 homers; he served up 16 in 31 starts in '16.

home_pitcher_note: Inserted back into the rotation at the end of the first half, Jimenez won his last start, against the Twins. The righty yielded four runs on four hits and four walks with three strikeouts in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana, acquired Thursday from the White Sox for four Minor Leaguers, will make his Cubs debut in the series finale. He faced the O's on May 7 and gave up four runs on nine hits in five innings. He's 1-3 with a 5.16 ERA at Camden Yards.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has struggled at home this season. He has a 7.58 ERA in nine home starts, including a 7-ER start vs. the Brewers on June 25. However, he has built some momentum by allowing just two runs in his last 13 1/3 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Lester ended the first half with the worst outing of his career, giving up 10 runs (four earned) over two-thirds of an inning. Maybe pitching near his offseason home will help. He was 4-1 with a 1.95 ERA in five career starts at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb has faced some tough offenses in his past two starts. On July 9, he allowed four walks and four runs against the Nationals. He now carries a 2.14 strikeouts-to-walks ratio this season and a 7.43 ERA over his last 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has been on the disabled list since July 5 because of plantar fasciitis in his right foot. He did post a quality start in his last outing against the Rays. In four career starts against the Braves, he's 1-1 with a 2.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey has found recent success with his knuckleball. In his last five starts, he has given up four runs and struck out 27. His location has been good as well, with no home runs allowed in his last 33 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery opened the second half but did not get a decision, giving up four runs over 4 1/3 innings against the Orioles. This will be Montgomery's eighth start of the season.
