away_pitcher_note: Martinez posted a quality start his last time out, but yet again, the Cardinals couldn’t turn it into a win. Seven times this season, Martinez has taken a no-decision or a loss despite making a quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Lester held the Braves to one run on three hits over seven innings in his last start. He's 0-1 with a 3.78 ERA in three outings vs. St. Louis this year, posting a quality start in one of those games. He is 3-3 with a 3.73 ERA in 11 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright continues to be the benefactor of generous run support, but he's also pitching better as of late. Since allowing 20 runs over 10 1/3 innings, Wainwright has posted a 3.52 ERA over five games.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Quintana's first Wrigley Field start with the Cubs. In his debut against the Orioles, he struck out 12 over seven scoreless innings. He is 0-1 in two career starts at Wrigley. He last pitched there on July 12, 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha twirled his first career complete game - and shutout - his last time out while throwing a career-high 119 pitches. Since posting an 8.17 ERA in a six-start stretch, Wacha is 4-0 with a 1.01 ERA over his last four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks makes his first start since June 4. He has been on the DL with inflammation in his right hand, and in his last Minors rehab outing, he threw five perfect innings for Double-A Tennessee. He's 2-1 with a 4.18 ERA in six home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez returned from a stint on the disabled list with a gem against the Dodgers the last time out, as he allowed one run in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start off the DL, Lackey gave up one run on five hits in five innings vs. the Braves. He's 1-4 with a 5.05 ERA at Wrigley. Lackey had been sidelined with plantar fasciitis in his right foot, which is something to keep an eye on.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw has made four starts, including his season debut on June 28, but he has struggled in his last two. Rodon has allowed 11 runs on 12 hits over his last nine innings, striking out eight and walking five.

home_pitcher_note: After three starts this season, Shields featured a 1.62 ERA over 16 2/3 innings. Since that point, the right-hander has an 8.10 ERA over 30 innings and six starts, and he has allowed nine home runs and 15 walks. Shields is 2-0 vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts since the All-Star break, Arrieta is 1-0 with a 2.13 ERA while holding opponents to a .191 batting average against. In his last outing against the Cardinals, he gave up two runs on five hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was the definition of wildly effective in his last start on Saturday vs. the Royals, yielding one run on two hits in five innings, but he also walked six. For the season, Pelfrey has issued 39 free passes over 78 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is coming off a solid outing against the Cardinals in which he retired the first 17 batters he faced. He went eight innings and gave up three hits, including back-to-back homers. He's 6-6 with a 4.43 ERA in 14 career starts vs. the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Suter pitched six innings of one-run ball in his fourth start in place of the injured Chase Anderson on Saturday. He struggled the last time he faced the Cubs on April 8, allowing four earned runs on four hits and two walks in one inning of relief.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana has posted a quality start in both of his outings with the Cubs. He admitted to being a little nervous in his first home start but settled down to work six innings. This will be his second career start at Miller Park and first since 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra only tossed four innings in his last start on Sunday, allowing five earned runs in a losing decision to the Phillies. He has yet to face the Cubs this season, but he made two quality starts (1-0) against them in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks' last outing was his first off the disabled list. He'd been sidelined with soreness in his right hand. Getting back on his five-day routine is key. He's 1-0 vs. the Brewers this season, but he has given up eight earned runs over 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davies is 1-1 against the Cubs and 6-4 with a 6.45 ERA at Miller Park this season. He earned a win in one of his best starts this season at Wrigley Field on July 6, surrendering just two earned runs on five hits with no walks over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in two starts since the break. He hit four batters in his last start, including three in one inning to load the bases. The best news for the Cubs is that he did not give up a home run (he's given up 25 this year).

home_pitcher_note: Lester is coming off a win over the White Sox, which was his third straight quality start. He gave up four hits over seven innings in that outing to finish July with a 3-2 record and 4.55 ERA. He's 4-3 with a 3.57 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin is riding a two-start winning streak. Last time out against the Braves, he allowed two runs in six innings. Over his last seven starts he has a 2.81 ERA and has lowered his season ERA from 5.19 to 4.36.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is 3-1 with a 2.25 ERA in his past five starts, including a strong outing vs the White Sox. He gave up two hits in 6 2/3 innings and was happy with his fastball command.
away_pitcher_note: Godley tossed seven shutout innings against the Cardinals his last time out. He began his career in the Cubs' organization, traded to the D-backs in the Miguel Montero deal prior to the 2015 season.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana took his first Cubs loss in his last start despite posting a quality start. The lefty gave up two runs to the Brewers over six innings. More exciting was Quintana collected his first hit with a single to right. Yes, he got the ball.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke completed seven innings in four of his past five starts, going 4-0 with a 2.12 ERA in July. The last time out, Greinke allowed one run on four hits and a walk with nine strikeouts over seven innings in a 7-1 win at St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers, holding them to one run on six hits over five-plus innings. This will be his third start since coming off the DL. He's still building up arm strength since the time off.
away_pitcher_note: Roark, from nearby Wilmington, Ill., will take the mound at Wrigley Field for the fifth time in his career (fourth start). He owns a 3.38 ERA there. Roark is trying to bounce back after giving up four runs in five innings, with four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey posted a quality start in his last outing over the Brewers, and finished the month of July 3-0 with a 3.27 ERA, striking out 16 over 22 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson played with the Cubs from 2013-15 and will make his first start at Wrigley Field since '14. He put together his best start as a National on Sunday, allowing one run over seven innings in a win over the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Lester hit his first Major League home run and collected his 2,000th career strikeout in his last start against the D-backs. But the lefty was mad at himself because he didn't go deep in the game, throwing 104 pitches over four-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fedde made his long-awaited Major League debut Sunday. The right-hander allowed seven runs over four innings, but his stuff looked better than the results showed as he struggled finishing batters off after throwing two strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Moore again felt frustrated in his last start when he allowed four runs in five innings against the A's. He's  still in search of his first win since June 20.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta is coming off one of his best outings of the season, holding the D-backs to one earned run over seven innings. He has a 2.08 ERA in his last six starts. Arrieta was paired with new catcher Alex Avila; watch to see if they're together again.

home_pitcher_note: Blach lifted his first home run, a three-run shot, and pitched eight innings of two-run ball in one of the best performances of his young career. Since the start of July, Blach has a 3.34 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana had a rough outing in his last start against the D-backs, giving up six runs over five innings. The problem was location -- the lefty simply could not execute his pitches well.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has thrived more on the road than at home. In five starts away from AT&T Park, he owns a 2.31 ERA and a 5.33 strikeout-to-walk ratio. His corresponding numbers in four home starts are 3.70 and 4.80.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks matched a season high by going seven innings in his last start against the Nationals. He also posted his sixth quality start of the season, but first since May 24. He was encouraged by the outing, his third since coming off the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Walker threw six innings and surrendered three earned runs in a no-decision on Aug. 5. He struck out 32 in 29.2 innings with a 3.64 ERA in the month of July.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is 4-0 with a 3.00 ERA since the All-Star break, and he has won four straight starts for the first time since July 9-27, 2011. He's healthy after battling some foot problems in the first half of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has allowed 14 runs in nine innings during his first two starts of August, but just 10 of those runs were earned. He struck out 10 batters over six innings against the Giants in an Aug. 6 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lester posted his 14th quality start in his last outing, but did not get a decision. He held the Nationals to three runs over 6 2/3 innings. In five starts since the All-Star break, he has a 3.03 ERA. He's 4-3 with a 4.25 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Godley has struck out 10 and allowed just three runs in 12 2/3 innings in August this season. He is 5-4 with a 2.94 ERA on the year with a 1.02 WHIP.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta is 3-1 with a 2.20 ERA in five starts since the All-Star break. He's coming off a win against the Giants in which he gave up two earned runs over 6 1/3 innings. He faced the D-backs on Aug. 2 and lost, despite posting a quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana regressed slightly over his past two starts after three strong outings to begin his Cubs tenure, allowing six runs vs. Arizona and four runs (three earned) vs. the Giants. That said, he's completed six innings in four of those five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wojciechowski took a shutout into the sixth inning but threw a season-high 92 pitches and tired in his final frame with two homers allowed. But the club was thrilled with his performance overall, and use of a three pitches and good location.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is 0-1 with a 2.57 ERA in four starts since the All-Star break. He did not get a decision in his last outing vs. the Giants in which he gave up one run over 4 2/3 innings but was pulled after throwing 96 pitches. He beat the Reds on May 17.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo has continued to impress manager Bryan Price by keeping the team in most games he pitches. Castillo worked into the seventh inning vs. the Padres in a no-decision. His only problem was a four-hit fifth inning, but the Reds won the game.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey is 5-0 with a 3.42 ERA in five starts since the All-Star break. He's struck out 23 over 26 1/3 innings. However,  he has only one quality start, and would like to go deeper in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Reds manager Bryan Price referred to Bailey as being fatigued following an 11-10 win where the right-hander pitched five innings and allowed two runs. He’s had three elbow surgeries since 2014, and has found it tough to find consistency on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Lester's third start against the Reds this season. He's given up eight earned runs over 11 2/3 innings in two previous starts and is 1-0. He's coming off a loss to the D-backs in which he gave up three earned runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman wasn’t too rusty but not overly sharp either over his four innings and 83 pitches in his first start since going on the DL July 18 with a right knee injury. But he was hurt by a Travis Shaw three-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta will open an Interleague series against the Blue Jays at Wrigley. He's now 4-1 with a 2.09 ERA since the break after picking up a win over the D-backs in his last start. The key? Fastball command.
away_pitcher_note: Happ is on a roll lately, having allowed just one run in each of his last three outings. The veteran lefty has surrendered more than three earned runs just twice since the start of June and hasn't lost since late July.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana had a tough time with his fastball command in his last start. He did get the win, his third with the Cubs, giving up one earned run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Tepesch hung onto his spot in the rotation by allowing just one run over six-plus innings vs. the Cubs in his last start. That was enough to pick up his first big-league victory since September of 2014. His job is safe until Joe Biagini returns.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks threw six scoreless innings in his last outing against the Reds, striking out six. He was encouraged by his fastball command and an uptick in velocity. In his last five starts, he has a 2.00 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Sanchez tossed five innings of two-run ball with seven hits and two walks against six strikeouts. Though he didn't pitch against the Cubs last season, Sanchez owns a career 3-2 record and a 3.82 ERA against Chicago.

away_pitcher_note: Wainwright rebounded from a rough debut to throw seven strong innings against the Brewers last time out. His next outing will be the 36-year-old's 35th career start against the rival Cubs.

away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals' most consistent starter in the early going, Weaver roared out of the gate after a strong spring. Now the righty (2-0, 2.08) eyes his first career win against the rival Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: For five innings in his last start, Gray held the Nationals to one run and pitched out of some two-out jams. But he yielded four runs and didn't escape the sixth, and his frustrating early season continued.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks posted a quality start in his last outing against the Pirates but took the loss, serving up a pair of home runs for the second straight outing. The problem was fastball command that the righty said will be his focus between starts.

away_pitcher_note: Darvish was fine through the first four innings in his last outing, but a balk call against him in the 5th created some frustration and led to a loss. He's failed to pitch past the 5th in two of his three starts. This will be his 1st game at Coors.

home_pitcher_note: A devastating combination of a mid-to-upper 90s fastball and a mid 70s curve helped Marquez baffle the Pirates to the tune of two hits and six strikeouts in six innings of a win in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Quintana pitched 2 1/3 innings, his shortest start since Sept. 2, 2013, vs. the Yanks. Part of the problem was the weather as it was wet and cold at Wrigley.

away_pitcher_note: The Cubs like what they've seen of Chatwood's pitches, but he needs to improve his command. He walked seven and struck out seven over 4 2/3 innings in his most recent outing, against the Cards. He's 0-1 in three games (two starts) vs. the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer will be tasked with outdueling Cubs lefty Jon Lester. Bauer has completed at least seven innings and allowed three or fewer earned runs in each of his last three starts.

away_pitcher_note: Suter has allowed 31 hits over 25 1/3 innings and opponents are hitting .295 against him. He escaped with a no-decision on Saturday against the Marlins despite allowing five runs in five innings. Suter has yet to complete six innings this season.

away_pitcher_note: Guerra is coming off a strong outing -- one unearned run over five innings against the Marlins. He has given up just one earned run with 15 strikeouts over 16 innings in three starts since being called up from Triple-A.

away_pitcher_note: Davies only surrendered two runs in six innings against the Royals on Tuesday, but he got away with some hard-hit outs. He last faced the Cubs on April 7 and allowed one run in six innings and struck out eight.

away_pitcher_note: Freeland was struck on the left heel by a line drive in his previous start, but won't miss any time. In a season-long seven-inning stint vs. San Diego, he shut out the Padres on three hits while striking out eight.

away_pitcher_note: Looking to put together a second consecutive quality start for the first time this season, Gray seeks consistency vs. the Cubs. He’s coming off his second scoreless start against the Padres, shutting them out on three hits over six innings.

away_pitcher_note: Scheduled to make this start after suffering from lightheadedness and a heartbeat issue, Anderson returns to the mound with a clean bill of health. Anderson couldn’t catch his breath after warming up for the second and was taken out as a precaution.

away_pitcher_note: Quintana threw seven scoreless innings against Milwaukee in his last outing. It was his 15th career start of at least seven scoreless innings, and third with the Cubs. He's 3-0 with a 3.13 ERA in four career starts vs. the Cardinals.

away_pitcher_note: Chatwood is coming off a stellar win against the Brewers in which he gave up two hits over seven scoreless innings. He relied on his two-seam fastball, and will continue to do so, to get ground balls and strikeouts.

away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Rockies, Lester did not give up an earned run for the third time in six starts this season. He's 3-1 with a 1.63 ERA in six career starts in St. Louis.

away_pitcher_note: Transitioning to the rotation has gone smoothly for Garcia. He has allowed a combined 10 hits, the fewest total by any pitcher in franchise history over his 1st 4 career starts. In 23 innings as a starter, Garcia has given up 2 runs.

away_pitcher_note: Urena faced the Cubs on Opening Day, and he gets them again while seeking his first win. In the opener, he allowed five runs in four innings. But in his past two starts, Urena has given up three runs (two earned) with 11 strikeouts in 14 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Chen got hurt by back-to-back 1st-inning homers in his last start on Friday in Cincinnati. He also walked 4 batters over 4 innings in his 2nd start since returning from the DL. Chen will make his 1st career appearance at Wrigley Field.

away_pitcher_note: Fulmer has been up and down in his most recent starts. Two starts ago on April 28, he tossed seven shutout innings, but last start, he struggled through 3 2/3 innings allowing 5 runs (4 earned). It’s his first career start vs. the Cubs.

away_pitcher_note: Shields flirted with perfection his last time out, retiring the first 16 batters he faced, but ended up with a tough-luck loss. The veteran righty pitched vs. the Cubs last year, giving up 5 runs (3 earned) in 4 innings at Guaranteed Rate Field.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is 2-0 with a 4.70 ERA in three home starts. The lefty is coming off a win over the Marlins in which he gave up one run over six innings. He has three quality starts out of his seven outings.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran’s velocity has dipped, but he has generated more action with both of his fastballs and his slider.  The veteran has relied on consistent command as he’s completed at least six innings of scoreless ball in three of his past four starts.

away_pitcher_note: This will be Darvish's first start since May 2. He was scratched from his last outing because of flu-like symptoms, and he was placed on the 10-day DL. He lost to the Braves on April 13, when he gave up four runs on nine hits over 4 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Hendricks did not walk a batter over six in his last outing yet took the loss vs. the White Sox. It was his fourth straight quality start. He's 4-1 with a 3.41 ERA in 10 career starts vs. the Reds, but is 1-1 with a 5.70 ERA in four starts at GABP.

away_pitcher_note: Darvish exited after the fourth inning of his most recent start, in Atlanta on May 15, with cramping in his right calf after giving up one run on three hits, with five strikeouts and two walks.

away_pitcher_note: Bauer had his best outing of the season in Detroit on May 16, throwing eight shutout innings, allowing four hits with 10 strikeouts and no walks. In three May starts, Bauer has a 2.89 ERA with 21 strikeouts in 18 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Plutko will be called up from Triple-A to make his second MLB start. At Columbus, he made seven starts, going 4-3 with a 2.25 ERA. The right-hander held Toronto to three runs over 7 1/3 innings in his first start on May 3.

away_pitcher_note: Holland will try to be more effective vs. the Cubs than in his previous outing, a 6-1 loss to Colorado. Over six innings, he gave up four runs on six hits, and his 112 pitches were the most he’s thrown since Sept. 5, 2015, vs. the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is coming off a stellar outing vs. the Reds in which he gave up one hit over seven scoreless innings. This will be his third career start vs. the Giants. He's 0-2 with a 4.97 ERA so far, with both games at AT&T Park.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Bruce Bochy wants his starters to go deeper in games and that includes Stratton, who has not gone more than five innings in each of his past three starts, though the past two were wins.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood will start in place of Yu Darvish, who went on the DL with triceps tendinitis. In Chatwood's last start, he walked 6 over 2 2/3 innings and took the loss vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Blach isn’t getting a lot of swings and misses, as opponents are batting .295 against him over 11 starts, and he has only 27 strikeouts in 57 2/3 innings. He gave up eight hits and four runs in 4 1/3 innings in his last outing, a no-decision.

away_pitcher_note: Hendricks pitched seven innings and allowed one run on two hits in his last outing vs. the Giants as he returned to form following a four-run (three earned), five-inning outing in Cincinnati in his previous start.

home_pitcher_note: After proving to be a key contributor out of the bullpen, Lugo will make his first start of the season. He had recorded 17 consecutive scoreless innings with 19 strikeouts as a reliever before allowing three runs in his last outing.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana has been unable to pitch 5 innings in 3 of his last 5 starts, including Saturday vs. the Giants, when he was pulled after 4 1/3 innings. He struck out 6 in his brief outing. He's 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in 2 career starts vs. the Mets.

away_pitcher_note: Lester is coming off a win vs. the Bucs in which he not only struck out 6 over 6 innings but collected 2 hits himself. Even better, the lefty didn't walk a batter. He's 5-1 with a 3.83 ERA in 7 career starts vs. the Mets, including 5 quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks took the loss in his last outing vs. the Bucs, giving up 2 runs over 5 IP. He said the start was more of a battle mentally than anything else. He'll be back at Wrigley Field, where he's 3-3 with a 2.38 ERA in 6 starts so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: This is a big start for Eflin, who has a 8.10 ERA (12 earned runs in 13 1/3 innings) in his past three starts. The Phillies have Enyel De Los Santos, Cole Irvin and Ben Lively all throwing well in Triple-A, who could all replace him in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana threw six scoreless innings in his last start against the Mets. It was the fourth time this season that he didn't give up an earned run while throwing at least six innings. He's 4-2 with a 2.62 ERA on the road, 2-2 with a 6.66 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Gabe Kapler called Nola one of the top 10 pitchers in baseball. The numbers back him up. Nola’s .521 opponents’ OPS and 2.18 ERA are two of the lowest marks in baseball.

away_pitcher_note: Pivetta struggled Friday vs. the Giants, allowing three runs in four innings. But since he allowed six runs in one inning May 4 vs. the Nats, he has a 1.93 ERA in his last five starts. He has 35 strikeouts and seven walks in 28 innings in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery will stay in the rotation while the Cubs wait and see with Yu Darvish, who is on the DL with inflammation in his right triceps. Montgomery has been stellar in his two starts, giving up one earned run over 11 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl has made three straight quality starts, allowing four runs in his last 18 innings while holding opponents to a .626 OPS. One of those starts was against the Cubs, who managed only one run on four hits and four walks over six innings on May 28.

home_pitcher_note: Lester threw seven shutout innings in his last start against the Mets. He's on a good roll, compiling a 1.94 ERA in his last nine starts. The lefty has given up one earned run or fewer in seven of his 12 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first two starts, Pittsburgh has lost each of Kingham’s last three outings even though he's allowed three earned runs while pitching at least five frames each time. Kingham gave up three runs in 5 2/3 innings vs. the Cubs on May 29.

away_pitcher_note: Nova will return from the disabled list (sprained right ring finger) to start Sunday. After a solid April, Nova posted a 7.61 ERA in May. The veteran righty allowed only three runs over seven innings and beat the Cubs at Wrigley Field on April 10.

away_pitcher_note: Montgomery has made it no secret he wants to start, and he's doing a good job subbing for Yu Darvish. He is 2-0 in 3 starts, yielding 2 earned runs in 17 2/3 innings. In his last outing vs. the Pirates, he threw a season-high 95 pitches in 6 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is having a career year, having won his last eight decisions. Wacha has faced the Cubs once this season, and the Cardinals won 4-3 on May 6. He allowed two runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander will make his third start since returning from the DL on Saturday against the Cubs. The Cardinals went 4-1 when Martinez pitched against Chicago in 2017.

away_pitcher_note: Quintana has given up two runs or fewer in three straight starts for the first time since June 2017. In his last start, he limited the Brewers to two runs, both on solo homers, over six innings. Quintana is 4-2 with a 2.68 ERA in seven road starts.

away_pitcher_note: In his return against Texas, Maeda showed no signs of the strained right hip that put him on the DL. He did walk three (one intentionally) and hit a batter, but he said he felt healthy and the club expects more this time.

away_pitcher_note: Quintana is coming off a loss to the Cardinals in which he gave up two runs over five innings. The lefty has given up two runs or fewer in five of his last six starts. He beat the Reds on May 19, giving up one hit over seven scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani, coming off the longest outing of his abbreviated season, will take the mound for the fourth time since returning from the DL earlier this month. The right-hander yielded two runs on three hits over 5 2/3 innings last Sunday in Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Luke Farrell will make his first start of 2018. The right-hander, who was named the starter following Friday's game, has made 12 relief appearances this year, allowing allowing seven earned runs over 17 1/3 innings for a 3.63 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Romano has strung together two solid outings, most recently on Tuesday against the Tigers, during which he yielded four hits over seven shutout innings. In his past two starts, Romano has allowed one run over 15 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery gets the call in place of Tyler Chatwood, whose wife went into labor on Sunday morning. Montgomery is 2-1 with a 1.21 ERA as a starter this season (five starts).

home_pitcher_note: Maeda needs to improve off a flat effort at Wrigley Field, where he walked five in 3 2/3 innings of a no-decision. It was his second start off the DL with a hip strain. As other injured starters return, Maeda could be headed to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs will call up Underwood to make his MLB debut vs. the Dodgers. Underwood, the club’s second-round pick in the 2012 Draft, is 3-7 with a 4.27 ERA over 14 games (13 starts) this year for Triple-A, allowing 34 earned runs over 71 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Stripling threw a quality start at the Cubs, but wasn’t as sharp as he had been and a six-game win streak was snapped. Now he gets the Cubs again with a chance to show he can quickly adjust and start another win streak for his longshot All-Star bid.
away_pitcher_note: Lester will be given an extra day of rest and will pitch the second game. The lefty threw 119 pitches in a win on Wednesday vs. the Dodgers, allowing five hits over seven scoreless innings. He has pitched at least six frames in seven straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has struggled through the first half, but he contained the Mets until a sixth-inning home run by Jose Bautista. More importantly, Wood’s postgame comments finally turned positive and his confidence could be returning.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks walked four on Friday in Cincinnati, allowing four earned runs over 5 2/3 innings in a loss. The righty has faced the Dodgers three times in his career, going 2-1 with a 3.15 ERA. Hendricks is 2-2 with a 4.78 ERA on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw allowed two runs on five hits with four strikeouts over three innings against the Mets on Saturday in his first start since going on the disabled list with lower back discomfort on June 1. He threw 55 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana took the loss in his most recent outing Friday in Cincinnati, allowing four earned runs over five innings with two walks and three K's. The lefty has faced the Dodgers twice in his career, both starts, and hasn't allowed a run in 14 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery will make his seventh start of the season in the series opener. In his last start, he gave up four runs over six innings, his first rough start since moving to the rotation. In his five other starts, he'd given up four runs total.
away_pitcher_note: Berrios has been on an impressive run with a 2.05 ERA over his last eight outings. He struck out 12 Rangers over seven scoreless innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood will make his first start since June 19 -- and first as a new daddy. He welcomed his first child last Sunday and returns from paternity leave. Chatwood still leads the National League in walks.
away_pitcher_note: Mejia is set to be called up from Triple-A Rochester to make his season debut. He's been on a roll at Triple-A Rochester, going 4-1 with a 1.41 ERA in five starts in June after missing time with a blister issue.

home_pitcher_note: Lester may hate to see the calendar turn to July. He went 5-0 with a 1.13 ERA in five June starts, holding batters to a .155 average. He's 4-1 with a 1.25 ERA at Wrigley Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn struck out eight in five innings against the White Sox, but ran into trouble in the sixth and was charged with five runs (four earned) in a loss last time out. But he still has a 2.83 ERA in five June starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off an abbreviated start against the Dodgers in which he lasted 2 2/3 innings. He gave up six runs in that short span on eight hits. The right-hander has a 2.96 ERA in eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer has settled into form just in time for trade speculation. He took the loss last Thursday against Oakland, but tied a season high with eight innings, the last four scoreless with one hit allowed. He has three walks over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana did not get a decision in his last outing against the Dodgers, giving up three runs over 5 1/3 innings. He has not won a game since May 31, going 0-2 with a 4.33 ERA in five June starts. He's 2-2 with a 6.00 ERA in six home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano remains winless since his strong April, including losses in each of his last three outings, but tossed a quality start Friday at Toronto with no hard-hit contact aside from Justin Smoak’s two-run homer. Expect trade interest to build.

home_pitcher_note: With Yu Darvish's status uncertain, Montgomery will make his 8th start. He's 3-1 with a 2.43 ERA in the rotation. He's made one start and pitched two games in relief vs. the Reds so far. In his start on June 24, he gave up four runs in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Mahle set a career high with 12 K's over only 5 2/3 frames, but got a no-decision in a 12-3 win over the Crew on Saturday. He had to work out of a couple of jams and wasn’t happy about that, but liked how his slider and fastball was working early on.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood will be making his second start since coming off the paternity list. In his last outing, he gave up seven runs over five innings vs. the Twins but the Cubs rallied. He still leads the Majors in walks with 66 free passes over 73 1/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Harvey had his best start of '18 in a win over the Crew on Sunday with 5 2/3 scoreless innings, two singles, no walks and six K's while throwing only 68 pitches. But he exited after a rain delay. He's won three straight for the first time since '15.

home_pitcher_note: Lester won his seventh in a row in his last outing vs. the Twins. He gave up two earned runs over five-plus frames. He also contributed at the plate, hitting a three-run HR to highlight an eight-run second. He's 5-1 with a 1.49 ERA in 8 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo arguably had his best start of 2018 as he took a shutout into the seventh inning vs. the White Sox on Monday. He earned a no-decision in the 5-3 win but allowed only one earned run and six hits over a season-high-tying 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 2.62 ERA across six June starts, Suarez dazzled in his first outing of July. The left-hander threw seven innings of one-run ball in Colorado, striking out six and walking none. Monday will be the rookie’s first time facing the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks will open the series in S.F. looking for his first win since June 16. The righty is 1-5 in his past seven starts. He's struggled with his fastball command although he felt a little better after his five-inning start vs. the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Holland has displayed decent stuff in his pair of outings since moving to the 'pen, fanning seven in 4 1/3 innings. He made his most recent start on July 1 at Arizona, surrendering three runs and seven hits in 3 2/3 innings in a Giants win.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana got his first win since May 31 in his last start vs. the Tigers. He posted a quality start, the first by a Cubs pitcher since Jon Lester on June 20. Quintana is 0-3 with a 5.82 ERA in three starts vs. the Giants, including a loss on May 26.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto has fared significantly better in his 106 lifetime day starts (47-27, .635 winning percentage, 2.76 ERA) than in his 183 performances at night (78-57, .578, 3.63). He has faced the Cubs 25 times, more than any other team.
away_pitcher_note: Last year, Montgomery totaled 69 2/3 innings in the first half. This year, he has 71 with one more start before the break. The lefty will try to finish the first half on a strong note after laboring (3 ER in 5 IP) in his last start vs. the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: The usually sturdy Richard is coming off his shortest start since May 2, but he made it through five solid innings in Arizona before he was lifted for a pinch-hitter. Richard is on pace to become the first Padre to throw 200 innings since 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood has been hit hard in his past two outings, giving up seven earned runs in each start. The right-hander will look to rebound at Petco Park, where he’s 4-1 with a 2.84 ERA in seven career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perdomo was rocked for five runs during a shaky fourth inning on Monday. Still, he managed to work through seven frames and help save a depleted ‘pen. Perdomo has showcased a vastly improved changeup since he was recalled from Triple-A on July 4.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off what was far and away his best start of the season. He threw 8 1/3 masterful innings Monday night, locating his fastball and generating seven swinging strikeouts on a devastating changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Lauer’s first half has been a tale of two halves. He posted a 7.67 ERA through Memorial Day, but he owns a 2.33 mark since then. The rookie left-hander is coming off his best start yet -- 8 2/3-innings of one-run ball vs. the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Lester has given up home runs in consecutive games for the first time this season. Despite that, the Cubs have won his past eight outings, and 15 of his 18 starts. The lefty is 2-1 lifetime with a 2.97 ERA against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is working on his fastball command. He has gone at least five innings in 18 of 19 starts and allowed three earned runs or fewer in 15 of those. But he hasn't gone as deep as the Cubs would like. He's 3-5 with a 3.18 ERA in nine home starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Reds got the best of the right-hander on Friday, accumulating six hits and three runs in five innings. Martinez had won the previous three outings, and the Cardinals need him to return to that form following the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Lester finished the first half tied with Aaron Nola and Max Scherzer for the most wins in the NL (12) and held the NL’s fourth best ERA (2.58). There's no place like Wrigley Field for the lefty, who is 5-1 with a 1.98 ERA in nine home starts.
away_pitcher_note: A rain delay chopped Flaherty’s recent start against the Reds to five innings, but the righty was convincing. His scoreless, two-hit start and ability to make pitches in big spots put the Cardinals in a winnable spot, though they fell 8-2.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood finished the first half as the Major League leader in walks (73 over 84 innings), and the Cubs are hoping the right-hander has better command in the second half. So far against the Cardinals, he's 0-1 in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver was solid in his last two starts, but the Cardinals only took one of those games. The White Sox shut out the Cardinals in Weaver’s most recent start, in which he twirled six innings allowing a single run and fanning seven.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery most likely didn't expect to have nine starts in the first half -- he began the season in the bullpen then stepped into the rotation when Yu Darvish was hurt. So far, Montgomery is 3-2 with a 3.20 ERA as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Gant put together a fine start against the Giants on July 6, allowing five hits and two runs in six innings. The Cardinals couldn't support Gant, though, and fell 3-2.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is 0-2 with a 2.00 ERA in two starts against the Cardinals. He has not fared well at Wrigley Field, posting a 3-2 record and 5.50 ERA in seven games (3.06 on the road). The lefty went 7-3 after the break last year.
away_pitcher_note: The All-Star right-hander tossed four innings last Sunday against the Reds. Mikolas gave up three runs on six hits, but the Cardinals backed him up with aggressive bats in a 6-4 win.

home_pitcher_note: Farrell will make his second start of 2018, filling in as the Cubs shuffle their rotation following Saturday's doubleheader. He's made six starts at Triple-A this season and one with the Cubs on June 23, when he gave up three runs over 2 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin made his second All-Star team but did not pitch Tuesday after his final pre-break start Sunday. He is among the NL leaders with 149 strikeouts and a 1.05 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks opened the second half against the Cardinals, throwing a season-high 113 pitches over 4 2/3 innings. He gave up three runs in that outing. He's 3-5 with a 3.38 ERA in 10 home starts. He has one quality start in his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Buchholz returns from the DL after straining his left oblique June 24 in Pittsburgh. Buchholz made one rehab appearance with Class A Visalia on July 19 and allowed two runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lester opened the second half with an abbreviated start, lasting three-plus innings against the Cardinals. He gave up a season-high eight earned runs in that outing and said he wasn't surprised to struggle because he's had some mechanical issues.
away_pitcher_note: Ray struggled in his last outing against the Rockies when he allowed five runs on eight hits over 5 1/3 innings. Ray has yet to rediscover the form from his All-Star season in 2017. Over his past four starts, his ERA is 7.65.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood may have walked six over 5 1/3 innings in his last outing against the Cardinals but he gave up only one hit. The right-hander is well aware that he needs to cut down on the walks: He leads the Majors with 79 over 89 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Godley is coming off a so-so outing against the Rockies where he allowed four runs (three earned) on five hits over five innings. He was outstanding in his two previous starts when he allowed just two runs over 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals plan to recall Weaver from Triple-A to face the Cubs for the second time in less than a week. The righty allowed three earned runs in four-plus frames in Saturday’s loss at Wrigley. He's 2-3 with a 5.08 ERA over his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery will have to deal with the Cards again. In his last start, he held them to one run on five hits over six innings and did not get a decision in the loss. This will be the lefty's 11th start subbing for Yu Darvish. He's 3-2 as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Cardinals interim manager Mike Shildt has been aggressive in pulling Mikolas, the club’s most reliable innings-eater for much of the first half. Mikolas has thrown just nine innings over his past two starts after averaging 6.4 over his first 18.
away_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see how Quintana bounces back after throwing 121 pitches in his last outing vs. the Cards. Working on extra rest, he gave up two runs over seven innings and got the win. The tweaks to his changeup have been working.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander blanked the Cubs over five innings last weekend in a 6-3 Cards win at Wrigley. He is 1-1 with a 2.22 in four starts since assuming Michael Wacha’s place in the rotation, and 3-3 with a 3.17 ERA in 13 appearances (7 starts) overall.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks has gone at least five innings in 19 of his 21 starts but hasn't gone much further than that, which means the bullpen has been busy. On Tuesday, Hendricks struck out eight, matching a season high, but he went only five innings vs. Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon is 5-4 with a 3.09 ERA over his last 11 starts, and he's held opponents to a .241 average and .647 OPS during that stretch. This will be Taillon's first start of the year against the Cubs; he has a 5.06 ERA against them in five career starts.
away_pitcher_note: The best thing about Lester's last outing was that he didn't walk anyone. He also lasted six-plus innings, which is what the Cubs needed. He's 7-1 with a 3.16 ERA on the road this season, and 2-0 with a 4.00 ERA in three starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Kingham didn’t have much in his last start Thursday vs. the Mets, falling behind in the count then getting hit hard as he allowed six runs on seven hits in three-plus innings. He’s given up five runs over 12 innings in two starts vs. the Cubs in '18.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Hamels' Cubs debut. The lefty last pitched on July 23. He's 3-3 against the Pirates in 10 career starts and 1-1 with a 1.22 ERA in five career starts at PNC Park. Hamels has done better on the road this season, posting a 4-2 record.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery will be making his 12th start subbing for Yu Darvish, and so far, he is 3-3 with a 3.50 ERA as a starter. In his last outing, he scattered a season-high 12 hits but said he felt good. He's 2-1 with a 4.93 ERA in 12 games at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander has been excellent in relief this season, having posted a 2.05 ERA in 27 appearances. But he owns a 14.14 mark in two starts. Erlin gets another crack at the rotation on Thursday, filling in for the injured Luis Perdomo.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana struggled with his command in his last outing, needing 51 pitches to get through the first inning against the Cardinals. He only lasted three innings in that outing. He'd been on a good roll before that outing, winning three in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Ross comes off another average outing, this one a five-inning start vs. Arizona where he gave up four runs on six hits. He pitched at least six frames in 13 of his 19 starts before the All-Star break, but has yet to pitch past the fifth inning since.

home_pitcher_note: If Hendricks could get through the first inning without giving up a run, he'd been in good shape. In his 22 starts so far, he's served up 21 runs, and 10 home runs. He did go seven innings in his last start, which was an improvement.
away_pitcher_note: Walker Lockett will make his second career start Saturday in place of Joey Lucchesi, who was scratched due to a stomach illness. Lockett was roughed up in his first start on June 1, when he allowed four runs in 3 2/3 innings vs. Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Lester had some command issues in his last outing against the Pirates, in which he gave up four runs over five innings. He's 5-2 with a 2.97 ERA at Wrigley Field, so maybe being home will help. He beat the Padres on July 15 in San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Joey Lucchesi (5-6, 3.74 ERA) will start on Sunday after being scratched Saturday due to a stomach bug. He allowed a career high five runs in his last outing. His breaking ball wasn’t working and he relied too much on his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Junis will open the series against the Cubs as the Royals return to Kansas City. He got his first win since May 18 on Wednesday against the White Sox, allowing four runs across 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels made a good first impression in his Cubs debut, striking out nine over five innings. Acquired from the Rangers, he has faced the Royals twice this year and is 1-1, including a win on June 19 in Kansas City when he struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Keller struggled through an up-and-down July, but got off to a strong start in August. The rookie racked up a career-high nine strikeouts as he held the Tigers to two runs over 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery changed the grip on his curveball and he was pleased with how it felt in his last outing against the Padres. He is 2-0 in three games (two starts) against the Royals, including a complete game on June 23, 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Fillmyer went three innings against the Twins before a 91-minute delay forced the Royals to turn to their bullpen on Friday. Fillmyer has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of his three starts since joining the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs have stressed the importance of throwing first-pitch strikes to Quintana, and he listened, getting a win over the Padres his last time out. Against the Royals, Quintana is 3-9 with a 4.05 ERA in 24 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks has struck out at least seven batters in each of his past three outings. He picked up the win in his last start against the Padres and felt good about his curveball, which catcher Willson Contreras keeps encouraging him to use.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson allowed two runs over 5 2/3 innings in a win over the Reds on Saturday. The right-hander is 1-1 with a 7.59 ERA in two career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Lester was an All-Star in the first half, going 12-2 with a 2.58 ERA. In four starts since the break, he's 0-2 with an 8.53 ERA. The Cubs have won one of those outings. He did not get a decision vs. the Nats in two starts in the NLDS last October.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling for more than a month, Roark has shined in his part three starts, allowing a combined two runs over 22 innings. The right-hander is 1-0 with a 1.46 ERA during his past two starts against the Cubs, dating back to 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is 2-0 and has given up one earned run over 11 innings with the Cubs. He's 16-9 with a 2.67 ERA vs. the Nats, but hasn't faced them since 2015. This will be his Wrigley Field debut as a Cub and first game there since July 17, 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer allowed only one run over seven innings against the Braves on Tuesday, but the Nats' offense managed only one run of support. The right-hander is 3-1 with a 2.92 ERA in six career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is coming off a frustrating outing vs. the Royals, in which he gave up five runs over 6 1/3 innings and had trouble with his command. He's 2-0 with a 0.95 ERA in four starts vs. the Brewers this year, yielding two runs over 19 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin looks to regain his July form in the opener vs. the Cubs. Chacin was 4-0 with a 2.64 ERA in five July starts, but has allowed 11 earned runs in 10 1/3 innings this month. In his last start vs. the Cubs on June 13, he hurled six shutout frames.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks did not get a decision in his last start against the Nationals, but he did record his team-leading 11th quality start. He has not walked a batter in three straight starts for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra looks to continue his good work vs. the Cubs this season. In two starts, Guerra has fired 12 innings with a 1.50 ERA and 10 strikeouts. For his career, Guerra has a 1.89 ERA in 19 innings vs. the Cubs with 22 strikeouts and a .194 BAA.

home_pitcher_note: Nova has put together a 3.88 ERA in 11 starts since coming off the DL in early June, and the Pirates have won eight of those games. He last faced the Cubs on June 10 at Wrigley Field, allowing one run with eight strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester has posted a 10.32 ERA in five starts since the All-Star break. His most recent outing was the worst of the bunch, when he allowed nine runs (eight earned) in 3 2/3 innings vs. the Nats. Opponents are hitting .383 off him in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Williams has allowed only two runs in 29 innings over his last five outings, a stretch capped by his start of seven scoreless innings on Saturday at AT&T Park. Williams allowed one run on four hits over six innings at Wrigley Field on April 12.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels made his first start for the Cubs against the Pirates on Aug. 1 and struck out nine over five innings, picking up the win. The lefty has given up two earned runs over 18 innings in three starts with the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Musgrove has completed seven innings in five of his last seven starts while posting a 2.70 ERA during that stretch, yet the Pirates have won only three of those starts. Musgrove held the Cubs to one run over seven innings on May 30 at PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood will make a spot start in place of injured Mike Montgomery. Chatwood began the year in the rotation and made 19 starts, posting a 4-5 record with a 4.98 ERA. He's struggled with his command, leading MLB with 90 walks issued this season.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon struggled through one rough inning but put together a quality start in Tuesday’s 5-2 loss to the Twins at Target Field. He is 7-5 with a 3.15 ERA over his past 14 starts, but just 3-3 with a 4.86 ERA in six career starts vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: It's been a rough stretch for Quintana, who has allowed 17 runs in 20 1/3 innings over his past four starts. The three home runs he gave up in his last outing were the most he's surrendered in a game since Aug. 3, 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann is 1-4 with a 5.96 ERA in five starts since the All-Star break, yielding a .978 OPS to opposing hitters in that span. His curveball, which has been inconsistent since the break, tends to be the indicator of his success this summer.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks matched a season high with eight K's in his last start vs. the Crew. He's 4-1 with a 3.78 ERA and 51 K's over 47 2/3 innings in his past eight starts. He faced Detroit on July 3 at Wrigley and did not get a decision, giving up three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano turned in a quality start against the Cubs last month at Wrigley Field despite five walks and two homers over six innings. But his loss in that game began a midsummer downturn. He's now 0-4 with a 6.37 ERA in his last eight games.
away_pitcher_note: Lester struggled coming out of the All-Star break, but he appeared to return to form his last time out. He struck out eight batters without issuing a walk over six scoreless innings against the Pirates last Thursday at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Hamels' fifth start for the Cubs and his second at Wrigley. The lefty has given up two earned runs over 25 innings in his four previous outings. He has not faced the Reds since 2016 and is 10-1 with a 1.93 ERA in 15 starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: DeSclafani has allowed two earned runs, 15 hits and two walks while striking out 16 over the last three starts (21 1/3 innings) for a 0.83 ERA. He's been able to get early swings in counts and induce weaker contact.

home_pitcher_note: Alec Mills will make his first big league start. The right-hander was 5-12 with a 4.84 ERA in 23 starts at Triple-A Iowa. In his last outing on Aug. 18 against Oklahoma City, he gave up two runs over six innings, striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: In a 7-1 win over the Giants on Saturday, Harvey had a no-hitter for 5 2/3 innings and was finished after 6 1/3 scoreless innings with four hits, one walk and five strikeouts. His last two starts have been solid as he continues to rebuild his resume.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is 1-2 with a 4.84 ERA in four August starts. The lefty has faced the Reds twice this year at Great American Ball Park and is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA, giving up four earned runs over 12 innings. He's 5-3 with a 5.00 ERA at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo has come on strong of late. After his quality start against the Giants on Sunday, he has a 2.96 ERA over his last eight outings. He's showing an ability to throw three pitches over the plate for strikes, including his slider and changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks deserved better after his last start in which he held the Tigers to two runs over seven innings. The right-hander has given up three or fewer earned runs in 20 of his 26 starts. He's 0-1 in two starts vs. the Reds this season.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey turned in a quality start of three earned runs allowed over six innings but was a 5-2 loser vs. the Crew on Monday. The Reds have lost 16 of Bailey’s 17 starts this season and all six of his quality starts. The righty is winless since May 12.

home_pitcher_note: Lester picked up his second win since the All-Star break in his last outing, holding the Tigers to one run over 5 2/3 innings. On June 3, he threw seven shutout innings against the Mets in New York, giving up two hits and striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Syndergaard submitted his best start of a disappointing month last time out, holding the Giants to two runs in six innings to lower his August ERA to 4.50. Syndergaard will close the month against the Cubs, whom he has not faced since 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has been hot, giving up three earned runs over 34 innings for an 0.79 ERA in five starts with the Cubs. He's coming off a complete-game win over the Reds. The lefty threw a season-high 114 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: deGrom’s quest for the National League Cy Young Award will continue in an unfriendly environment for pitchers: Wrigley Field, where he holds a 7.20 ERA in two career starts. In five August outings, deGrom is 3-2 with a 1.26 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his first MLB start, Mills fanned eight over 5 2/3 innings vs. the Mets. He'll stay in the rotation another turn. What was Mills' goal? He said: "I just wanted to come up here and eat as many innings as possible and give us a chance to win."
away_pitcher_note: Quietly solid of late, Vargas has produced a 2.08 ERA over his last three starts to lower his overall mark to a season-low 6.96. Key to Vargas’ improvement has been control; he’s walked just three batters in 17 1/3 innings over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has posted a 1.38 ERA  in five August starts. The All-Star righty limited the Cubs to an unearned run and three hits over five innings on May 15.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery will make his first appearance since Aug. 11 when he's activated from the DL for this makeup game. As a starter, Montgomery is 4-3 with a 3.08 ERA. He's had success in Atlanta. On July 19, 2017, he hit his only big league home run there.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies tout Pivetta’s FIP and xFIP, but the overall results have not been there lately. He has allowed 11 runs in 10 1/3 innings in his last two starts. He has a 5.92 ERA in 11 appearances (10 starts) since late June.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani gave up two runs over 4 2/3 innings in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday. He is 4-3 with a 3.91 ERA in 12 career starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Davies allowed one run over five innings against the Reds Saturday, putting the final touch on a stellar May (1.72 ERA in six starts). The righty lowered his season ERA to 4.65 from 9.47 in that span. He had a 2.25 ERA in two starts vs. the Giants in 2020.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir will be activated off the restricted list and make his third appearance and second start of the year for the Giants. He'll fill in for Logan Webb, who landed on the injured list with a right shoulder sprain on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta yielded five runs (two earned) in 3 2/3 innings of a loss to the Reds on Sunday at home. The veteran has a 6.65 ERA in his last five starts after posting a 2.57 ERA in his first five outings this year. He has a 5.68 ERA in five road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman departed his last start Sunday after six innings with hip tightness, but he isn't expected to miss a turn in the rotation. He earned NL Pitcher of the Month honors in May after going 5-0 with a 0.73 ERA over six starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his Cubs and season debut on Monday, Stewart allowed one unearned run over five innings in a win over San Diego. The righty generated nine outs via grounder with a heavy sinker-cutter combination. He struck out two and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto fired seven innings of one-run ball in his last start against the Angels on Monday. He is 9-9 with a 3.41 ERA over 26 career starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks logged a quality start on Tuesday against the Padres, improving to 4-0 with a 2.60 ERA in his last four starts. The righty has 21 strikeouts and one walk in 27 2/3 innings in that span. He is 3-1 with a 4.26 ERA on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Weathers endured his roughest outing as a big leaguer against the Cubs on Tuesday, allowing four runs over five innings. Still, he's been one of the most effective rookies in the sport, and he's allowed four runs, total, in four starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Alzolay beat the Padres at home in his last start, allowing one run in five innings with seven strikeouts and one walk. The righty has a 1.53 ERA with 19 strikeouts against four walks in his past three outings (17 2/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Lamet looked like vintage Lamet vs. the Cubs on Wednesday, with a lively fastball and a biting slider. The Padres have limited his workload after his elbow injury in September. He hasn't thrown more than four innings in any 2021 outing.
away_pitcher_note: Davies lost on the road to the Giants on Thursday, giving up four runs on eight hits in 4 1/3 innings. Even so, the right-hander has a 2.52 ERA in his past seven starts (35 2/3 innings). He has a 6.75 ERA on the road in '21.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish was a Cy Young contender with the Cubs last season before he was dealt to the Padres for Zach Davies and four prospects. Sure enough, Darvish has looked every bit a Cy Young candidate again, and the Padres have won 11 of his 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta lasted just two innings on Friday, allowing six runs on six hits, including a pair of homers, to the Giants. The righty noted that he was pitching through illness. He has an 8.28 ERA in his past six starts after posting a 2.57 ERA in his first five.

home_pitcher_note: Stewart last started on June 5, allowing three runs in 3 2/3 innings of a road loss to the Giants. He gave up no earned runs over five on May 31 vs. the Padres. Stewart was optioned to Triple-A, but recalled to fill in for the injured Adbert Alzolay.
away_pitcher_note: Oviedo was pitching as sharp as he had been all season last time out but was yanked early when the Reds were threatening at the plate. home_pitcher_note: Hendricks beat the Cardinals on May 21 in St. Louis as part of his most recent seven-start stretch, in which he is 6-1 with a 3.13 ERA. On Sunday in San Francisco, the righty allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings with five strikeouts and three walks.
away_pitcher_note: Gant will look to move past his toughest outing of the year, when he set a season-high in earned runs (seven) and tied a season-low in innings (four) vs. the Reds. Continuing to be of concern is the walks, with nine over his last three starts and an MLB-leading 37 overall.

home_pitcher_note: Davies logged six shutout innings to beat the Padres on the road on Tuesday, ending with four strikeouts, two walks and one hit allowed. The righty has a 2.16 ERA in his last eight turns, including five shutout frames in St. Louis on May 23.
away_pitcher_note: Martínez took a modest step forward his last time out, though he was still tagged for five runs over four innings. The right-hander has struggled as of late, with 18 earned runs over his last six innings across three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets are committed to keeping Peterson in the rotation despite a 9.88 ERA over his last four starts. Although the Mets don't have a wealth of alternative options, Peterson will need to turn things around quickly if he wants to stick.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta had a strong bounceback start on Wednesday, holding the Padres to one run over five innings. He struck out six and walked one. The veteran had an 8.28 ERA in his previous six turns. Arrieta is 3-3 with a 6.40 ERA in seven road starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Walker has had periodic control problems, but really that's just quibbling. Overall, he's been one of the best starting pitchers in the National League and one of last offseason's best free-agent signings, with a 1.32 ERA in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mills recently returned from an IL stint due to a back issue. The righty has spent the bulk of this year in the bullpen, with his lone start (four innings, two runs) falling on April 13 against Milwaukee. He was 5-5 with a 4.48 ERA as a starter in 2020.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom exited his start on Friday against the Padres after only 80 pitches due to right flexor tendinitis, but the Mets expect him to be ready in time for his next one against the Cubs. They will likely monitor his workload due to the injury scare.
away_pitcher_note: Stock will make his Cubs debut on Wednesday. He was 0-3 with a 4.12 ERA in nine games for Triple-A Iowa this season, but the 31-year-old has Major League experience with 52 games for the Padres and Red Sox from 2018-'20.

home_pitcher_note: No Mets pitcher has been more consistent than Stroman, who has delivered between six and seven innings in each of his last seven starts, allowing three or fewer runs in six of them. Stroman owns a 2.49 ERA over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks logged a quality start on Saturday, holding St. Louis to two runs over six innings. The righty struck out two, walked one and gave up three hits. He has been homer prone (19 on the season), but is 6-0 with a 2.93 ERA in his last six outings.

home_pitcher_note: Davies looks to extend his winning streak to three, having thrown 12 2/3 scoreless innings in his past two starts. He is 3-2 with a 5.74 ERA in six career starts against the Marlins, whom he last faced in 2019.
away_pitcher_note: Poteet will be activated from the IL to start the series opener. Prior to sustaining a sprained right MCL, Poteet had provided stability at the back of the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is seeking his first win in five starts, having gone 0-3 with a 7.47 ERA in his past four outings. The Marlins might be the perfect opponent; Arrieta is 8-1 in 12 career starts against Miami.
away_pitcher_note: López has been a consistent arm in the Miami rotation this season, but in his last start against the Braves on June 13 he allowed six hits and four runs through three innings for his shortest start of the season. He looks to regroup in his first matchup of the season against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Mills will make his 15th appearance of the season -- but just his third start -- when he takes the mound for his first career outing against the Marlins. He allowed three runs over 4 1/3 innings on Tuesday against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins will give rookie Trevor Rogers extra rest, so Thompson will start the series finale. He last pitched on June 12, shutting out the Braves over five innings.

away_pitcher_note: With Shane Bieber and Zach Plesac on the IL, Civale is the front man of the Indians' rotation. He will take the mound against the Cubs for the second time in his career. Civale's previous start vs. Chicago saw him allow just two runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks tossed six shutout innings in a road win over the Mets on Thursday. The righty has gone 7-0 with a 2.54 ERA in his last seven turns, striking out 35 and walking seven in 46 innings. He has a 4.60 ERA in eight home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed rookie will make his third career start for the Indians -- his second since his June 15 callup from Triple-A Columbus. In his last start, Morgan fanned five batters and allowed three runs to score over 3 2/3 innings of work.
